ce3b73a766337b1f.description: List domain addresses — Returns the domain-level and site addresses of a domain, the emergency (E911) addresses users and devices are assigned. Personal addresses and endpoints are left out unless you add `show_all_personal=yes`.  Requires Office Manager or Site Manager scope for your own domain, Reseller scope for the domains in your territory, or Super User scope. Site Manager scope is not limited to its own site here: it reaches every address in the domain. Super User Read Only scope can read.  An address is one of three kinds, set by its `user` field: `*` for a domain-level address that every user in the domain can see, a site name for a site address, or an extension for a personal address. To use an address, set its `emergency-address-id` on a device, a user, a site, or the domain. A device without one uses its user\'s address, a user without one uses its site\'s, and a site without one uses the domain\'s. User and device reads report where the address came from in `emergency-address-source`: `user_level`, `site_level`, or `domain_level`.  Each address carries `count-users-configured`, the number of users assigned it, and `address-formatted-pretty`. `address-is-default-for-site` is `true` on a site\'s own address, `domain_default` is `true` on the domain\'s, and `site_address` is `true` on any other address a site owns.  Filter with `address-name` (contains) and `caller-name` (exact). Page with `start` and `limit`. `limit` defaults to `100`, and `0` returns every address. `GET /domains/{domain}/addresses/count` counts the addresses, and returns `404` when the domain does not exist. — [GET /domains/{domain}/addresses]

address-name.description: Returns only the addresses whose name contains this text.

caller-name.description: Returns only the addresses with exactly this caller name.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

limit.description: The most addresses to return. Defaults to `100`. `0` returns every address. Default: 100

show_all_personal.description: `yes` returns every address in the domain: domain-level, site, and personal addresses, and the endpoint rows. By default only domain-level and site addresses are returned. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

ce3b73a766337b1f.title: Get Addresses For Domain

551a2b8ba3d9ca90.description: Create domain address — Creates an emergency (E911) address in a domain. Without `user` in the body it is a domain-level address that every user in the domain can see. Send a site name in `user` to create a site address.  Requires Office Manager or Site Manager scope for your own domain, Reseller scope for the domains in your territory, or Super User scope. Site Manager scope is not limited to its own site here: it reaches every address in the domain.  `address-name` and `address-line-1` are required. `emergency-address-id` is optional: without it the API generates one, `a-` followed by 13 hexadecimal characters. An ID already used in any domain returns `409`. To add an address the carrier has checked, call `POST /domains/{domain}/addresses/validate` first, then send its `emergency-address-id`, `address-formatted-pidflo`, and `carrier` with the other fields. `address-formatted-pidflo` is used only together with a supported `carrier`: `bandwidth`, `brightlink`, `inteliquent`, or `voipinno`. Without one, the address is saved with an empty `address-formatted-pidflo`.  Returns `200` with the address as stored. The address is stored shortly after the response, so a read straight after may not show it yet. Users, devices, and domains already assigned this ID get the new location. Send `address-postal-code` as a string so leading zeros are kept.  To use an address, set its `emergency-address-id` on a device, a user, a site, or the domain. A device without one uses its user\'s address, a user without one uses its site\'s, and a site without one uses the domain\'s. User and device reads report where the address came from in `emergency-address-source`: `user_level`, `site_level`, or `domain_level`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/addresses]

address-country-abbreviation.description: The country code, such as `US` or `CA`.

address-formatted-pidflo.description: The standardized address from `POST /domains/{domain}/addresses/validate`, as an object. Send it back unchanged with `carrier`. Its keys depend on the carrier: `bandwidth` and `inteliquent` use `HouseNumber`, `StreetName`, `StreetSuffix`, `City`, `StateCode`, `Zip`, `PlusFour`, and `Country`; `brightlink` uses `houseNumber`, `streetName`, `streetSuffix`, `city`, `stateCode`, `zip`, `plusfour`, and `country`.

address-line-1.description: The house number and street. The house number is the text up to the first space.

address-location-description.description: Where in the building, such as a room or desk.

address-name.description: A label for the address, shown when users pick one.

address-postal-code.description: The postal code. Send it as a string to keep leading zeros.

address-state-province-abbreviation.description: The state or province code, such as `CA`.

caller-name.description: The caller name stored with the address.

carrier.description: The emergency calling carrier, as returned by validate. `address-formatted-pidflo` is used only with one of these values. Allowed values: "bandwidth", "brightlink", "inteliquent", "voipinno"

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

emergency-address-id.description: The address ID. IDs the API generates are `a-` followed by 13 hexadecimal characters. Paths accept only letters, digits, spaces, and `* . - _ '`. Optional: without it the API generates one. An ID used in any domain returns `409`.

ip-address-public.description: A public IP address stored with the address, as sent. The API does not detect it.

user.description: `POST /domains/{domain}/addresses` only: leave it out for a domain-level address, or send a site name for a site address. On a user path, the path decides.

551a2b8ba3d9ca90.title: Create Address For Domain

47a3802940d22bd6.description: Validate address — Checks an address with the platform\'s emergency calling carrier and returns it in the carrier\'s standard form. It does not save the address. Send the result to `POST /domains/{domain}/addresses` to save it.  Requires Office Manager, Site Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. It counts as a create, so read-only scopes and Basic User scope cannot call it.  The carrier is set for the whole platform, so you cannot choose it. Send `address-line-1`, `address-line-2`, `address-city`, `address-state-province-abbreviation`, `address-postal-code`, and `address-country-abbreviation`. The house number is read from `address-line-1` up to the first space. `address-name` and `caller-name` are returned as sent. Send `emergency-address-id` to check an existing address again. Without it, the response carries a new one, `a-` followed by 13 hexadecimal characters.  A valid address returns `200` with `address-formatted-pidflo`, the standardized address as an object whose keys depend on the carrier, and `carrier`. An address the carrier rejects also returns `200`, with `valid: false` and the carrier\'s `reason`. Fix the address and validate again. A platform with no carrier set up answers `valid: false` with `reason` `Vendor not configured`.  With the `bandwidth` carrier the check takes a few seconds, and it registers the address with the carrier under its `emergency-address-id`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/addresses/validate]

address-country-abbreviation.description: The country code, such as `US` or `CA`.

address-line-1.description: The house number and street. The house number is the text up to the first space.

address-location-description.description: Where in the building, such as a room or desk.

address-postal-code.description: The postal code. Send it as a string to keep leading zeros.

address-state-province-abbreviation.description: The state or province code, such as `CA`.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

emergency-address-id.description: Send it to check an existing address again. Without it, the response carries a new ID.

47a3802940d22bd6.title: Validate Address

545c914393941c3d.description: Update domain address — Changes an emergency (E911) address in a domain, addressed by its `emergency-address-id`.  Requires Office Manager or Site Manager scope for your own domain, Reseller scope for the domains in your territory, or Super User scope. Site Manager scope is not limited to its own site here: it reaches every address in the domain.  An ID that is not in this domain returns `404`, and nothing is changed.  `address-name` is required. Send the other fields you want to change. `address-formatted-pidflo` is used only together with a supported `carrier`: `bandwidth`, `brightlink`, `inteliquent`, or `voipinno`. Without one, the address is saved with an empty `address-formatted-pidflo`. To change the street, validate the new address first and send its `address-formatted-pidflo` and `carrier`.  A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after. Users, devices, sites, and domains assigned this address get the new location. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/addresses/{emergency-address-id}]

address-country-abbreviation.description: The country code, such as `US` or `CA`.

address-formatted-pidflo.description: The standardized address from `POST /domains/{domain}/addresses/validate`, as an object. Send it back unchanged with `carrier`. Its keys depend on the carrier: `bandwidth` and `inteliquent` use `HouseNumber`, `StreetName`, `StreetSuffix`, `City`, `StateCode`, `Zip`, `PlusFour`, and `Country`; `brightlink` uses `houseNumber`, `streetName`, `streetSuffix`, `city`, `stateCode`, `zip`, `plusfour`, and `country`.

address-line-1.description: The house number and street. The house number is the text up to the first space.

address-location-description.description: Where in the building, such as a room or desk.

address-name.description: A label for the address, shown when users pick one.

address-postal-code.description: The postal code. Send it as a string to keep leading zeros.

address-state-province-abbreviation.description: The state or province code, such as `CA`.

caller-name.description: The caller name stored with the address.

carrier.description: The emergency calling carrier, as returned by validate. `address-formatted-pidflo` is used only with one of these values. Allowed values: "bandwidth", "brightlink", "inteliquent", "voipinno"

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

emergency-address-id.description: The address ID (`emergency-address-id`). IDs the API generates are `a-` followed by 13 hexadecimal characters.

ip-address-public.description: A public IP address stored with the address, as sent. The API does not detect it.

545c914393941c3d.title: Update Address For Domain

dfb6f8ba1f7a9eac.description: Delete domain address — Deletes an emergency (E911) address in a domain, addressed by its `emergency-address-id`. It can be a domain-level, site, or personal address.  Requires Office Manager or Site Manager scope for your own domain, Reseller scope for the domains in your territory, or Super User scope. Site Manager scope is not limited to its own site here: it reaches every address in the domain.  An ID that is not in this domain returns `404`. Deleting an address also removes it from the carrier for `bandwidth` and `brightlink`, and clears `emergency-address-id` on every user, device, site, and domain that used it. Those then fall back to the site address, then the domain address.  A `202` means the delete is accepted and applied shortly after. — [DELETE /domains/{domain}/addresses/{emergency-address-id}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

emergency-address-id.description: The address ID (`emergency-address-id`). IDs the API generates are `a-` followed by 13 hexadecimal characters.

dfb6f8ba1f7a9eac.title: Delete Address For Domain

b468bcbd03c0182e.description: Read user address — Returns one of a user\'s emergency (E911) addresses, addressed by its `emergency-address-id`, with `address-formatted-pretty` added.  Basic User scope can call it for its own user, with `~` or its own extension. Office Manager and Site Manager scopes can call it for any user in their domain, Reseller scope for the domains in its territory, and Super User scope for any domain. Super User Read Only scope can read.  The address must belong to the user in the path. Any other ID returns `404`. To read a domain-level or site address, use `GET /domains/{domain}/addresses/{emergency-address-id}`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/addresses/{emergency-address-id}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

emergency-address-id.description: The address ID (`emergency-address-id`). IDs the API generates are `a-` followed by 13 hexadecimal characters.

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

b468bcbd03c0182e.title: Get Address Using Address ID

0a205ce68c4ce38a.description: Update user address — Changes one of a user\'s emergency (E911) addresses, addressed by its `emergency-address-id`.  Basic User scope can call it for its own user, with `~` or its own extension. Office Manager and Site Manager scopes can call it for any user in their domain, Reseller scope for the domains in its territory, and Super User scope for any domain. A feature you leave out keeps its settings. For `phone-numbers-to-allow` and `phone-numbers-to-reject`, numbers you send are added; send `remove: yes` to drop them. `new-position` moves the rule to the top or bottom of the order. To set the full order, use `PUT /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/answerrules/reorder`. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/answerrules/{timeframe}]

enabled.description: Whether the rule is used at all. A disabled rule is skipped when calls are matched. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

new-position.description: Moves the rule to the top (checked first) or the bottom (checked last) of the user's rules. Allowed values: "top", "bottom"

phone-numbers-to-allow.description: An answer rule list of caller numbers.

phone-numbers-to-reject.description: An answer rule list of caller numbers.

prompt-no-answer.description: An answer rule feature that sends calls to a destination.

simultaneous-ring.description: The simultaneous ring feature of an answer rule.

1bca6cdf5fde68b3.description: List auto attendants in domain — Lists a domain\'s auto attendants: each one\'s name, user, starting tier, time frames, and the path that reads it in full.  Requires Office Manager, Site Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Site Manager sees only attendants of users in their site, whatever `site` it sends.  An attendant answering several time frames is one row, with each time frame in `timeframes`. Returns 100 rows unless you send `limit`. The response is an array, empty when there are none. To see an attendant\'s menu, use its `read-path` with **Read auto attendant**. **List auto attendants with list access** returns the same rows to Basic User scope and higher, and **Count auto attendants in domain** counts them. — [GET /domains/{domain}/autoattendants]

filter_users.description: Comma-separated extensions to leave out, such as `8000,8001`. `no` or `false` leaves nothing out.

1bca6cdf5fde68b3.title: Get Domains Domain Autoattendants

ded69c262739100d.description: Create auto attendant — Creates an auto attendant: a menu that answers calls to `user` and sends each key press to a destination.  Requires Office Manager, Site Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope.  When `user` does not exist, it is created as an attendant user with its own dial plan. When it exists, the menu is added to its dial plan, and its answering rule for `time-frame` is changed to send calls to the menu. The menu always starts at tier `Prompt_100`, and submenus and greetings take the next free numbers. A tier\'s `audio` is read aloud by text to speech and saved as its greeting. It can be sent inside the tier or beside it, the way **Read auto attendant** returns it.  The response is `202`: the attendant is accepted and applied shortly after. Send `synchronous=yes` to wait for it: the response is `200` with the new attendant, or `202` if it is not applied within about five seconds.  A user whose answering rule for the time frame already sends calls to an auto attendant returns `409`. To change the menu, use **Update auto attendant**. — [POST /domains/{domain}/autoattendants]

attendant-name.description: Name of the auto attendant, shown in lists. Without it the attendant has an empty name until **Update auto attendant** sets one.

audio.description: A greeting to make by text to speech.

auto-attendant.description: One tier of an auto attendant menu, as sent to create or update it. Only the fields you send are changed.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

synchronous.description: `yes` waits up to about five seconds for the attendant to be applied and answers `200` with it, or `202` if it is not applied by then. `no`, the default, answers `202` as soon as the request is accepted. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

time-frame.description: Time frame whose calls go to the attendant. The user's answering rule for it is set to send calls to the menu. Leave it out, or send `Default` or `*`, for the user's default answering rule. Default: "Default"

user.description: Extension that answers as the auto attendant, such as `8000`. An extension that does not exist is created as an attendant user with its own dial plan. An existing user keeps its dial plan, and the menu is added to it. It becomes `{user}` in the attendant's path.

ded69c262739100d.title: Post Domains Domain Autoattendants

3b436bec44691315.description: Read auto attendant — Returns one auto attendant: its name, starting tier, greetings, and what every key does, with submenus in full.  Requires Office Manager, Site Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Site Manager can read only attendants of users in their site.  Each greeting has a `file-access-url` that plays it without a token until it expires. A tier with no greeting has an empty `audio` array. A submenu\'s greeting sits beside its `auto-attendant`, and an attendant with intro greetings lists them in `intro-greetings`, one per time frame.  A `{prompt}` that is not one of the user\'s attendants returns `404`. To find an attendant\'s `{prompt}`, use **List auto attendants in domain**. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/autoattendants/{prompt}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

prompt.description: Tier of the menu, such as `Prompt_100`. Use the attendant's `starting-prompt` from **List auto attendants in domain**. An attendant made with **Create auto attendant** always starts at `Prompt_100`.

user.description: Extension that answers as the auto attendant, such as `8000`. It is the `user` in the attendant's `read-path`. `~` means your own user.

3b436bec44691315.title: Get Domains Domain Users User Autoattendants Prompt

98059d8bb068f844.description: Update auto attendant — Changes one tier of an auto attendant\'s menu, and renames the attendant. It must be `Prompt_<n>` and already exist, or the response is `404`. `attendant-name` renames the attendant and is accepted on the starting tier only. The time frame is not changed by an update. A `PUT` or `DELETE` on `/domains/{domain}/autoattendants`, without the user and tier in the path, returns `405`.  The response is `202`: the change is accepted and applied shortly after. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/autoattendants/{prompt}]

audio.description: A greeting to make by text to speech.

prompt.description: Tier to change, `Prompt_<n>`, such as `Prompt_100`. Use the attendant's `starting-prompt` from **List auto attendants in domain**, or a submenu's tier. Any other value, or a tier the user does not have, returns `404`.

user.description: Extension that answers as the auto attendant, such as `8000`. It is the `user` in the attendant's `read-path`. `~` means your own user.

805773fa6770c72e.description: Back up domain — Runs a manual backup of one domain now, on the server that answers the request. The domain\'s databases are backed up and its stored files copied to backup storage, and the response reports both.  Requires Reseller or Super User scope. A Reseller can back up only a domain in its own territory. This path accepts only `POST`; any other method returns `405`.  A request body is optional. A `domain` in the body must name the domain in the path, or the request returns `400`. To name the domain in the body instead, use `POST /backup`.  The call waits for the backup to finish, which can take up to 5 minutes for a large domain. `backup-index` identifies the new restore point. To see it, use `GET /domains/{domain}/restore`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/backup]

domain.description: Domain to back up, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. On `POST /backup`, backs up only this domain instead of every domain on the server, with the same access as `POST /domains/{domain}/backup`. On `POST /domains/{domain}/backup`, it must name the domain in the path, or the request returns `400`.

805773fa6770c72e.title: Post Domains Domain Backup

615b0bf2a81688e0.description: Start full system backup — Starts the backup job now for every domain on the server that answers the request. The job runs in the background, and the call returns as soon as it starts.  Requires Super User scope. Super User Read Only and every other scope get `403`. This path accepts only `POST`; any other method returns `405`.  To back up one domain instead, send its name in `domain`. The request then works like **Back up domain**: it needs the same access, waits for the backup to finish, and returns the same response. A Reseller can name only a domain in its own territory; any other returns `403`. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.  Only one backup runs at a time: if one is already in progress, the request returns `409`, so retry after it finishes. When backup storage is not configured on the server, the request returns `502` with the message `missing configs`. Contact support to set it up. — [POST /backup]

domain.description: Domain to back up, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. On `POST /backup`, backs up only this domain instead of every domain on the server, with the same access as `POST /domains/{domain}/backup`. On `POST /domains/{domain}/backup`, it must name the domain in the path, or the request returns `400`.

615b0bf2a81688e0.title: Post Backup

2742a40557cfda2b.description: List restore points — Lists the backups you can restore a domain from, grouped by the server that holds them, newest first. Name the domain in the query string.  Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope.  Send every filter as a query parameter; this request takes no body. `domain` is required, and without it the request returns `400`. Each restore point carries a `confirmation-value`. To restore one, send it with the point\'s server hostname, `type`, and `day` (as `index`) to `PUT /restore`.  A domain with no restore points returns an empty array. When the backup service is unavailable or slow, the request returns `502` or `504` instead. To name the domain in the path instead, use `GET /domains/{domain}/restore`. — [GET /restore]

domain.description: Domain whose restore points to list, such as `example.com`. Without it, the request returns `400`.

hostname.description: Server whose backups to list, as returned in the restore-point list. Omit it to list every server that holds a backup of the domain.

index.description: Restore point to list, matched against its `day`. Nightly backups use `0` (Sunday) to `6`. Manual backups use the `backup-index` the backup returned.

show-file-details.description: Set to `yes` to include `files`, the stored files behind each restore point. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

type.description: Kind of backup to list. Omit it to list both. Allowed values: "nightly", "manual"

2742a40557cfda2b.title: Get Restore

a5b30946205128da.description: Restore domain from backup — Restores a domain from one of its backups. This overwrites the domain\'s current data: the backup\'s database files are imported, the domain\'s stored files are restored, and the domain is reloaded.  Requires Reseller or Super User scope.  List the restore points with `GET /restore` first. Send the chosen point\'s server as `hostname`, its `type`, its `day` as `index`, and its `confirmation-value`, together with `domain`, in the body. A `domain` in the query string is ignored, so a body without one returns `400`. A missing field returns `400` naming it. Values that do not identify exactly one current restore point also return `400`.  The call waits for the restore to finish, which can take up to 5 minutes. With `geo` set to `yes`, the restore is queued instead, and the response carries only `logs`. — [PUT /restore]

confirmation-value.description: The restore point's `confirmation-value`, from the restore-point list. It proves you picked the point that exists now.

domain.description: Domain to restore, such as `example.com`. Send it in the body: a `domain` in the query string is ignored.

geo.description: `yes` or `no`. Defaults to `no`. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

hostname.description: Server that holds the backup, as keyed in the restore-point list.

index.description: Restore point to restore, from its `day`. Nightly backups use `0` to `6`. Manual backups use the `backup-index` the backup returned.

type.description: Kind of backup, from the restore point's `type`. Allowed values: "nightly", "manual"

a5b30946205128da.title: Put Restore

6ea9507351b9e631.description: List domain restore points — Lists the backups you can restore the domain in the path from, grouped by the server that holds them, newest first. When the backup service is unavailable or slow, the request returns `502` or `504` instead. — [GET /domains/{domain}/restore]

show-file-details.description: Set to `yes` to include `files`, the stored files behind each restore point. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

6ea9507351b9e631.title: List Domain Restore Points

0cd567cadb3790ec.description: Read domain blocked numbers — Returns the domain\'s blocked-number list. Calls to the domain from a number on the list are rejected. The list belongs to the default answering rule (time frame `*`), so the response has at most one entry. Numbers are returned as strings, so a leading zero is kept. 860c041b6d93c527.description: Add domain blocked numbers — Adds numbers to the domain\'s blocked-number list, kept on the domain\'s system user `domain`.  Requires Office Manager scope for your own domain, or Reseller or Super User scope.  Send the numbers in `phone-numbers-to-reject.parameters`. Each one is added to the list, or updated if it is already there. Numbers you leave out stay on the list. A single number in place of the list is taken as a one-item list.  To pause or resume the whole list, send `phone-numbers-to-reject` with `enabled` set to `no` or `yes` and an empty `parameters` list. Every number already on the list takes that setting.  The list always belongs to the default answering rule. A `time-frame` in the request is ignored. A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after. `PUT` on the same path behaves the same way. — [POST /domains/{domain}/number-filters]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

860c041b6d93c527.title: Post Domains Domain Number Filters

The list always belongs to the default answering rule. A `time-frame` in the request is ignored. domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

74de9f12a878fc57.description: Log agent in — Logs an agent in to one call queue, or to every queue they are on with `all`: the agent\'s availability becomes `automatic` and calls are dispatched to them. The agent log records `Auto`, shown as Online.  Call Center Agent, Basic User, Advanced User, and Simple User act only on their own agent entries: use `~` as the agent. Site Manager acts on agents who are users at its own site; on a named queue, the queue must be at its site too. Call Center Supervisor, Office Manager, Route Manager, Reseller, and Super User act on any agent in the domain. Office Manager Read-Only and Super User Read Only get `403`.  `202` means the change was published over the service bus (SBUS), not yet applied. Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, or Super User. Send `synchronous=yes` to wait up to 2 seconds and get the created queue back with `200`. A queue that already exists returns `409`. A `phone-number` that is not in the domain\'s number inventory, or belongs to another domain, returns `422` before anything is created. A value too long for its field returns `400`. 2e1882c51754f13a.description: Read call queue statistics — Returns call center statistics for one call queue over a time window: call volume, answers, abandons, service level, and talk, hold, and wait times. Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Site Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Reseller reads the domains in its territory.  Calls count when they entered the queue inside the window, from `datetime-start` up to but not including `datetime-end`. There is no limit on the window length, but long windows are slow. `fields` picks the statistics; it defaults to `VOL,CH,ATT,AC,AAS,SL`. Units follow each field\'s name except `calls-after-call-work-avg-duration-seconds`, which is in minutes without `interval`. `unit` changes the units.  Without `interval` the response is one object. With `interval`, the response is a map from bucket to rows. Bucket keys are RFC 3339 for `minute`, `hour`, and `day` (`2026-09-01T14:00:00+00:00`), `YYYY-Www` for `week` (`2026-W36`), and `YYYY-MM` for `month` (`2026-09`). Buckets are in UTC unless `datetime-start` names a bracketed time zone.  A queue that does not exist, or that has statistics turned off, answers `404`. For every queue at once, use `GET /domains/{domain}/statistics/callqueues/per-queue`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/statistics/callqueues/{callqueue}]

callqueue.description: The call queue's extension, for example `2000`.

datetime-end.description: The end of the time window, RFC 3339 with an offset, for example `2026-09-02T00:00:00-07:00`. It must be later than `datetime-start`. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (read as UTC) and `YYYY-MM-DD` (end of that day, UTC) are also accepted.

datetime-start.description: The start of the time window, RFC 3339 with an offset, for example `2026-09-01T00:00:00-07:00`. The window includes this moment. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (read as UTC) and `YYYY-MM-DD` (start of that day, UTC) are also accepted. To group `interval` buckets by local time, add the IANA time zone in brackets after the offset, for example `2026-09-01T00:00:00-07:00[America/Phoenix]`. The offset must match the zone.

dnis.description: Counts only calls to this dialed number, for example `15555550100`.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

fields.description: The statistics to return, as a comma-separated list of codes: `VOL`, `CH`, `CO`, `ACO`, `AC`, `AAC`, `AR`, `AAR`, `SL`, `DT`, `VM`, `FWD`, `AST`, `CB`, `ATT`, `TT`, `AHT`, `AH`, `AWT`, `ACW`, `SMS_VOL`, and `SMS_AHT`. Each field's description names its code. Defaults to `VOL,CH,ATT,AC,AAS,SL`. An unknown code is skipped. v2 field names are not accepted here.

interval.description: Splits the window into buckets of this size and returns the statistics per bucket. The response then becomes a map of bucket to rows (see the response). Buckets with no calls are filled with `0`, except `minute` buckets over a window longer than 24 hours. Leave it out for one total over the whole window. Allowed values: "minute", "hour", "day", "week", "month"

op_term_sub.description: Counts only calls handled by this agent extension, for example `1001`.

range_interval.description: Shifts both ends of the window by a relative amount, for example `-5 hour`. Kept for older integrations: give the offset in `datetime-start` and `datetime-end` instead.

remove_zeros.description: `true` leaves out every row whose statistics are all `0`. Any other value keeps them. Allowed values: "true", "false". Default: "false"

remove_zeros_interval.description: With `interval`, `true` leaves out every bucket whose statistics are all `0`. Allowed values: "true", "false". Default: "false"

sla.description: The service-level threshold in seconds for `SL`: a call answered within this wait counts as meeting the service level. Defaults to `60`. Default: 60

unit.description: `seconds` returns the `-minutes` fields (`ATT`, `TT`, `AHT`, and `ACW` without `interval`) in seconds. `minutes` returns the `-seconds` fields (`AH`, `AWT`, and `ACW` with `interval`) in minutes. Every duration on this endpoint is in **seconds**, including the fields whose names end in `-minutes`. `unit=minutes` turns `AH` and `AWT` into minutes.  With `interval`, the response is a map from bucket to rows. 921fe7d6c020153d.description: List agent status times — Returns how many minutes agents spent in each call center status: available, unavailable, lunch, break, and your custom statuses. Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Site Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Reseller reads the domains in its territory. A Site Manager sees only agents in its own site, whatever `agent_list`, `group_list` or `site_list` names.  A status period counts toward the window for the part of it that falls inside the window, so an hour inside a lunch reads as 60 minutes of lunch. A status the agent is still in counts up to now. A status\'s minutes are never more than the window length.  Without `interval`, the response is a map from agent extension to minutes per status over the whole window.  With `interval=15m` or `interval=hour`, the window is split into buckets aligned in UTC, and each bucket gives the minutes summed over all the selected agents, which `agents` lists. The minutes of a bucket divided by its length in minutes is the average number of agents in that status. A bucket that has not ended yet is left out, and at most 2000 buckets can be returned. `MC` adds each bucket\'s missed calls. For one agent\'s individual status changes, use `GET /domains/{domain}/statistics/agent/{agent}/timeline`.  Filter the agents with `site_list`, `group_list`, or `agent_list`. `fields` picks the statuses. It defaults to `AM,UM,L,B`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/statistics/agentLog]

agent_list.description: A comma-separated list of agent extensions, `1001` or `1001@example.com`. Returns only these agents.

fields.description: The statuses to return, as a comma-separated list of codes: `LI` (logged in), `AM` (available), `UM` (unavailable), `L` (lunch), `B` (break), `M` (meeting), `O` (other), `W` (web), and `CUST1` to `CUST8` (your custom statuses). Not case-sensitive. Defaults to `AM,UM,L,B`. With `interval`, `MC` is also accepted: the agents' missed calls per bucket, as `calls-unanswered-count`. With `interval`, any other code returns `400`.

a177e579f99c5c47.description: Read an agent\'s status timeline — Returns each status period of one agent that overlaps the window, clipped to it, oldest first, and the seconds spent in each status. All times in the response are UTC.  The last period runs to `datetime-end`. While the window has not ended yet, it runs to now instead and is marked `open`, with `end-datetime: null`.  A window may cover at most 31 days. Status history is kept indefinitely, so any past window can be read.  **Who can read it.** Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Reseller and Super User read any agent in the domain. A Site Manager reads only agents in its own site; any other agent is `403`. Basic User, Simple User, Advanced User and Call Center Agent read only their own timeline, in their own domain; any other agent or domain is `403`.  Where compliance access logging is on for the domain, each read of another person\'s timeline is recorded in the access log as a read of that agent\'s activity record. — [GET /domains/{domain}/statistics/agent/{agent}/timeline]

agent.description: The agent's extension (user) in the domain. Letters, digits, `-` and `_` only; give the bare extension, not `user@domain`. A user that does not exist in the domain is `404`.

datetime-end.description: The end of the window, RFC 3339 with an offset. Must be later than `datetime-start` and at most 31 days after it. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (read as UTC) and `YYYY-MM-DD` (end of that day, UTC) are also accepted. An end time on second `:59` is read as the start of the next second, so `2026-10-17 23:59:59` closes the window at midnight.

datetime-start.description: The start of the window, RFC 3339 with an offset, for example `2026-10-17T00:00:00-07:00`. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (read as UTC) and `YYYY-MM-DD` (start of that day, UTC) are also accepted.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

deb1f37ccb728fab.description: Read 15-minute, hourly or daily call queue history — One point per bucket over the range, oldest first. Each point gives every covered queue\'s statistics for that bucket and a domain-wide `*`. A queue absent from a point has no history for that bucket.  The queues covered are the ones the caller may see in the other call center statistics, narrowed by `queue_list`. A Site Manager sees only the queues of its own site. Agent-level scopes (Basic User, Call Center Agent and the like) may read only their own agent statistics and get `403` here.  Available when the platform has call center reports enabled; `404` otherwise. — [GET /domains/{domain}/statistics/callqueues/history]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

period.description: Bucket size, not case-sensitive. Omitted or blank is `hour`. `15m` gives quarter hours aligned to :00, :15, :30 and :45 UTC, and reaches back only as far as the server keeps its raw queue samples (about two days by default; `oldest-available` says where it starts). Allowed values: "hour", "day", "15m". Default: "hour"

range.description: How far back to go; the allowed values depend on `period`. For `hour`: `24h` (default), `7d` or `14d`. For `day`: `30d` (default), `7d` or `90d`. For `15m`: `24h` (default) or `48h`. Omitted or blank is the period's default. Allowed values: "24h", "48h", "7d", "14d", "30d", "90d"

ae21bdd3cd17c292.description: Read per-minute call queue gauges for the last hour or two — One point per minute, from `range` ago up to the current (partial) minute, oldest first. Each point gives every covered queue\'s values for that minute (the highest it reached during the minute) and a domain-wide `*`.  The queues covered are the ones the caller may see in the other call center statistics, narrowed by `queue_list`. A Site Manager sees only the queues of its own site. Agent-level scopes (Basic User, Call Center Agent and the like) may read only their own agent statistics and get `403` here.  Each core server keeps its own samples, so the read asks every core and, per queue, takes the larger of the cores\' values. A core that does not answer is left out and named in the `X-NS-Fanout-Missing` response header; the values then cover the other cores only, and the response is still `200`.  Available when the platform has call center reports enabled; `404` otherwise. — [GET /domains/{domain}/statistics/callqueues/live-history]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

queue_list.description: Comma-separated queue extensions. Narrows the queues covered; a queue the caller may not see is left out, not refused.

range.description: How far back to go. Omitted or blank is `1h`. Allowed values: "1h", "2h". Default: "1h"

0ee4bf488b8617c6.description: Get call trace — Builds the trace of a call from the SIP servers\' event logs and returns it in the rendering you pick with `type`. Name the call by its SIP call IDs and a time window. To trace a call by its CDR instead, use `GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/sipflow`.  Super User and Super User Read Only see every trace. A Reseller sees calls that have a party domain (originating, terminating, or `by`) in its territory. Office Manager and the other domain-tier scopes see calls that have their own domain as a party domain. User-tier scopes see only calls where their own user is the originating or terminating party. A call outside your scope answers the same `404` as a call that does not exist. A scope without the call-trace privilege gets `403`; by default Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only hold it. Every call ID you send must match a CDR in your scope inside the window; call IDs that do not are ignored, and if none remain the answer is `404`.  **Share links.** Send `k` instead of `start_time`, `end_time`, and `callids` to open a stored trace made with `POST /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/sipflow/store`. A share link needs no token, is read-only, and stops working when the share expires or is revoked. A share stored on another server of the cluster is opened by adding `location`.  **What is included.** The trace follows transfers, forks, and conference bridges from your call IDs and adds those calls; `sql` lists every call ID it covered. The window is widened to cover the whole of every call found. A trace holds both parties\' numbers, every hop\'s address, and the raw SIP messages, so treat it as call metadata. In `cradle_to_grave`, steps outside your scope are removed: by territory for a Reseller, and by domain for the other scopes below Super User.  **Renderings.** The documented response is JSON. `call_trace`, `cradle_to_grave`, and `csv` answer inside an `event` envelope, and `call_trace_details` answers the bare object. The other renderings answer a file of their own media type:  - `type=csv&download=yes`: a CSV file (`text/csv`, `trace.csv`) - `type=call_trace&download=yes`: the SVG diagram (`image/svg+xml`, `sipflow.svg`) - `type=call_trace_html`: an HTML viewer page (`text/html`); add `download=yes` for `sip_flow.html` - `type=call_trace_text`: plain text (`text/plain`); add `download=yes` for `sipflow.txt` In `call_trace_text`, each block header shows its time as `YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS` in UTC, and `csv` rows show the same form, with the millisecond Unix time in `UnixTsm`.  A long call can take a minute or more to build.  **Example requests**  - Ladder diagram: `GET /sipflow?start_time=2026-09-01T14:30:00+00:00&end_time=2026-09-01T14:34:10+00:00&callids=0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0@192.0.2.10&type=call_trace` - Trace details: `GET /sipflow?start_time=2026-09-01T14:30:00+00:00&end_time=2026-09-01T14:34:10+00:00&callids=0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0@192.0.2.10&type=call_trace_details` - Cradle to grave: `GET /sipflow?start_time=2026-09-01T14:30:00+00:00&end_time=2026-09-01T14:34:10+00:00&callids=0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0@192.0.2.10&type=cradle_to_grave` - CSV file: `GET /sipflow?start_time=2026-09-01T14:30:00+00:00&end_time=2026-09-01T14:34:10+00:00&callids=0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0@192.0.2.10&type=csv&download=yes` - Share link: `GET /sipflow?k=202609019f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015&type=call_trace_html` — [GET /sipflow]

callids.description: Comma-separated SIP call IDs of the call: the `Call-ID` header value, as the CDR shows it in `call-orig-call-id` or `call-term-call-id`. Each must match a CDR in your scope inside the window; the rest are ignored. Related calls are added automatically. Required unless `k` is sent.

download.description: `yes` to receive the rendering as a file attachment instead of inline. Applies to `call_trace` (`sipflow.svg`), `call_trace_html` (`sip_flow.html`), `call_trace_text` (`sipflow.txt`), and `csv` (`trace.csv`). Without it, `call_trace` and `csv` answer JSON. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

ds.description: Event sources to read, comma-separated: `diag` for the SIP servers, `ncs` for the conferencing servers. Defaults to `diag`. A conference bridge found on the way adds its conferencing server. Allowed values: "diag", "ncs", "diag,ncs". Default: "diag"

end_time.description: End of the window to search. Same forms as `start_time`. Required unless `k` is sent.

k.description: Share key from `POST ../sipflow/store`. Opens that stored trace with no token, read-only; `start_time`, `end_time`, `callids`, and the search options are then ignored.

location.description: Base64 of the `store-location` hostname the share answer gave. Send it with `k` when the share was stored on another server of the cluster. A hostname that is not a known server of this cluster answers `404`.

margin.description: Seconds added before `start_time` and after `end_time` when reading events. A whole number. Defaults to `10`. Default: 10

search_callids.description: `no` to trace only the call IDs you sent, without following related calls. `false` and `0` also turn it off. Defaults to `yes`. Allowed values: "yes", "no", "true", "false", "1", "0". Default: "yes"

servers.description: Comma-separated hostnames of cluster servers to read events from, used with `search_callids=no` to skip the related-call search. Leave it out otherwise: the servers come from the call's CDRs.

show_attendees.description: `yes` to follow a conference bridge and include every attendee's legs. Defaults to the platform setting, `no` unless changed. An ad hoc monitor bridge is always followed. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

start_time.description: Start of the window to search, RFC 3339 with an offset. A legacy `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` value is also accepted. Required unless `k` is sent. An unparsable value returns `400`.

type.description: Rendering to return. Defaults to `call_trace`. - `call_trace`: the ladder diagram as a base64 SVG in `svg` - `call_trace_details`: devices and messages as JSON - `call_trace_html`: a self-contained HTML viewer (`text/html`) - `call_trace_text`: the raw SIP messages and log lines (`text/plain`) - `cradle_to_grave`: the call-progress summary in `cradle` - `csv`: the event rows, encoded in `csv`, or a `text/csv` file with `download=yes`. Allowed values: "call_trace", "call_trace_details", "call_trace_html", "call_trace_text", "cradle_to_grave", "csv". Default: "call_trace"

Calls are returned oldest first, 100 at a time by default. Page with `start` and `limit`, and narrow the list with `type`, `user`, or `site`. Calls routed between servers of the platform itself are left out. To count calls without reading them, use **Count active calls in domain**. — [GET /domains/{domain}/calls]

Any other value returns `400`. 418dc12c715494e7.description: Create call — Starts a call on behalf of the user in the path. The body takes one of two shapes, selected by `dial-rule-application`:  **Dial a number** (omit `dial-rule-application`, or send `call`). The platform rings the first party in `call-orig-user`, by default the user in the path, and dials `call-term-user` once it answers. Send `synchronous=yes` to wait up to 10 seconds for the call to appear: the response is then `200` with the call. Otherwise, or if the call has not appeared by then, the response is `202`.  **Record an audio file** (`dial-rule-application` is `record`). The platform rings `call-term-user` so its user can record the greeting, music on hold file, or message named by `call-record-type` and `call-record-index`. The response is always `202`.  Requires Basic User scope for your own user, Office Manager scope for a user in your own domain, or Reseller or Super User scope.  Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent tokens can start the first leg only from their own user or one of their own devices. An outside number or a SIP address outside the domain is allowed as the first leg.  Keep the `call-id` you send: it is the `{callid}` that reads, transfers, holds, and ends the call. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/calls]

To turn away a call that is still ringing without ending other legs, use **Reject call**.  The user in the path must be a party on the call, on any leg; otherwise the request returns `404`. The call is looked up for about a second before `404` is returned, so a control sent right after the call starts still finds it. Each bucket holds the most calls in progress at once during it. The bucket size follows `range` unless you set `period`. Only `GET` is accepted. — [GET /domains/{domain}/calls/active-history]

33eaf5e134d53b92.description: List CDRs — Returns call detail records (CDRs) across domains, newest first. Requires Super User, Super User Read Only, or Reseller scope. A Reseller sees only its own territory\'s domains. A Super User sees every domain unless you narrow the request with `domain` or `reseller`. Office Manager and Basic User scopes use `GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs` and `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/cdrs`.  Set the window with `datetime-start` and `datetime-end`, matched on `call-start-datetime`. 53a336307934e2c8.description: Read configuration — Returns the value of one setting in the context you describe with the key parts. Configurations are the named settings the portal and the API look up at run time, such as `PORTAL_SHOW_SHARED_CONTACTS`. Each row sets one value for one combination of key parts: `reseller`, `domain`, `user`, `user-scope`, `admin-ui-account-type`, and `core-server`. A key part of `*` matches everything, so the row with every key part `*` is the system value.  Name every key part that applies, such as `reseller`, `domain`, and `user`. For each one you send, rows with that value or with `*` match, and the most specific row is returned. Each key part you leave out matches only `*`, so with none you get the system value. `include_wildcards=false` matches only the exact values you sent.  Every scope reads its own tiers and the system rows, never another tenant\'s:  - Super User and Super User Read Only read every row. - Reseller reads its territory\'s rows, rows of domains in its territory, and system rows. - Office Manager reads its own domain\'s rows and system rows. - Other scopes read the rows for their own domain, user, and scope, and system rows. Sending a `user-scope` other than your own returns `403`.  Values of secret-named settings are masked, as `/nmsconfig` masks them: a name containing a secret keyword (`password`, `key`, `token`, `secret`, and others), less the names in the `NsConfigurationMaskExempt` setting, has its value masked unless the value is shorter than `NsConfigurationMaskMinLength` (default `4`) or a plain switch (`yes`, `no`, `true`, `false`, `on`, `off`, `enabled`, `disabled`). A Super User can send `include-secrets=yes` to get them in clear; any other scope that sends it gets `403`.  The response is an array with at most one row. A setting with no matching row returns an empty array: its definition\'s `default` then applies (`GET /config-definitions/{config-name}`). — [GET /configurations/{config-name}]

admin-ui-account-type.description: Login type to resolve for, such as `Domain` or `Subscriber`. Left out, only `*` matches.

config-name.description: Name of the setting, such as `PORTAL_SHOW_SHARED_CONTACTS`. On a read, `*` matches any run of characters.

core-server.description: Core server to resolve for, such as `core1.example.com`. Left out, only `*` matches.

domain.description: Domain to resolve for, such as `example.com`. Rows for this domain and rows with `*` match. Left out, only `*` matches.

include-secrets.description: `yes` returns secret-named values in clear. Super User only; any other scope that sends `yes` gets `403`. Defaults to `no`. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

include_wildcards.description: `false` matches only the exact key-part values you sent, without falling back to `*`. Defaults to `true`. Default: true

reseller.description: Territory to resolve for, such as `example-reseller`. Rows for this territory and rows with `*` match. Left out, only `*` matches.

9efd7f9abc3f80f3.description: Delete configuration — Deletes one configuration row. The name comes from the path; name the rest of the key in the body, as the list returns it. Who can delete:  - Super User deletes any row, including system rows, for any name. - Reseller deletes rows for its own territory or a domain in it. With neither `reseller` nor `domain`, the row is stored for your territory. - Office Manager and Route Manager delete their own domain\'s rows. `domain` left out means your domain. - Other scopes with delete rights delete only their own user\'s rows in their own domain. `user` and `domain` left out mean yours. - Super User Read Only, Route Manager Reseller, Call Center Supervisor, Site Manager, and Office Manager Read-Only are read-only and get `403`. A key that matches no row returns `404`. `DELETE /configurations` without a name answers `405`. The delete is published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied on every server shortly after, so `202` means accepted. Send `domain`, `reseller`, and `user` in the body: in the query string they\'re ignored. — [DELETE /configurations/{config-name}]

85de2d4d510a058c.description: List configurations — Lists configuration rows. Configurations are the named settings the portal and the API look up at run time, such as `PORTAL_SHOW_SHARED_CONTACTS`. Each row sets one value for one combination of key parts: `reseller`, `domain`, `user`, `user-scope`, `admin-ui-account-type`, and `core-server`. A key part of `*` matches everything, so the row with every key part `*` is the system value.  Every scope reads its own tiers and the system rows, never another tenant\'s:  - Super User and Super User Read Only read every row. - Reseller reads its territory\'s rows, rows of domains in its territory, and system rows. - Office Manager reads its own domain\'s rows and system rows. - Other scopes read the rows for their own domain, user, and scope, and system rows. Sending a `user-scope` other than your own returns `403`.  Values of secret-named settings are masked, as `/nmsconfig` masks them: a name containing a secret keyword (`password`, `key`, `token`, `secret`, and others), less the names in the `NsConfigurationMaskExempt` setting, has its value masked unless the value is shorter than `NsConfigurationMaskMinLength` (default `4`) or a plain switch (`yes`, `no`, `true`, `false`, `on`, `off`, `enabled`, `disabled`). A Super User can send `include-secrets=yes` to get them in clear; any other scope that sends it gets `403`.  How the filters work:  - `config-name` takes one name, a pattern with `*`, or a comma-separated list. It defaults to `*`. - Each key part you send matches that value. Each key part you leave out matches only `*`, so with no filters the list holds the system rows. - For one exact `config-name`, rows with `*` in a key part you sent match too, and the most specific row comes first. That row is the value that applies in that context. `include_wildcards` turns this on or off. - The result has one row per config name.  Rows are paged with `start` and `limit`, which defaults to `100`. No match returns an empty array. `GET /configurations/count` counts differently: a key part it is not sent matches every value. To see what each setting means, call `GET /config-definitions`. — [GET /configurations]

admin-ui-account-type.description: Returns rows for this login type, such as `Domain` or `Subscriber`. Left out, only rows whose `admin-ui-account-type` is `*` match.

config-name.description: Name to return, such as `PORTAL_SHOW_SHARED_CONTACTS`. `*` matches any run of characters (`PORTAL_CONTACTS_*`), and a comma-separated list returns each name. Defaults to `*`. Default: "*"

core-server.description: Returns rows for this core server, such as `core1.example.com`. Left out, only rows whose `core-server` is `*` match.

domain.description: Returns rows for this domain, such as `example.com`. Left out, only rows whose `domain` is `*` match.

filter.description: Returns rows where the name, value, `reseller`, `domain`, `user-scope`, `user`, or `admin-ui-account-type` contains this text. With a `*` or list `config-name`, replaces the name filter.

include-secrets.description: `yes` returns secret-named values in clear. Super User only; any other scope that sends `yes` gets `403`. Defaults to `no`. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

include_wildcards.description: `true` also matches rows with `*` in each key part you sent. Defaults to `true` for one exact `config-name` and `false` for a pattern or list.

limit.description: Most rows to return. Defaults to `100`. Default: 100

reseller.description: Returns rows for this territory, such as `example-reseller`. Left out, only rows whose `reseller` is `*` match.

sort.description: Sort order: comma-separated column names, each optionally followed by `asc` or `desc`. Columns: `config_name`, `config_value`, `description`, `reseller`, `domain`, `user`, `role`, `login_type`, and `hostname`. Anything else returns `400`. With no `sort`, the most specific rows come first.

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

user.description: Returns rows for this user (extension), such as `1001`. Left out, only rows whose `user` is `*` match.

user-scope.description: Returns rows for this user scope, such as `Office Manager`. Scopes below Office Manager may send only their own. Left out, only rows whose `user-scope` is `*` match.

cfb80134e76582f7.description: Create connection — Creates a connection in the domain that the body\'s `domain` names. Requires Office Manager, Route Manager, or Call Center Supervisor scope in that domain, Reseller scope in its territory, or Super User scope. The API publishes the connection on the service bus (SBUS) `connection_events` channel, and each server writes it when the event arrives, so `202` means published, not applied.  `connection-orig-match-pattern` and `domain` are required. `connection-orig-match-pattern` is the connection\'s key and must be unique across the platform, not only the domain: a value any connection already uses returns `409`. `connection-term-match-pattern` defaults to it, and `connection-translation-request-host` and `connection-translation-destination-host` default to `connection-address`, as the API formats it for the connectivity type. `connection-source-ip-checking-enabled` and `connection-include-server-header-enabled` default to `no`. `connection-connectivity-type` defaults to `header_ip_match` and sets `connection-sip-authenticate-as-client-enabled`: `yes` for `outbound_registration`, `no` for every other type. A value you send that contradicts the type is overridden, and the response carries a `Warning` header and a `warnings` list. `connection-sip-registration-password` defaults to a random 8-character value.  Create route profiles with `POST /domains/{domain}/routeprofiles`. Sending `call-routing` here returns `404`.  Send `synchronous=yes`, in the body or the query string, to wait up to 2 seconds for the connection to be written. You then get `200` with the connection. If it is not written in time, you get the usual `202`.  If a connection with the same `connection-orig-match-pattern` was deleted in the last 15 minutes, and the platform is set to block re-created connections, some servers can refuse the new one after the `202`. Read it back, and repeat the create if it is missing.  `POST /domains/{domain}/connections` does the same with the domain in the path. — [POST /connections]

e79a352222009cb5.description: List user contacts — Lists the contacts a user sees: their personal contacts, the domain\'s shared contacts, and, on request, the users in the domain directory.  Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, and Call Center Supervisor can read their own contacts only. Site Manager can read its own contacts and those of users at its own site. Office Manager can read the contacts of any user in its domain, Reseller those of users in domains of its territory, and Super User any user\'s. Super User Read Only and Office Manager Read-Only can read too, platform-wide and in their own domain. A request for any other address book returns `403`.  The list is built in this order:  - the user\'s personal contacts - the domain\'s shared contacts, marked `is-shared: true`, unless `PORTAL_SHOW_SHARED_CONTACTS` is `no` for the domain or its reseller - with `includeDomain=yes`, one on-net row per user in the domain directory, carrying `user`, `department`, `site`, and presence  A personal contact whose first and last name match a directory user is merged into that user\'s row instead of listed twice. Rows are then sorted (directory users by extension first, then by last name and first name, unless you send `sort`) and paged with `start` and `limit`, which defaults to `100` and is clamped to 1 to 1,000.  For your own contacts, call `GET /domains/~/users/~/contacts`. `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/contacts/count` counts the same rows with the same filters. `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/contacts/list` returns a reduced row for pickers. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/contacts]

department.description: With `includeDomain=yes`, adds only directory users in this department. `*` means every department. Personal and shared contacts are not filtered by it.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

includeDomain.description: `yes` or `1` adds the users listed in the domain directory as on-net rows; any other value leaves them out. A personal contact with the same first and last name as a directory user is merged into that user's row. Has no effect in a residential domain. Allowed values: "yes", "1", "no". Default: "no"

limit.description: Most rows to return, from 1 to 1,000, counted after personal, shared, and directory rows are merged. A value outside that range is clamped to it. Defaults to `100`. Default: 100

name-first-name.description: Returns only contacts with exactly this first name. Applies to personal, shared, and directory rows.

name-last-name.description: Returns only contacts with exactly this last name. Applies to personal, shared, and directory rows.

site.description: With `includeDomain=yes`, adds only directory users at this site. Personal and shared contacts are not filtered by it.

sort.description: Sort keys, comma-separated, each a field optionally followed by `asc` or `desc` (any case; `asc` when left out). Fields: `name-first-name`, `name-last-name`, `name-middle-name`, `company`, `email`, `user`, `department`, `site`, `phonenumber-work`, `phonenumber-cell`, `phonenumber-home`, `phonenumber-fax`, `created-datetime`, `unique-id`. 8fa3275190088af7.description: Create user device — Creates a SIP device for the user and, when you send a MAC address and model, links it to a phone on the Endpoints server.  Requires Basic User for your own devices, or Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User for the users you administer. A Basic User or other user-level scope can create devices only for itself, and a Site Manager only for users in its site; anyone else gets `403`.  Only `device` is required. Settings you leave out come from the domain\'s and territory\'s device defaults, and a flag you send wins over the default. f3f51064da21a211.description: Create domain — Creates a domain in a reseller\'s territory. Requires Reseller scope for that territory, or Super User scope. Send `reseller` as `~` to use your own territory.  With the domain, the API creates its dial plan, named by `dial-plan` or after the domain, with a default dial rule. It also creates the domain user `domain@<domain>`, which holds the defaults new users inherit: time zone, dial plan, dial permission, caller ID, area code, language, and voicemail settings. Fields you leave out take your reseller\'s or the platform\'s default values.  A `202` means the domain is accepted and created shortly after. Send `synchronous=yes` to wait instead: the answer is `200` with the new domain, or `202` if it is not ready within about 10 seconds.  A domain name that already exists returns `409`. Setting `recording-configuration` requires Reseller scope or above. — [POST /domains]

account-id.description: Your own account reference for the domain, up to 64 characters.

account_recovery_user_primary_email.description: `1` lets users recover their account from the login page with a verified email. `0` means an Office Manager or above must reset the password. Allowed values: 0, 1

active-calls-against-license-count.description: Calls in progress that count against the platform license. Excludes legs on other geographic servers and guest video sessions.

active-calls-offnet-current.description: Calls in progress to or from off-net destinations.

active-calls-total-current.description: Calls in progress in the domain, including calls across geographic servers and guest video sessions.

allow_sso_with_additional_emails.description: `1` lets one user log in with SSO from more than one email address. Allowed values: 0, 1

allow_user_primary_email_edit.description: `1` lets Office Manager and lower scopes edit primary email addresses. Which addresses a user can change still depends on scope. Allowed values: 0, 1

area-code.description: The area code added to a 7-digit number dialed by users in the domain.

caller-id-name.description: The caller ID name used on outbound calls when no user or site caller ID applies.

caller-id-number.description: The caller ID number used on outbound calls when no user or site caller ID applies.

caller-id-number-emergency.description: The caller ID number used on emergency calls when no user or site emergency caller ID applies.

count-users-configured.description: Number of users in the domain, not counting departments and the system users that features create. In a list, it is counted only when `limit` is 100 or less.

description.description: A display name for the domain, up to 127 characters. Defaults to the domain name.

dial-plan.description: The dial plan new users in the domain get. On create, a dial plan with this name is created; it defaults to the domain name. On update, it changes the plan for users created afterward.

dial-policy.description: The dial permission new users in the domain get. Name an existing dial permission.

domain.description: The domain name. Letters, digits, and `. - _`, up to 63 characters. It cannot be changed after the domain is created.

domain-type.description: The feature set of the domain: - `Standard` is for a business, with a company directory and configurable PBX features - `Residential` has no company directory and no PBX features, like an analog line - `Hospitality` is for hotels, with limited voicemail and no company directory. Errors forward to the operator Any other value is stored as `Standard`. Allowed values: "Standard", "Residential", "Hospitality". Default: "Standard"

email-send-smtp-hostname.description: SMTP server for the domain's email. Empty uses the reseller or platform server.

email-send-smtp-password.description: SMTP password. Empty uses the reseller or platform server. Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User scopes get it masked, such as `co*****************ry`. Other scopes do not get the field. A Super User can send `include-secrets=yes` to get it in full. On update, sending the masked value back keeps the stored password, and any other masked value returns `400`.

email-send-smtp-port.description: SMTP port, 1 to 65535, sent as a string. Empty uses the reseller or platform server.

email-send-smtp-username.description: SMTP user name. Empty uses the reseller or platform server.

emergency-address-id.description: The emergency address used for users that have no user or site address. Use the `address-id` of an address in the domain.

include-secrets.description: `yes` returns `email-send-smtp-password` in full in the `synchronous=yes` answer instead of masked. Super User scope only: any other scope gets `403` before the domain is created. Every request is logged. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

7c869d80b8950592.description: Delete domain — Deletes a domain and everything in it: users and their devices, dial plans and dial rules, call queues, conferences, connections, recording settings, time frames, emergency addresses and numbers, and settings. Requires Reseller scope for the domain\'s territory, or Super User scope. A delete cannot be undone.  Phone numbers, SMS numbers, and device (MAC) records assigned to the domain are deleted too, unless you send `phone_numbers_option`, `sms_numbers_option`, or `mac_option` set to `unassign`. An unassigned phone number goes back to the pool of available numbers, an unassigned SMS number becomes available, and an unassigned MAC is cleared and kept.  The request can take a while on a large domain. A `202` means the delete is accepted and applied shortly after. — [DELETE /domains/{domain}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

mac_option.description: `unassign` keeps the domain's device (MAC) records, cleared of their lines and credentials. Omit it to delete them. Allowed values: "unassign"

phone_numbers_option.description: `unassign` keeps the domain's phone numbers and returns them to the pool of available numbers. Omit it to delete them. Allowed values: "unassign"

sms_numbers_option.description: `unassign` keeps the domain's SMS numbers and marks them available. Omit it to delete them. Allowed values: "unassign"

e0a221a81b32eff5.description: Read domain billing summary — Returns usage counters for one domain next to its main limits: users, departments, call queues, agents, call parks, auto attendants, conferences, phone numbers, and devices, plus peak simultaneous calls and SMS volumes for this month and last month. Any token that can read the domain can read its summary. Use `~` for the domain of your token.  The counters are calculated on each request, so the call can be slow on a large domain. Counters by user scope, service code, and transcription vendor are present only for the ones in use. When video conferencing is licensed, `allow-video-conference` and video usage counters are added. — [GET /domains/{domain}/billing]

aec309e8d4cee5a9.description: Send email to user — Sends a templated email to a user, at the address stored on their account. `template` picks the email:  - **Call center report.** A call center statistics report for a time window, `call_center_* (PHP)`. - **Account email.** Welcome, password reset, or forgotten login name. - **Custom template.** A `custom_*` template uploaded for the domain. - **Lost authenticator.** A recovery link for a user who lost their authenticator app. - **Email verification.** A verification link for one of the user\'s addresses.  A Basic User can send to themselves. Office Manager can send to users in their domain, Reseller to users in their territory, and Super User to anyone. Below Office Manager, every `cclist` address must also be one of the user\'s own addresses, or the answer is `403`.  The response is `200` when the request was understood, with `sent` saying whether the email went out: `sent: false` means it could not be built, for example because the user has no email address. A body that matches no email is a `400`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/email]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

user.description: The user's extension. The email goes to the address on this user's account. Use `~` for the user of your token.

aec309e8d4cee5a9.title: Send Email

0cfe66af9731d615.description: Check email address verification — Says whether one of a user\'s email addresses is verified. No token is needed. Name the address by its hash: the first 8 hexadecimal characters of the SHA-256 of the address, trimmed and in lowercase. An unknown user or address answers `verified: false`, not an error. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/email/checkVerified/{email-hash}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

email-hash.description: The first 8 characters of the SHA-256 of the lowercase address, in lowercase hex.

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.
