53e40d2bb25b6623.description: List event subscriptions — Returns the event subscriptions your token can see. Each one sends events of one `model` to its `post-url`.  Requires Basic User, Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only. Super User and Super User Read Only see every subscription. A Reseller sees the subscriptions in its own territory, except the ones a Super User created, and can narrow to one of its domains. Every other scope sees the subscriptions its own scope created in its own domain, and user-level scopes see only their own and domain-wide ones. Naming a domain you cannot see returns `403`.  `post-url` comes back in full only when you can change the subscription. Otherwise its user-info, query string, and fragment are masked.  Filter with `domain`, `user`, and, for a Super User or Super User Read Only, `reseller` and `user-scope`. Page with `start` and `limit`, 100 subscriptions by default. There is no sort and no `/count`. `GET /subscriptions/list` returns fewer fields per subscription. — [GET /subscriptions]

domain.description: Only subscriptions for this domain. A domain you cannot see returns `403`.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page. Default: 100

reseller.description: Only subscriptions whose territory is this one. Super User and Super User Read Only only. A Reseller always gets its own territory.

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

user.description: Only subscriptions for this user. `*` means no filter.

user-scope.description: Only subscriptions created with this scope. Super User and Super User Read Only only.

53e40d2bb25b6623.title: Read Subscriptions

b6902b54f01fd429.description: Create event subscription — Creates a subscription that sends events of one `model` to your `post-url` as they happen. Create one subscription per model.  Requires Basic User, Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User, and read access to the model you name. Without it you get `403`. An unknown `model` returns `400`.  What you can subscribe to depends on your scope:  - Super User: any domain, or `*` for every domain on the platform - Reseller: one domain in its own territory, for one user or `*` for all - Office Manager: its own domain, for one user or `*` for all - Site Manager: users of its own site in its own domain, never `*` - Basic User: its own extension  A platform-wide subscription (`domain` `*`) from any other scope returns `403`, and a domain that does not exist returns `404`. The territory is taken from the domain.  Choose `model` from these values:  | `model` | Sends | |---|---| | `call` | Active call updates | | `call_origid` | Active call updates, only the latest state of each call per batch | | `cdr` | Completed call records | | `agent` | Call center agent status changes, matched on the call queue | | `voicemail` | New voicemail | | `message`, `messagesession` | Chat and SMS messages and sessions |  Also available: `presence`, `subscriber`, `auditlog`, `auditlog_lite` (creates and deletes of main objects only), `domain`, and `device`. `presense` is a misspelt presence model that is still accepted.  Events are matched on `domain` and `user` only. `*` matches every value.  `post-url` must be an `http://` or `https://` URL with a host, at most 256 characters, with the scheme only once and no `user:password@` part. Unless you are a Super User, every address the host resolves to must be public: loopback, link-local, private, shared (CGNAT), and unique-local addresses are refused, and so are this platform\'s own servers. A host that does not resolve is refused too. Each refusal is a `400` that names the rule. An installation can allow private addresses with the `NsSubscriptionAllowPrivateUrls` setting. Use `https://` with a certificate that validates, because a certificate error counts as a failed delivery.  `subscription-expires-datetime` takes RFC 3339, such as `2027-09-01T14:30:00+00:00`, or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC. It is stored in UTC and read back as RFC 3339. Any other value returns `400`.  The `id` is derived from the model, scope, territory, domain, user, `post-url`, and `subscription-geo-support`, so creating the same subscription twice returns `409`. The call waits up to 5 seconds for the new subscription to be stored and then returns it with `200`. Delivery starts within about 5 seconds after that.  Delivery: every 500 milliseconds, the server that owns the subscription sends one `POST` to `post-url` with a JSON array of every event queued since the last send. The request carries `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and `X-Correlation-ID` set to the subscription `id`, and no credentials or signature. The events are the platform\'s own records, with their internal field names, not the v2 names. A response above `302`, a connection failure, or no answer within 15 seconds counts as an error. A failed batch is not retried and its events are lost, so reconcile gaps with the matching read endpoint. Redirects are not followed, and a `301` or `302` counts as delivered. Repeated failures never disable a subscription: it keeps sending until it expires or you delete it. Retries and a signing secret are tracked in NN-663.  Watch `status` and `error-count` to see whether delivery works. Delivery stops at `subscription-expires-datetime`, and the subscription is deleted about 8 hours later. To keep it, send a later `subscription-expires-datetime` with `PUT /subscriptions/{id}` before then. — [POST /subscriptions]

domain.description: Domain whose events are sent. Defaults to your own domain. `*` means every domain and needs Super User (`403` otherwise). A domain that does not exist returns `404`. Ignored on `/domains/{domain}/subscriptions`, which takes the path domain.

model.description: Kind of event the subscription sends. One model per subscription: `call`, `call_origid` (latest state of each call only), `cdr`, `agent` (matched on the call queue), `voicemail`, `message`, `messagesession`, `presence`, `presense` (a misspelt presence model, still accepted), `subscriber`, `auditlog`, `auditlog_lite` (creates and deletes of main objects only), `domain`, or `device`. Your scope needs read access to the model. Any other value returns `400`. Allowed values: "agent", "auditlog", "auditlog_lite", "call", "call_origid", "cdr", "device", "domain", "message", "messagesession", "presence", "presense", "subscriber", "voicemail"

post-url.description: URL each batch of events is sent to with `POST`. An `http://` or `https://` URL with a host, up to 256 characters, with no `user:password@` part. Unless a Super User sets it, it must resolve only to public addresses outside this platform.

preferred-server.description: Hostname of the core server that should deliver a `subscription-geo-support: yes` subscription. It takes over after it has been up for 60 seconds. Defaults to the server that handled the create. Name a real core server: an unknown hostname can leave the subscription with no server delivering it.

reseller.description: Ignored: the territory comes from the domain. A Super User sending it with `domain` `*` gets `400`.

subscription-expires-datetime.description: When delivery stops, as RFC 3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC. Stored in UTC. Defaults to the expiry of your token, or 20 years for a token that does not expire. Any other value returns `400`.

subscription-geo-support.description: `yes` stores the subscription on every server and has one of them deliver it, with another taking over if that server stops. `no` stores it only on the server that handled the create, which alone delivers it. Defaults to `yes`. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "yes"

user.description: User whose events are sent, or `*` for every user in the domain. `*` needs Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User; a Site Manager must name a user of its own site, and user-level scopes always get their own extension. Default: "*"

ed54991fe8995c21.description: Read event subscription — Returns one event subscription, with its delivery state: `status`, `error-count`, `posts-count`, and `current-active-server`.  Requires Basic User, Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only. Super User and Super User Read Only see every subscription. A Reseller sees the subscriptions in its own territory, except the ones a Super User created, and can narrow to one of its domains. Every other scope sees the subscriptions its own scope created in its own domain, and user-level scopes see only their own and domain-wide ones. Naming a domain you cannot see returns `403`.  `post-url` comes back in full only when you can change the subscription. Otherwise its user-info, query string, and fragment are masked. A subscription you cannot see returns `404`, the same as one that does not exist.  Use it after a create to see whether delivery works. `status` is `error` when a delivery failed in the last 5-second cycle. — [GET /subscriptions/{id}]

3f001410b62fac66.description: Update event subscription — Changes where a subscription sends, what it sends, or how long it lives. Send only the fields to change.  Requires Basic User, Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User.  Who can change or delete a subscription:  - Super User: any subscription - Reseller: one for a domain in its own territory, never a platform-wide one or one a Super User created - Office Manager: any in its own domain - Site Manager: its own, or one for a user of its own site, never a domain-wide one - Every other scope: its own  Anything else returns `403`, and the message names the reason.  You can change `post-url`, `model`, `subscription-expires-datetime`, `subscription-geo-support`, and `preferred-server`. A new `post-url` follows the create rules. A new `model` must be a known model (`400`) that you can read (`403`). Send `error-count` or `posts-count` as `0` to reset it; any other value is ignored. `domain`, `user`, and `reseller` cannot change: a different value returns `400`, so delete the subscription and create a new one. Leaving out `subscription-expires-datetime` keeps the current expiry. `subscription-expires-datetime` takes RFC 3339, such as `2027-09-01T14:30:00+00:00`, or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC. It is stored in UTC and read back as RFC 3339. Any other value returns `400`.  A `202` means the change was saved on this server and published to the others over the service bus (SBUS), including a switch of `subscription-geo-support` from `yes` to `no`. Delivery picks it up within about 5 seconds. — [PUT /subscriptions/{id}]

099c6c2393a743ff.description: Create image — Stores a new image under the name in the path, for a reseller, a domain, a server, or all of them. Send the file as a multipart part, or as base64 in a JSON body.  Requires Super User or Reseller scope. A Reseller can manage images stored for its own reseller or for a domain in it. An image that applies to every reseller and every domain (`reseller` and `domain` both `*`) is platform-wide, and only a Super User can create, change, or delete it. Other scopes get `403`.  An image is stored per reseller, domain, and server, and each defaults to `*`, meaning all. The values are matched exactly: an image stored for every domain is not found when you name one domain. If an image already exists under this name for the same reseller, domain, and server, the request returns `400`; replace it with `PUT /images/{filename}`.  The file must be a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, or ICO image. Both the declared media type and the file\'s contents are checked, and the type detected from the contents is the one stored. SVG and other types return `400`. The request can be at most 64 MB.  Send `reseller` and `domain` in the body; query-string values for them are ignored. The request returns `202`: the image is accepted and stored shortly after. — [POST /images/{filename}]

6d375c126c08b7fa.description: List user greetings — Lists a user\'s voicemail greetings, in index order. The recorded name (`name.wav`) is not listed; read it as index `0`.  Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent can read their own greetings. Office Manager, Site Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, and Super User can read any user\'s greetings in the domain, as can Office Manager Read-Only and Super User Read Only.  Returns up to 100 greetings by default; page with `limit` and `start`. Count them with `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/greetings/count`. `file-access-url` is a signed link that plays the file with no token, for 24 hours by default; see `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/greetings/{index}/play`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/greetings]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page. Default: 100

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

user.description: User (extension) whose voicemail greetings you work with, such as `1001`. `~` means yourself. A user with no record returns `400` `Invalid User` on a read and `404` `User not found` on a write.

9f34260f04341f28.description: Create user greeting — Adds a voicemail greeting for the user, from an uploaded file, a base64 file, or text to speech. It takes the next free index unless you send `index`; an `index` that is already used is overwritten, and `index` `0` replaces the user\'s recorded name.  Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent can change their own greetings. Site Manager can change the greetings of users at its own site. Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, and Super User can change any user\'s. The read-only scopes get `403`.  The file is written on the server that handles the request, before the response, and copied to the other servers over the service bus (SBUS) file journal. The call answers `202` by default. Send `synchronous=yes` to get `200` with the stored file instead. With `synchronous=yes` the call waits up to 2 seconds for the file to appear. Every upload is converted to 8 kHz, 8-bit, mono mu-law WAV. Audio that cannot be converted returns `400` and nothing is stored.  **Upload a file.** Send `multipart/form-data` with the audio in the `file` part (`File` also works). The part\'s `Content-Type` picks the decoder: `audio/mpeg` or `audio/mp3` is decoded as MP3, `audio/ogg`, `audio/webm`, `video/ogg`, `video/webm` and `application/ogg` as Ogg or WebM, and anything else is read as WAV. The request can be up to 64 MB.  **Base64 file.** Send JSON with the audio as base64 in `file-base64`, with no line breaks, and its format in `file-encoding`: `audio/wav` (the default), `audio/mpeg`, `audio/ogg`, or `audio/webm`. Base64 that does not decode, or another encoding, returns `400`.  **Text to speech.** Send JSON with the words to speak in `file-script-text` and no file. The voice defaults to the domain\'s text-to-speech voice (`en-US-Wavenet-C` in `en-US` when none is set); name another with `text-to-speech-voice-id` and `text-to-speech-language`. A voice id that the language does not offer falls back to the language\'s first voice. Text to speech must be enabled for the user (`PORTAL_VOICE_TEXT_TO_SPEECH`), or the call returns `400`; `text-to-speech-language` must be a BCP 47 tag, or `400`; a voice-service failure returns `503`. Usage is billed to the owner in the path: that user, or the domain itself for a domain-owned path. List voices with `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/voices/{language}`.  With a file, `file-script-text` is stored as a description of the audio.  A user that does not exist returns `404`, and a user at its storage limit returns `507`. Change a greeting with `PUT` on `/domains/{domain}/users/{user}/greetings/{index}`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/greetings]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

d124679baa0b4192.description: Update user greeting — Replaces the audio of the greeting at `index` with an uploaded file or a base64 file, or changes only its description. The index does not change.  Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent can change their own greetings. Site Manager can change the greetings of users at its own site. Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, and Super User can change any user\'s. The read-only scopes get `403`.  The file is written on the server that handles the request, before the response, and copied to the other servers over the service bus (SBUS) file journal. The call answers `202` by default. Send `synchronous=yes` to get `200` with the stored file instead. Every upload is converted to 8 kHz, 8-bit, mono mu-law WAV. Audio that cannot be converted returns `400` and nothing is stored.  **Upload a file.** Send `multipart/form-data` with the audio in the `file` part (`File` also works). The part\'s `Content-Type` picks the decoder: `audio/mpeg` or `audio/mp3` is decoded as MP3, `audio/ogg`, `audio/webm`, `video/ogg`, `video/webm` and `application/ogg` as Ogg or WebM, and anything else is read as WAV.  **Base64 file.** Send JSON with the audio as base64 in `file-base64`, with no line breaks, and its format in `file-encoding`: `audio/wav` (the default), `audio/mpeg`, `audio/ogg`, or `audio/webm`. c1ad27ab7a710f60.description: Create domain MoH file — Adds a music on hold (MoH) file to the domain, from an uploaded file, a base64 file, or text to speech. It takes the next free index unless you send `index`; an `index` that is already used is overwritten.  Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Reseller, or Super User. Site Manager can read domain MoH but gets `403` on a change, and so do Basic User and the read-only scopes.  The file is written on the server that handles the request, before the response, and copied to the other servers over the service bus (SBUS) file journal. The call answers `202` by default. Send `synchronous=yes` to get `200` with the stored file instead; the call then waits up to 2 seconds for it to appear. Every upload is converted to 8 kHz, 8-bit, mono mu-law WAV. Audio that cannot be converted returns `400` and nothing is stored.  **Upload a file.** Send `multipart/form-data` with the audio in the `file` part (`File` also works). The part\'s `Content-Type` picks the decoder: `audio/mpeg` or `audio/mp3` is decoded as MP3, `audio/ogg`, `audio/webm`, `video/ogg`, `video/webm` and `application/ogg` as Ogg or WebM, and anything else is read as WAV. The request can be up to 64 MB.  **Base64 file.** Send JSON with the audio as base64 in `file-base64`, with no line breaks, and its format in `file-encoding`: `audio/wav` (the default), `audio/mpeg`, `audio/ogg`, or `audio/webm`. Base64 that does not decode, or another encoding, returns `400`.  **Text to speech.** Send JSON with the words to speak in `file-script-text` and no file. The voice defaults to the domain\'s text-to-speech voice (`en-US-Wavenet-C` in `en-US` when none is set); name another with `text-to-speech-voice-id` and `text-to-speech-language`. A voice id that the language does not offer falls back to the language\'s first voice. Text to speech must be enabled for the user (`PORTAL_VOICE_TEXT_TO_SPEECH`), or the call returns `400`. List voices with `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/voices/{language}`.  With a file, `file-script-text` is stored as a description of the audio.  A user that does not exist returns `404`, and an owner at its storage limit returns `507`. Change a file with `PUT` on /domains/{domain}/moh/{index}, and change the order with `PUT` on /domains/{domain}/moh/reorder. — [POST /domains/{domain}/moh]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

c1ad27ab7a710f60.title: Create MOH Domain Tts

4a79d65df66e363c.description: Update domain MoH file — Replaces the audio of the MoH file at `index` with an uploaded file or a base64 file, or changes only its description. The index does not change.  Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Reseller, or Super User. Site Manager can read domain MoH but gets `403` on a change, and so do Basic User and the read-only scopes.  The file is written on the server that handles the request, before the response, and copied to the other servers over the service bus (SBUS) file journal. The call answers `202` by default. Send `synchronous=yes` to get `200` with the stored file instead. Every upload is converted to 8 kHz, 8-bit, mono mu-law WAV. Audio that cannot be converted returns `400` and nothing is stored.  **Upload a file.** Send `multipart/form-data` with the audio in the `file` part (`File` also works). The part\'s `Content-Type` picks the decoder: `audio/mpeg` or `audio/mp3` is decoded as MP3, `audio/ogg`, `audio/webm`, `video/ogg`, `video/webm` and `application/ogg` as Ogg or WebM, and anything else is read as WAV.  **Base64 file.** Send JSON with the audio as base64 in `file-base64`, with no line breaks, and its format in `file-encoding`: `audio/wav` (the default), `audio/mpeg`, `audio/ogg`, or `audio/webm`. Base64 that does not decode, or another encoding, returns `400`.  With a file, `file-script-text` replaces the description; leave it out to keep the stored one.  **Description only.** Send JSON with `file-script-text` and no file. Only the description changes: the audio stays as it is and nothing is spoken, so text-to-speech fields are ignored. To replace the audio with text to speech, `POST` to the same index on `/domains/{domain}/moh` instead; a `POST` with an index that is in use overwrites it.  An index with no file returns `404`. Add a file with `POST` on `/domains/{domain}/moh`. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/moh/{index}]

20f23321acc005da.description: List text-to-speech voices — Lists the text-to-speech voices the voice service offers for one language. Use a voice\'s `id` as `text-to-speech-voice-id` when you create a greeting, hold message, or music on hold (MoH) file from text.  Needs the `read` right on audio for the user in the path: every user for itself; Office Manager, Site Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, and Super User for any user in the domain; Office Manager Read-Only and Super User Read Only as their parent scope. The voice service answers for the user in the path, and its text-to-speech settings must allow it, or the call returns `403`. The list is kept for a few minutes on each server, per path user, caller scope, and language.  `language` must be a BCP 47 tag of letters and hyphens, such as `en-US`: a tag the router accepts but BCP 47 does not returns `400`, and one with a digit (`es-419`) is not a route and returns `404`. Narrow the list with `text-to-speech-gender`, `text-to-speech-name`, `vendor` (matches `text-to-speech-type`), or `id`. A filter that matches nothing answers an empty array. A voice-service failure returns `503`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/voices/{language}]

id.description: Only the voice with this `id`.

eb8269b180e8134e.description: Synthesize speech with query string — Speaks the text in the `file-script-text` query parameter and returns the audio, without storing it. It works like `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/voices`, for players that can only fetch a URL.  Needs the `create` right on audio for the user in the path: Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent for themselves; Office Manager, Site Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, and Super User for any user in the domain. Office Manager Read-Only and Super User Read Only get `403`. Synthesis also needs text to speech enabled (`PORTAL_VOICE_TEXT_TO_SPEECH`) for the user in the path, or the call returns `400`; the voice service answers for that user, and refuses with `403` when its settings do not allow text to speech.  Returns the audio as `audio/wav` (8 kHz, 8-bit, mono), named `tts_<hash>.wav` in `Content-Disposition`. A request with a `Range` header gets `206` with that byte range unless you send `download`. The same words in the same voice for the same user are rendered once and served from cache afterward. Text to speech not enabled for the path user, or a `text-to-speech-language` that is not a BCP 47 tag, returns `400`; a voice-service failure, including no voice for the language, returns `503`. Long text is better sent with `POST`, since URLs have length limits. There is no usage cap: synthesis is limited only by your scope and the platform\'s general request rate limit, and each new text is a call to the voice service. Usage is billed to the owner in the path: that user, or the domain itself for a domain-owned path. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/voices]

download.description: Any value turns off byte ranges: the whole file is sent with `200`.

nofilename.description: Any value leaves out `Content-Disposition`, so a browser plays the audio in place.

text-to-speech-language.description: Language of the voice, a BCP 47 tag such as `en-US`; anything else returns `400`, including a singleton (such as `x` or `u`) with no subtag after it. Omit it to use the domain's default language.

text-to-speech-voice-id.description: Voice to speak with, by id, name, or gender. Omit it to use the domain's default voice.

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

461cf1db90ceedeb.description: Forward voicemail message — Copies a voicemail message into the `new` folder of another mailbox, and emails that user the new-voicemail notice. Your copy stays where it is. The recipient\'s copy shows who forwarded it in `voicemail-forward-from`: the user, or `user@domain` when the message came from another domain.  Name the recipient in `voicemail-forward-new-destination`: a bare user (extension) such as `1002` means that user in the path\'s domain, and `user@domain`, such as `1002@acme.example.com`, names a mailbox in that domain. The mailbox the message is in cannot be the recipient.  Any user may forward a message from its own mailbox to any mailbox in its own domain. Otherwise your scope must be able to change both mailboxes: Site Manager within its site, Office Manager and Route Manager within their own domain, Reseller and Route Manager Reseller within their territory, and Super User anywhere. So a recipient in another domain needs Reseller (a domain in its territory) or Super User. Anything else returns `403`. Office Manager Read-Only and Super User Read Only never forward.  The copy and its metadata are written on the server that handles the request and copied to the other servers over the service bus (SBUS) file journal. The call answers `202`. Each forward is recorded in the compliance access log as a disclosure of the message to the recipient. Only `PATCH` and `PUT` are accepted.  A missing or malformed recipient, or the message\'s own mailbox, returns `400`. A recipient that does not exist returns `404`, one without voicemail returns `409`, and one without room for the message returns `507`. A message that is not in the folder returns `404`. — [PATCH /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/voicemails/{folder}/{filename}/forward]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

filename.description: The message's `filename` as the list returns it, such as `vm-20260901143000123456-0e4a6c8b2d1f3a5c7e9b0d2f4a6c8e1b.wav`. The `.wav` may be left off: `vm-20260901143000123456-0e4a6c8b2d1f3a5c7e9b0d2f4a6c8e1b` names the same message.

folder.description: Voicemail folder: `new`, `saved`, or `trash`. `save` is the same folder as `saved`. Any other value is not a route and returns `404`. Allowed values: "new", "saved", "save", "trash"

The user must exist and have voicemail on, and must not be the mailbox the message is in. Another domain needs Reseller (a domain in its territory) or Super User.

8ae52180f7ebd39b.description: Create meeting with ID — Creates a meeting with the meeting ID in the path, usually one reserved with `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/getId`.  Requires a token for the user in the path, or Office Manager scope or higher for the domain. The ID must be free: an ID in use, or reserved with `getId` for a different user, returns `409`.  The meeting is owned by the user in the path. Creating it also sets up its audio bridge and invites everyone in `attendees` by email. Omitted settings take their defaults: the start is now, the length is 60 minutes, and the participant limit comes from the domain\'s configuration. The response is the new meeting. When the create has not been applied yet, it holds the fields that were accepted. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}]

attendees.description: People to invite. On a change, the list replaces the stored one: attendees left out are removed, and new ones are invited by email.

description.description: Longer text about the meeting, shown in invitations.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

limits-max-participants.description: Most participants the meeting allows. Omit it on a create to use the domain's configured maximum for the meeting type.

meeting-allow-changes-from-hosts-enabled.description: `1` lets hosts other than the owner change the meeting in the app. The API does not check it: every host can change the meeting through the API. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-audio-allowed-from.description: Who can share audio. Allowed values: "everyone", "host", "presenters"

meeting-chat-enabled.description: `1` turns on chat in the meeting. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-chat-history-enabled.description: `1` keeps the chat history after the meeting. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-dial-in-number-blob.description: Phone numbers audio-only attendees dial to join. Filled from the domain's configuration when a meeting is created without an ID.

meeting-hide-attendee-list-enabled.description: `1` hides the attendee list from attendees who are not hosts or presenters. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-join-require-invite-enabled.description: `1` admits only invited attendees. `0` lets anyone with the meeting ID join while the meeting is not locked. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-join-require-passcode-enabled.description: `1` requires `meeting-passcode` to join. Sending `0` clears the passcode. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-lock-enabled.description: `1` locks the meeting: only attendees already connected can stay or rejoin. Takes effect on a change. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-name.description: Name of the meeting, shown in invitations and in the app. Required on a create.

meeting-passcode.description: Passcode attendees enter to join. Kept only when `meeting-join-require-passcode-enabled` is `1`. A masked value (asterisks, as a read returns it to someone who may not see the passcode) is refused on a create and leaves the passcode unchanged on a change.

meeting-presenter-attendee-id.description: Attendee ID of the attendee presenting now. Empty when nobody is.

meeting-question-answer-enabled.description: `1` turns on questions and answers. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-recording-enabled.description: `1` records the meeting. On a change, turning it on starts recording now unless `meeting-require-host-to-begin-enabled` is sent as `1`, and turning it off stops recording. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-registration-id.description: Registration ID guests use to register for a `presentation` meeting: 8 letters or digits. Generated when omitted or not in that form. Ignored for other meeting types.

meeting-require-host-to-begin-enabled.description: `1` keeps attendees waiting until a host joins. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-room-enabled.description: `1` makes this a permanent room rather than a scheduled meeting. List rooms with `type=room`. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-schedule-duration-minutes.description: Planned length in minutes. Defaults to `60` on a create.

meeting-schedule-recurrence-rule.description: Repeat rule for a recurring meeting, as an RFC 5545 `RRULE` (with any `EXDATE`), such as `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU;UNTIL=20261215T150000Z`. An `UNTIL` without a trailing `Z` is read as UTC. Empty for a one-time meeting.

meeting-schedule-start-datetime.description: When the meeting starts, in RFC 3339 form. Unix seconds are also accepted. Omit it on a create to start the meeting now.

meeting-status.description: Set on a change only. `started` starts recording when recording is on. `ended` ends the current instance and resets the meeting. Allowed values: "started", "ended"

meeting-type.description: `conference` is a meeting where everyone can take part. `presentation` is a webinar: guests register themselves with the meeting's `meeting-registration-id`. Allowed values: "conference", "presentation"

meeting-video-allowed-from.description: Who can share video. Allowed values: "everyone", "host", "presenters"

meeting-video-layout.description: Default video layout for the meeting.

timezone.description: Time zone the meeting was scheduled in, such as `US/Eastern`. Used for the calendar invitation.

user.description: Extension of the user, such as `1001`. `~` means your own user. The new meeting's owner. Use the same user the ID was reserved for.

a2d11f9236d080c9.description: List meetings for user — Returns the upcoming meetings a user owns or is invited to, soonest first.  Requires Basic User scope or higher. Any user can list the meetings of another user in its own domain, and Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User can list them in the domains they manage. `meeting-passcode` is shown only to the meeting\'s owner, its hosts, and Office Manager or higher for its domain. Everyone else gets it masked with asterisks; `include-secret=yes` does not change that.  Each occurrence of a recurring meeting is its own row, with `meeting-instance-schedule-start-datetime` set. Meetings and occurrences whose scheduled end has passed are left out. `type=room` returns the user\'s permanent rooms instead. `limit` defaults to `100`.  For identity fields only, use `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/list`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings]

user.description: Extension of the user, such as `1001`. `~` means your own user. The list holds meetings this user owns or is an attendee of.

8048b462163196c6.description: Create meeting — Schedules a meeting, or creates a permanent room, with a generated meeting ID.  Requires a token for the user in the path, or Office Manager scope or higher for the domain. A Basic User creates meetings only for itself.  The meeting is owned by the user in the path. Creating it also sets up its audio bridge and invites everyone in `attendees` by email. Omitted settings take their defaults: the start is now, the length is 60 minutes, and the participant limit comes from the domain\'s configuration. The response is the new meeting as a one-item array. When the create has not been applied yet, the item holds the fields that were accepted.  To choose the ID yourself, reserve one with `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/getId`, then create the meeting with `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings]

attendees.description: People to invite. On a change, the list replaces the stored one: attendees left out are removed, and new ones are invited by email.

description.description: Longer text about the meeting, shown in invitations.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

limits-max-participants.description: Most participants the meeting allows. Omit it on a create to use the domain's configured maximum for the meeting type.

meeting-allow-changes-from-hosts-enabled.description: `1` lets hosts other than the owner change the meeting in the app. The API does not check it: every host can change the meeting through the API. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-audio-allowed-from.description: Who can share audio. Allowed values: "everyone", "host", "presenters"

meeting-chat-enabled.description: `1` turns on chat in the meeting. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-chat-history-enabled.description: `1` keeps the chat history after the meeting. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-dial-in-number-blob.description: Phone numbers audio-only attendees dial to join. Filled from the domain's configuration when a meeting is created without an ID.

meeting-hide-attendee-list-enabled.description: `1` hides the attendee list from attendees who are not hosts or presenters. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-join-require-invite-enabled.description: `1` admits only invited attendees. `0` lets anyone with the meeting ID join while the meeting is not locked. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-join-require-passcode-enabled.description: `1` requires `meeting-passcode` to join. Sending `0` clears the passcode. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-lock-enabled.description: `1` locks the meeting: only attendees already connected can stay or rejoin. Takes effect on a change. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-name.description: Name of the meeting, shown in invitations and in the app. Required on a create.

meeting-passcode.description: Passcode attendees enter to join. Kept only when `meeting-join-require-passcode-enabled` is `1`. A masked value (asterisks, as a read returns it to someone who may not see the passcode) is refused on a create and leaves the passcode unchanged on a change.

meeting-presenter-attendee-id.description: Attendee ID of the attendee presenting now. Empty when nobody is.

meeting-question-answer-enabled.description: `1` turns on questions and answers. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-recording-enabled.description: `1` records the meeting. On a change, turning it on starts recording now unless `meeting-require-host-to-begin-enabled` is sent as `1`, and turning it off stops recording. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-registration-id.description: Registration ID guests use to register for a `presentation` meeting: 8 letters or digits. Generated when omitted or not in that form. Ignored for other meeting types.

meeting-require-host-to-begin-enabled.description: `1` keeps attendees waiting until a host joins. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-room-enabled.description: `1` makes this a permanent room rather than a scheduled meeting. List rooms with `type=room`. Allowed values: 0, 1

meeting-schedule-duration-minutes.description: Planned length in minutes. Defaults to `60` on a create.

meeting-schedule-recurrence-rule.description: Repeat rule for a recurring meeting, as an RFC 5545 `RRULE` (with any `EXDATE`), such as `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU;UNTIL=20261215T150000Z`. An `UNTIL` without a trailing `Z` is read as UTC. Empty for a one-time meeting.

meeting-schedule-start-datetime.description: When the meeting starts, in RFC 3339 form. Unix seconds are also accepted. Omit it on a create to start the meeting now.

meeting-status.description: Set on a change only. `started` starts recording when recording is on. `ended` ends the current instance and resets the meeting. Allowed values: "started", "ended"

meeting-type.description: `conference` is a meeting where everyone can take part. `presentation` is a webinar: guests register themselves with the meeting's `meeting-registration-id`. Allowed values: "conference", "presentation"

meeting-video-allowed-from.description: Who can share video. Allowed values: "everyone", "host", "presenters"

meeting-video-layout.description: Default video layout for the meeting.

timezone.description: Time zone the meeting was scheduled in, such as `US/Eastern`. Used for the calendar invitation.

user.description: Extension of the user, such as `1001`. `~` means your own user. The new meeting's owner.

694d17b0ad5cf9b2.description: Register for meeting — Registers a guest for a `presentation` meeting with the registration ID from the meeting\'s registration link, and emails the guest the meeting details.  Needs no token: the registration ID is the credential. Each client address can register 10 times a minute per registration ID; more returns `429`.  A guest whose email address is already on the meeting is not added twice. The details are emailed at most once a minute per address. The response is the meeting with only the registrant in `attendees`. `meeting-passcode` is always masked here. `PUT` on this path does the same. — [POST /meetings/register/{registration_id}]

email.description: Email address the meeting details are sent to. A guest already on the meeting with this address is not added again.

name.description: Name of the guest registering, 1 to 128 characters.

registration_id.description: Registration ID from the meeting's registration link: 8 letters or digits, such as `k4Rt9xQ2`. It is the meeting's `meeting-registration-id`.

694d17b0ad5cf9b2.title: Post Meetings Register Meeting Registration ID

6b068d5bbbd8567f.description: Update meeting — Changes a meeting\'s settings, schedule, or attendees. Send only the fields to change.  Only the meeting\'s owner, its hosts, Office Manager for the meeting\'s domain, Reseller for its territory, and Super User can change it. Anyone else gets `403`. A host who is not the owner puts its own user in the path.  Some fields act at once: `meeting-lock-enabled` locks or unlocks the meeting for the attendees connected now, `meeting-recording-enabled` starts or stops recording, `meeting-status` `ended` ends the current instance, and `attendees` replaces the attendee list and emails the new attendees. Each change raises `meeting-ordinal-sequence` so calendar invitations update in place. Sending back the masked `meeting-passcode` a read returned leaves the passcode unchanged. A change never moves the meeting to another owner or domain.  `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}]

ba7b70822a2addb6.description: Delete meeting — Cancels a meeting, cancels one occurrence of it, removes it for good, or removes some of its attendees. The `type` field in the body chooses which.  Only the meeting\'s owner, its hosts, Office Manager for the meeting\'s domain, Reseller for its territory, and Super User can change it. Anyone else gets `403`. A host who is not the owner puts its own user in the path.  - `meeting` marks the meeting cancelled, removes its audio bridge, and emails a cancellation to the attendees. It returns `412` while anyone is connected. - `instance` cancels one occurrence of a recurring meeting, named by `meeting-instance-schedule-start-datetime`. - `record` removes the meeting, its attendees, and its audio bridge. - `attendee` removes the attendees listed in `attendeeids`.  `202` means the delete is accepted and applied shortly after. — [DELETE /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}]

attendeeids.description: Required with `type` `attendee`. Attendee IDs to remove, 6 letters or digits each. A comma-separated string is also accepted.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

meeting-instance-schedule-start-datetime.description: Required with `type` `instance`. Scheduled start of the occurrence to cancel, in Unix seconds.

type.description: What to delete: `meeting` cancels the meeting, `instance` cancels one occurrence of a recurring meeting, `record` removes the meeting and its attendees for good, and `attendee` removes the attendees in `attendeeids`. Allowed values: "meeting", "instance", "record", "attendee"

user.description: Extension of the user, such as `1001`. `~` means your own user. The owner, or your own user when you are a host.

ba7b70822a2addb6.title: Delete Domains Domain Users User Meetings Meeting

8ade252de6840484.description: Reserve meeting ID — Reserves an unused meeting ID for the user in the path, for a client that needs the ID before it creates the meeting, such as to put the join link in a calendar entry.  Requires a token for the user in the path, or Office Manager scope or higher for the domain.  The ID is held for that user for a limited time; create the meeting with `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}` and the same user in the path. The response also suggests a registration ID and lists the domain\'s dial-in numbers. Send no body. `GET` on this path is not this operation: it returns the user\'s meetings. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/getId]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

user.description: Extension of the user, such as `1001`. `~` means your own user. The ID is reserved for this user.

8ade252de6840484.title: Post Domains Domain Users User Meetings Get ID

b7cd9dfdbd320677.description: List meetings for user (identity only) — Returns a reduced view of a user\'s upcoming meetings, enough to pick one: its ID, name, owner, and start. Dial-in numbers, sharing, and recording options are on `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings`.  `/list` is authorized by the `list` privilege rather than `read`, and shares it with `/count`, so a scope that may not read full meetings can still list them. Rows are the same meetings and occurrences the full list returns, but `limit` defaults to `10` here. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/list]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

limit.description: Most items to return. Defaults to `10`. Default: 100

offset.description: Items to skip before the first one returned, for paging.

type.description: `room` returns the user's permanent rooms. `meeting` returns scheduled meetings only. Omit it for both. Allowed values: "room", "meeting"

user.description: Extension of the user, such as `1001`. `~` means your own user. The list holds meetings this user owns or is an attendee of.

b7cd9dfdbd320677.title: List User Meetings

123d65760626be20.description: Log meeting event — Adds an event to the log of one instance of a meeting, recorded as written by the user in the path with `file-source` `apiv2`.  Only the meeting\'s hosts and attendees, its owner, and Office Manager or higher for its domain can use its event log. An attendee puts its own user in the path.  Only `event`, `target`, and `details` are taken from the body. `202` means the event is accepted and applied shortly after. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}/instance/{instance}/log]

details.description: Extra detail, stored with the event. An object is stored as a JSON string.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

event.description: What happened, such as `part_join` or `meeting_locked`. Not checked against a list.

instance.description: Instance ID of one occurrence of the meeting: 13 characters, such as `66e6f0a1b2c3d`. Each time a meeting starts it gets a new instance ID, returned as `meeting-instance-id`.

target.description: Who or what the event is about, such as the user who joined.

user.description: Extension of the user, such as `1001`. `~` means your own user. Recorded as the event's `source_id`.

123d65760626be20.title: Post Domain User Meeting Instance Log

09084cb59afe48d6.description: Start ad hoc video conference — Creates a video conference hosted by the user, starting now or at `start`, and invites the participants you list. The conference is titled `Conference`, lasts 30 minutes, and uses the user\'s time zone.  Requires a token for this user. Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User can change the video host of any user in a domain they manage.  The domain must have a video account that is not suspended. Otherwise the request returns `400` with `Not Able to make request`. The user must have a video host. A participant is an email address or an extension in the same domain. An extension with no video host stops the whole request with `404`. When the video service rejects a value you sent, the request returns `400` with the service\'s message. When the video service fails or does not answer, it returns `502` or `504`. `PUT` and `DELETE` on this path return `405`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/video/conference]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

participants.description: Who to invite. Each entry is an email address, or an extension in the host's domain that has a video host. An extension is invited through its video host, and an email address by email. No participant is a moderator.

secure.description: Sent to the video service as its `secure_url` setting.

start.description: When the conference starts, sent to the video service as it is. Defaults to now.

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

09084cb59afe48d6.title: Post Domains Domain Users User Video Conference

1917d5fd13748a4d.description: List message sessions — Returns a user\'s message sessions: their chat, SMS, and MMS conversations, the most recently active first. Each row carries the last message, so this is the conversation list. Every scope reaches its own user. Office Manager reaches every user in its domain, Reseller the domains in its territory, and Super User every domain.  A session the user deleted or left is not returned. `limit` defaults to `100`. For the total, call `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions/count` with the same filters. For the messages in one session, call `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions/{messagesession}/messages`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page. Default: 100

messagesession-id.description: Returns only the session with this ID.

messagesession-last-sender.description: Returns only the sessions whose last message came from this user ID or number. `remote` returns the sessions whose last message did not come from the user.

messagesession-last-status.description: Returns only `read` or only `unread` sessions. Allowed values: "read", "unread"

messagesession-muted.description: Returns only muted (`yes`) or only unmuted (`no`) sessions. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

messagesession-queue-status.description: Returns only the call queue conversations in this state, such as `queued` or `active`.

messagesession-queue-termination.description: Returns only the call queue conversations of this queue, as its user ID.

messagesession-remote.description: Returns only the sessions with this remote party: a user ID such as `1002@example.com`, or a phone number. A 10-digit number gets a leading `1`. Exact match.

855c9682db40c290.description: Send message — Sends a chat, SMS, or MMS message in an existing session. Every scope reaches its own user. Office Manager reaches every user in its domain, Reseller the domains in its territory, and Super User every domain. You send as the user in the path.  Leave `type` out, or send `chat`, in an SMS or MMS session, and the message goes out as that session\'s type, to its number, from the number used last. To start a conversation without a session ID, use `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messages`.  `type` is one of these values:  - `chat`: a text message to users in the same domain. The default. - `chat-media`: a chat message with a file attached. - `sms`: a text message to phone numbers, sent from one of your SMS numbers. - `mms`: an SMS with a file attached. - `chat-video-invite`, `chat-video-decline`: video call invitations sent in a chat.  The API itself writes `chat-name-change`, `chat-participant-add`, `chat-participant-remove`, `chat-participant-remove-notification`, and `chat-participant-leave` messages when a session changes. Do not send them.  ### Chat  Send `message` and `destination`, the extension of a user in the same domain. `type` can be left out.  ### Group chat  Send `destination` as a list of extensions, or as one comma-separated string.  ### Media chat  Set `type` to `chat-media` and attach the file as base64 in `data`, with `mime-type` and `size`. Or send `upload_id` for a file you already uploaded. `message` is still required.  ### SMS  Set `type` to `sms`, `destination` to the phone number, and `from-number` to your SMS number. `from-number` must be assigned in this domain to the sending user, or to a call queue.  ### Group SMS  Send `destination` as a list of numbers. The message goes out as a group MMS.  ### MMS  Set `type` to `mms`, add `from-number`, and attach the file as for a media chat.  A number that texted STOP to `from-number` does not get the message. When every recipient has opted out, the request answers `409`. For the opt-out list, see `GET /domains/{domain}/smsblocks`.  Below Office Manager, your token\'s user must be a participant of the session: posting into anyone else\'s session answers `403`. A session ID that no session has yet is allowed, and starts that session. A video meeting chat is the exception: your token\'s user must attend the meeting, even to post its first message, and only a host or presenter can post into the meeting\'s hosts chat.  A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made right away can still show the old values. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions/{messagesession}/messages]

a229b26d5dc2777c.description: Update message session — Changes a message session: renames a group session, sets a group chat\'s participants, or marks your copy read or muted. Every scope reaches its own user. Office Manager reaches every user in its domain, Reseller the domains in its territory, and Super User every domain. Send one shape per request.  ### Rename the session  Send `session-name`. Every participant\'s copy is renamed, and every participant gets a `chat-name-change` message.  ### Set the participants  Send `messagesession-participants` with the complete list of user IDs, including your own, for example `1001@example.com,1002@example.com,1003@example.com`. A user added gets the session, and a user left out loses it. The other participants get a `chat-participant-add` or `chat-participant-remove` message, and a removed user gets a `chat-participant-remove-notification`. Use it on a group chat only.  Below Office Manager, only a participant can rename a session or change its participants: your token\'s user must hold a copy of it, or the answer is `403`. Marking read or muted touches only the path user\'s copy and needs no such check. To leave a group yourself, use `PUT /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions/{messagesession}/leave`.  ### Mark read or mute  Send `messagesession-last-status` `read` after the user has seen the last message, or `messagesession-muted` `yes` or `no`. Only your own copy changes.  A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made right away can still show the old values. When you only mark read or muted, a session ID the user does not have changes nothing and still answers `202`. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions/{messagesession}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

messagesession.description: The message session ID, as returned in `messagesession-id`. A chat, SMS, or MMS session ID is 32 lowercase hex characters. Any other ID is refused with `400` unless it is a video meeting chat ID.

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

Office Manager reaches every user in its domain, Reseller the domains in its territory, and Super User every domain.  Only this user\'s copy changes: the other participants keep the session and every message. The session disappears from the user\'s list, and its earlier messages are no longer returned to this user. A new message in the conversation brings the session back, starting from that message.  A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made right away can still show the old values. A session ID the user does not have answers `202` too. — [DELETE /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions/{messagesession}]

Office Manager reaches every user in its domain, Reseller the domains in its territory, and Super User every domain.  The user\'s copy of the session is hidden, the other participants\' lists drop the user, and they get a `chat-participant-leave` message naming the user. The session must be a group chat: a one-to-one session answers `400`. To hide a one-to-one session, use `DELETE /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions/{messagesession}`. `POST` does the same as `PUT`.  Below Office Manager, your token\'s user must be a participant of the session, or the answer is `403`, and the remaining participants are always worked out from the session.  A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made right away can still show the old values. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions/{messagesession}/leave]

Each participant has their own copy of a session, so a conversation between two users appears twice, once per `user`. Sessions that were deleted or left are not returned. `limit` defaults to `100`. For one user\'s sessions, call `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/messagesessions]

8d8e864e72292722.description: List phone numbers in all domains — Returns the phone numbers across every domain your token can see, with where calls to each one go and its SMS assignment, if any. Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope. A Reseller sees the domains in its territory. A Super User sees every domain, or one territory with `territory`. Super User Read Only must send `territory`.  Numbers that exist only as an SMS assignment follow the dial-rule rows with `sms-only` set to `true`, up to 5,000 of them. `start` and `limit` page across both sets, 100 rows at a time unless you set `limit`. An SMS-only row whose domain was deleted carries `domain-invalid`.  The platform\'s default DID table is read, so a domain whose `inventory.did-table` setting names another dial plan is missing from this list. For one domain, use `GET /domains/{domain}/phonenumbers`. For the total, call `GET /phonenumbers/count`. — [GET /phonenumbers]

dial-rule-application.description: Returns only the numbers that use this application, such as `to-user` or `available-number`. Use `%` as the wildcard: `to-callqueue%` matches every call queue application.

dial-rule-description.description: Returns only the numbers whose description matches this pattern. Use `%` as the wildcard, for example `Sales%`.

dial-rule-parameter.description: Returns only the numbers whose application parameter is exactly this value.

dial-rule-translation-destination-host.description: Returns only the numbers routed to this destination host, exact match.

dial-rule-translation-destination-user.description: Returns only the numbers routed to this destination, exact match. `lookup:` needs a domain to look in, so on this path it matches no number. Use `GET /domains/{domain}/phonenumbers` for it.

enabled.description: Returns only enabled (`yes`) or disabled (`no`) numbers. `all`, or leaving it out, returns both. Allowed values: "yes", "no", "all". Default: "all"

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page. Default: 100

start.description: The zero-based offset of the first row to return. Paging runs over the dial-rule rows first, then the SMS-only rows. Default: 0

territory.description: Returns only the numbers in domains of this territory. A Super User can name any territory. A Reseller sees only its own territory, with or without this parameter.

8d8e864e72292722.title: Get Phonenumbers

593ddff9d31715e0.description: List phone numbers — Returns the phone numbers assigned to a domain, with where calls to each one go and its SMS assignment, if any. Every user scope can read the numbers of its own domain. A Reseller reads the domains in its territory, and Super User and Super User Read Only read every domain.  Numbers that exist only as an SMS assignment, with no dial rule, follow the dial-rule rows with `sms-only` set to `true`. `start` and `limit` page across both sets, 100 rows at a time unless you set `limit`. For the total, call `GET /domains/{domain}/phonenumbers/count` with the same filters.  Each domain keeps its numbers in the dial plan its `inventory.did-table` setting names, `DID Table` unless the domain changes it. Numbers that are not assigned to any domain are not listed here. — [GET /domains/{domain}/phonenumbers]

dial-rule-application.description: Returns only the numbers that use this application, such as `to-user` or `available-number`. Use `%` as the wildcard: `to-callqueue%` matches every call queue application.

dial-rule-description.description: Returns only the numbers whose description matches this pattern. Use `%` as the wildcard, for example `Sales%`.

dial-rule-parameter.description: Returns only the numbers whose application parameter is exactly this value.

dial-rule-translation-destination-host.description: Returns only the numbers routed to this destination host, exact match.

dial-rule-translation-destination-user.description: Returns only the numbers routed to this destination, exact match. f30553830e44c0ec.description: Update phone number by body — Changes where calls to a phone number go, or its other settings. Name the number in the body with `phonenumber`. It is the same change as `PUT /domains/{domain}/phonenumbers/{phonenumber}`, with the number in the body instead of the path. Requires Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Scopes below Reseller change only their own domain, and a Reseller only the domains in its territory.  The request is a partial update: a field you leave out keeps its value. A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made right away can still show the old values.  A Reseller or Super User can name a number that is not assigned to any domain. The change assigns it to the domain in the path. A Super User can also name a number assigned to another domain, and the change moves it to the domain in the path, so check the path before you send.  A number that has only an SMS assignment can be changed too. Send only `sms-*` fields to change the assignment, or `dial-rule-translation-destination-user` to give the number a dial rule.  If an Office Manager sends `dial-rule-translation-destination-host`, it must be its own domain, except with the `to-connection` and `to-single-device` applications, or the request answers `403`. A number in neither place answers `404`: add it with `POST /domains/{domain}/phonenumbers`.  ### Send to a user  Set `dial-rule-application` to `to-user`, `dial-rule-translation-destination-user` to the user\'s extension, and `dial-rule-translation-destination-host` to your domain.  ### Send to a call queue  Set `dial-rule-application` to `to-callqueue` and `dial-rule-translation-destination-user` to the queue\'s extension.  ### Use another application  Set `dial-rule-application` to any other application, such as `to-connection-add-header-update-cdr-by-user` for an off-net number. Put a header the application adds in `dial-rule-parameter`.  ### Move back to available  Set `dial-rule-application` to `available-number`, the destination user and host to `[*]`, and `dial-rule-parameter` to `<NULL>`. The number stays in this domain, ready to assign again.  ### Change other fields  Leave `dial-rule-application` out and send the fields to change: `enabled`, the description, the destination, the caller ID name, or the `sms-*` fields. Send `sms-enabled` `false` to remove the SMS assignment.  A body without `phonenumber` answers `400`. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/phonenumbers]

45b54037285f1545.description: Add phone — Adds a phone to the inventory on the Endpoints server by MAC address, so it can download its configuration. Send `device-provisioning-mac-address` and `device-models-brand-and-model`, and `domain`. The MAC address can use `:`, `-`, or `.` separators, and is stored as 12 bare hex digits. Assign lines with `device-provisioning-sip-uri-1` to `device-provisioning-sip-uri-8`. A line you assign is enabled unless you send its `device-provisioning-line-N-enabled`. The user who owns line 1 is the phone\'s user.  Requires Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Site Manager can put only a device of a user in its site on line 1. Basic User and the other user scopes can add a phone only with their own device on line 1.  The response is `202`: the phone is accepted and added shortly after. A MAC address that already exists in any domain returns `409`. A soft phone model (`Manual or Softphone`) or a blank model returns `400`, because there is nothing to provision. For Yealink, Polycom, Snom, Fanvil, Grandstream, and Htek phones, the MAC address is also registered with the vendor\'s zero-touch provisioning service when the platform has one configured.  Every line (`device-provisioning-sip-uri-1` and up) must be a device in the phone\'s own domain. Line 1 must also belong to a user you may act for; lines 2 and up can be any device in the domain, for shared or monitored lines. A line from another domain returns `400`. — [POST /phones]

8abc041bc9400f1d.description: Update phone — Changes a phone, found by `device-provisioning-mac-address` in the body. Send only the fields to change. When you change a line and leave out `device-models-brand-and-model`, the phone keeps its stored model. A line you assign is enabled unless you send its `device-provisioning-line-N-enabled`. Setting `device-provisioning-line-N-enabled` to `no` on line 1 or 2 clears that line\'s extension.  Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Site Manager can change a phone whose line 1 belongs to a user in its site, and hand line 1 only to a user in its site. Basic User and the other user scopes can change only their own phone, the one whose line 1 they own. Another user\'s phone, a phone with nobody on line 1, or giving line 1 to someone else returns `403`. A phone in a domain your token cannot reach returns `404`. Super User can change any phone.  The response is `202`: the change is accepted and applied shortly after. `created-datetime` never changes. Every change clears `device-provisioning-last-retrieved-datetime` until the phone downloads its configuration again. `device-provisioning-password` as returned by a read is masked. Sending that masked value back keeps the stored password. A soft phone model (`Manual or Softphone`) returns `400`.  Every line (`device-provisioning-sip-uri-1` and up) must be a device in the phone\'s own domain. Line 1 must also belong to a user you may act for; lines 2 and up can be any device in the domain, for shared or monitored lines. A line from another domain returns `400`. Changing `domain` moves the phone and every line on it: you need access to the target domain (a Reseller, a domain in its own reseller; other scopes, their own domain), or the request returns `403`. — [PUT /phones]

d80f0ad84aa043cc.description: Delete phone — Removes a phone from the Endpoints server inventory, found by `device-provisioning-mac-address` in the body or query string. Send `domain` too unless you are a Super User. The phone\'s own configuration (`/domains/{domain}/phoneconfiguration/{mac}`) is removed with it. To free one line instead of removing the phone, also send `id` (the device on that line) and `user` (its owner). If that device is on line 2 or higher, only that line is cleared and the phone stays. On line 1, or when the device\'s line cannot be found, the whole phone is removed.  Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Site Manager can remove phones whose line 1 belongs to a user in its site. Basic User and the other user scopes can remove only their own phone, the one whose line 1 they own. A phone filed in a domain other than the one you name returns `404`.  The response is `202`: the removal is accepted and applied shortly after. The devices on the phone\'s lines are not removed. — [DELETE /phones]

device-provisioning-mac-address.description: MAC address of the phone: 12 hex digits with no separators.

domain.description: Domain the phone belongs to. Required unless you are a Super User. Not needed on `/domains/{domain}/phones`, where the path names it.

id.description: Device to take off the phone, such as `1002a`. Send it with `user` to free only that device's line. If the device is on line 1, the whole phone is removed.

user.description: User that owns the device in `id`, such as `1002`. Needed only when freeing one line.

a6fb36e017091c90.description: List phones in domain — Lists the domain\'s provisioned phones by MAC address, with each phone\'s model, line assignments, and line 1 registration state. Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Site Manager uses `GET /domains/{domain}/phones/list` instead, and Basic User and the other user scopes read their own phone with `GET /domains/{domain}/phones/{mac}`.  Results are paged with `start` and `limit`. Get the total with `GET /domains/{domain}/phones/count`, or a reduced row per phone with `GET /domains/{domain}/phones/list`. Per-line passwords are left out, and `device-provisioning-password` is masked except on your own phone. A Super User can send `include-secrets=yes` to get them in plaintext. The reveal is audit-logged.  A phone\'s own configuration overrides are returned as `device-provisioning-overrides-blob`. The same value is also returned as `device-models-overrides-blob`, which is deprecated and will be removed in the next release. — [GET /domains/{domain}/phones]

extension.description: Only phones with a device on any line whose address contains this text, such as `1001`. Part of an address matches, so `100` also matches `1001`.

include-secrets.description: `yes` returns `device-provisioning-password` and the per-line passwords in plaintext. Super User only. Any other scope gets `403`. The reveal is audit-logged. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

aa3ebeccc5de310f.description: Add phone in domain — Adds a phone to the domain\'s inventory on the Endpoints server by MAC address, so it can download its configuration. Send `device-provisioning-mac-address` and `device-models-brand-and-model`. The MAC address can use `:`, `-`, or `.` separators, and is stored as 12 bare hex digits. Assign lines with `device-provisioning-sip-uri-1` to `device-provisioning-sip-uri-8`. A line you assign is enabled unless you send its `device-provisioning-line-N-enabled`. The user who owns line 1 is the phone\'s user. The domain comes from the path.  Requires Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Site Manager can put only a device of a user in its site on line 1. Basic User and the other user scopes can add a phone only with their own device on line 1.  The response is `202`: the phone is accepted and added shortly after. A MAC address that already exists in any domain returns `409`. A soft phone model (`Manual or Softphone`) or a blank model returns `400`, because there is nothing to provision. For Yealink, Polycom, Snom, Fanvil, Grandstream, and Htek phones, the MAC address is also registered with the vendor\'s zero-touch provisioning service when the platform has one configured.  Every line (`device-provisioning-sip-uri-1` and up) must be a device in the phone\'s own domain. Line 1 must also belong to a user you may act for; lines 2 and up can be any device in the domain, for shared or monitored lines. A line from another domain returns `400`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/phones]

c3b93443ed37a9ae.description: Delete phone in domain — Removes a phone in the domain from the Endpoints server inventory, found by `device-provisioning-mac-address` in the body or query string. The phone\'s own configuration (`/domains/{domain}/phoneconfiguration/{mac}`) is removed with it. To free one line instead of removing the phone, also send `id` (the device on that line) and `user` (its owner). If that device is on line 2 or higher, only that line is cleared and the phone stays. On line 1, or when the device\'s line cannot be found, the whole phone is removed.  Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Site Manager can remove phones whose line 1 belongs to a user in its site. Basic User and the other user scopes can remove only their own phone, the one whose line 1 they own. A phone filed in a domain other than the one you name returns `404`.  The response is `202`: the removal is accepted and applied shortly after. The devices on the phone\'s lines are not removed. — [DELETE /domains/{domain}/phones]

device-provisioning-mac-address.description: MAC address of the phone: 12 hex digits with no separators.

domain.description: Domain the phone belongs to. Required unless you are a Super User. Not needed on `/domains/{domain}/phones`, where the path names it.

id.description: Device to take off the phone, such as `1002a`. Send it with `user` to free only that device's line. If the device is on line 1, the whole phone is removed.

user.description: User that owns the device in `id`, such as `1002`. Needed only when freeing one line.

d60b8bca60d75f2d.description: List device models — Returns the phone and gateway models that the Endpoints server (NDP) can provision, from `device_models`, one object per model. Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope.  By default the list holds only models whose `device-models-visible-in-portal` is `yes` and whose type is `Device` or `AnalogGW`. Models whose config format is `Counterpath` are always left out. Send `portal_view=any` to include hidden models, and send `device_type` as a comma-separated list to choose types.  Send both `brand` and `model`, or send `brand_model`, to get one object instead of a list. That form still applies the defaults above, and it returns `404` when nothing matches. To read any model by its key, whatever its type or visibility, use `GET /phones/models/{brand}/{model}`. Use `GET /phones/models/count` for a total with the same defaults. — [GET /phones/models]

brand.description: Vendor-cased brand, such as `Polycom`. On its own, it filters the list. With `model`, it returns one object.

brand_model.description: Brand and model separated by one space, such as `Yealink SIP-T42G`. Returns one object instead of a list. Also accepted as `device-models-brand-and-model`.

device_type.description: Comma-separated types to include: `Device`, `AnalogGW`, `DigitalGW`. The default is `Device,AnalogGW`. Also accepted as `device-models-type`.

fields.description: Comma-separated v2 field names to return instead of every field.

limit.description: Maximum number of models to return. Omit it to get every model. Default: 100

model.description: Model name. With `brand`, it returns one object instead of a list.

ndp_syntax.description: Config format to match, such as `Polycom` or `CiscoSPA`. `Counterpath` models are always excluded. Also accepted as `device-models-config-format`.

portal_view.description: `yes` (the default) returns models shown in the portal, and `no` returns hidden ones. `any` or `all` returns both. Also accepted as `device-models-visible-in-portal`. Allowed values: "yes", "no", "any", "all". Default: "yes"

sort.description: A column name such as `brand` or `model`, optionally followed by ` DESC`. Separate several with commas. Use the column names, not the v2 field names; a v2 name is ignored.

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

1e22c009cf6a67fd.description: List core servers — Returns the core servers that the Endpoints server (NDP) provisions devices against, from `servers_config`. Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope.  The fields you get depend on your scope. A Reseller gets `name`, `address-location-description`, `device-provisioning-redundancy-group`, the TCP and TLS ports, `backup_ok`, the postfix and API FQDNs, and `status`, plus their aliases. Super User and Super User Read Only also get the hostname, database, TAC, OAuth, and token-expiry fields. Credentials are left out unless a Super User sends `include-secrets=yes`, and every such request is logged. Certificates are left out unless you send `include-certs=yes`.  Omit `server` to list every server. Name one server to get it and every server in the same redundancy group. Send a bracketed list such as `[east,west]` to list whole redundancy groups. Add `geo_group` to keep only servers in one redundancy group; it narrows whatever `server` selected. An unmatched filter returns `[]`. Use `GET /phones/servers/count` for a total. — [GET /phones/servers]

geo_group.description: Redundancy group to keep. Combines with `server`: a server outside this group is left out. Blank is ignored.

include-certs.description: `yes` adds the PEM fields `core-server-cert` and `core-server-ca`. Super User or Super User Read Only. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

include-secrets.description: `yes` adds the credential fields in plain text. Super User only, not Super User Read Only. Every request is logged. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

server.description: Filter. Omit it, or send `SiPbx`, `lookup`, or `*`, to list every server. A server name returns that server and every server in its redundancy group. A server with no group returns only itself. A bracketed, comma-separated list such as `[east,west]` returns every server in those redundancy groups.

3ea920f0cfba7292.description: Read core server — Returns one core server from `servers_config`. Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope.  The fields you get depend on your scope, exactly as on `GET /phones/servers`. Credentials need `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Certificates need `include-certs=yes`. Unlike the list, this read returns only the named server, not its redundancy group.  An unknown name returns `404`. — [GET /phones/servers/{server}]

include-certs.description: `yes` adds the PEM fields `core-server-cert` and `core-server-ca`. Super User or Super User Read Only. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

include-secrets.description: `yes` adds the credential fields in plain text. Super User only, not Super User Read Only. Every request is logged. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

server.description: The core server's `name`. Letters, digits, spaces, and `* . - _ '`. `readconfig` is reserved for `GET /phones/servers/readconfig`.
