de7c17af8feb2b25.description: Read recording of user call — Returns the recording of a call that the user in the path was part of, with a signed `file-access-url` that plays it. Scopes: Basic User and Call Center Agent on their own user; Office Manager and Site Manager on their domain; Reseller on their territory; Super User.  The response is one recording, not an array. When a call has several recordings, the first one made for this user, one of the user\'s devices, or a domain-wide rule (`*@domain`) is returned. Narrow it with `call-recording-match-pattern`.  A Super User Read Only token is refused unless it is a party to the call.  To list every recording of a call in a domain, use `GET /domains/{domain}/recordings/{callid}`. To play the audio, open `file-access-url`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/recordings/{callid}]

call-recording-match-pattern.description: Return only the recording made for this case, exact match: `user@domain`, or `*@domain` for a domain-wide rule. Also accepted as `case_id`.

callid.description: The SIP call ID of either leg of the call, as `orig-callid` or `term-callid` on its CDR. Letters, digits, `@`, `*`, `.`, `-`, `_`, and `'`.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

Scopes: Office Manager and Site Manager on their domain, Reseller on their territory, and Super User. A Basic User reads their own calls with `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/recordings/{callid}`.  A call can have several recordings, one per case it matched, such as the user\'s own rule and a domain-wide rule. Only recordings whose case belongs to the domain, or to a SIP trunk in it, are returned. Narrow them with `call-recording-match-pattern`.  A Super User Read Only token is refused unless it is a party to the call. — [GET /domains/{domain}/recordings/{callid}]

callid.description: The SIP call ID of either leg of the call, as `orig-callid` or `term-callid` on its CDR. Letters, digits, `@`, `*`, `.`, `-`, `_`, and `'`.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

622193b6d7853299.description: List territories — Returns territories with their SMTP settings and live totals: domains, users, and active calls. A territory is the configuration record that a Reseller\'s domains belong to, and `reseller` is its name.  Super User and Super User Read Only see every territory. A Reseller sees only its own, as a one-item array. A Reseller that filters on another territory gets `403`, and so does every other scope.  Filter with `reseller`. Page with `start` and `limit`, 100 territories by default, and sort by `reseller` or `description`. Use `GET /resellers/count` for a total, and `GET /resellers/list` for names and descriptions only. 1c20e909ab97a196.description: List routes — Returns the platform\'s call routes from `route_config`, each with the `route-id` you use to read, update, or delete it and to manage its route connections. Routes apply to the whole platform, not to one domain or territory. Requires Super User, Reseller, or Super User Read Only scope.  Without `route-destination-match-pattern`, the list holds only routes whose destination pattern starts with `sip` and contains `@`, such as `sip:1800*@*`. That leaves out the routes behind route profiles, which you read with `GET /domains/{domain}/routeprofiles`. Every filter is an exact match, and filters combine. Rows are sorted by `route-destination-match-pattern` and paged with `start` and `limit`, 100 rows by default.  `GET /routes/count` takes the same filters and counts the same rows. `GET /routes/{route-id}` returns one route. — [GET /routes]

5d84b5dcb1231a16.description: Create route — Adds a call route to `route_config`. Routes apply to the whole platform. Requires Super User scope. Other scopes, Reseller included, get `403`. The API publishes the change on the service bus (SBUS) `NmsRoute` channel, and core applies it when the event arrives, so `202` means published, not applied.  Only `route-destination-match-pattern` is required. `route-source-match-pattern`, `route-class`, and `route-match-server-hostname` default to `*`, `route-is-enabled` to `yes`, and `route-method` to `fixed`. Those 4 match fields identify the route, and `route-id` encodes them. The API does not check for an existing route with the same 4 values.  Send `synchronous=yes`, in the body or the query string, to wait up to 2 seconds for the change to be applied. You then get `200` with the route and its `route-id`. If it is not applied in time, you get the usual `202` and the write still completes.  Add the route\'s next hops with `POST /routes/{route-id}/routecon`. — [POST /routes]

description.description: Free-text description of what the route is for.

route-class.description: Call class the route applies to. `*`, the default, matches every class. Part of the route's identity. Default: "*"

route-destination-match-pattern.description: Destination pattern a call must match, such as `sip:1800*@*`. Required on create. Part of the route's identity.

route-id.description: Read only. Key for `PUT` and `DELETE /routes/{route-id}` and the route's connections: base64url, without padding, of `route-destination-match-pattern` when the other 3 match fields are `*`, otherwise of all 4 joined by `||`.

route-is-enabled.description: `yes` or `no`. Defaults to `yes`. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "yes"

route-match-server-hostname.description: Core server hostname the route is limited to, such as `core1.example.com`. `*`, the default, applies it on every core server. Part of the route's identity. Default: "*"

route-method.description: How the route picks a connection: `fixed` tries them in `route-connection-ordinal-index` order, `cost` picks the lowest `route-connection-integer-cost`, and `percentage` splits calls by `route-connection-integer-percentage`. Defaults to `fixed`. Allowed values: "fixed", "cost", "percentage"

route-source-match-pattern.description: Source pattern a call must match. `*`, the default, matches every caller. Part of the route's identity. Default: "*"

synchronous.description: `yes` waits until the change is applied before answering. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

81decc9115d8b1dc.description: List sites — Returns the domain\'s sites, 100 by default, sorted by name. A site is a system extension that holds settings for the users and call queues filed under it, such as dial plan, caller ID, time zone, and emergency address. The site\'s name is in `site`, and also in `user` for older clients.  Requires Office Manager, Site Manager, or Basic User in the domain, Reseller for a domain in your territory, or Super User or Super User Read Only. A Site Manager and a Basic User see every site in the domain, not only their own. Other scopes, and a Reseller outside its territory, get `403`.  Page with `start` and `limit`. Use `fields` to return only the fields you name. The site name is always included. `sort` defaults to `user asc`. `site` returns only that site, with the shorter field set and live counts that `GET /domains/{domain}/sites/{site}` returns. `billing=yes` adds those counts to every site, at the cost of several queries per site.  When a site has no emergency address of its own, `emergency-address-id` is the domain\'s and `emergency-address-source` is `domain_level`. Credentials and identity fields of the site\'s extension, such as its voicemail PIN, are never returned.  Use `GET /domains/{domain}/sites/count` for a total, and `GET /domains/{domain}/sites/list` for a short form of every site. `PUT` and `DELETE` on this collection path return `405`: address one site by name. — [GET /domains/{domain}/sites]

fields.description: Comma-separated field names to return, such as `site,dial-plan,time-zone`. The site name is always included. Names that are not site fields, and fields a site never returns, are ignored; if none is left, every field is returned.

2f581fe7b7dad62d.description: Create site — Creates a site. Send its name in `site`, and any settings the site\'s users should share, such as `dial-plan`, `caller-id-number`, `time-zone`, or `emergency-address-id`.  Requires Office Manager in the domain, Reseller for a domain in your territory, or Super User. Site Manager, Basic User, Super User Read Only, and every other scope get `403`.  The name is the site\'s key and cannot be changed later. Use letters, digits, spaces, and `.`, `-`, `_`, `\'` only. The create accepts other characters, but a site named with them cannot be read, updated, or deleted by its path. Avoid `*`, which scope checks read as a wildcard. The name shares the domain\'s extension namespace:  - a name another site uses returns `409` `Site already exists` - a name a user or other extension uses returns `409` `Extension already exists` - a login already in use returns `409` `Login already exists`, naming the extension that holds it  The login defaults to `<site>@<domain>`. Set `login-username` to choose another. Check a name first with `GET /domains/{domain}/sites/count?site=<name>`.  Settings you leave out are copied from the domain\'s defaults. A user created later with `site` set copies the site\'s dial plan, dial policy, caller ID, time zone, area code, limits, language, and emergency address, unless the request sets them. Creating a user with a `site` that does not exist also creates that site.  A `202` means the site was published over the service bus (SBUS), not yet created, so a read straight after it can still return `404`. With `synchronous=yes`, the call waits up to 2 seconds. It returns `200` with the site once the site appears, or `202` if it has not appeared yet. — [POST /domains/{domain}/sites]

With `reseller`, the response is a list of the numbers alone, as strings, for every domain in the territory, up to 20,000. `domain`, `dest`, and `number` still narrow it, and `site` is ignored. With no filters, every number in the domain is returned. Filter with `dest`, `number`, `number_LIKE`, or `site`, and page with `start` and `limit`. `mms-capable` and `group-mms-capable` appear only on numbers whose carrier supports them.  To count the same numbers, use `GET /domains/{domain}/smsnumbers/count`. To read one number, use `GET /domains/{domain}/smsnumbers/{smsnumber}`. To list one user\'s numbers, use `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/smsnumbers`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/smsnumbers]

40c9d112871f9b2e.description: Create SMS number — Adds an SMS number to the domain in the path and assigns it to a user, a call queue, or the domain\'s pool of available numbers.  Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope.  Set `application` to `user` or `callqueue` and `dest` to the extension or call queue that receives messages, or set `application` to `available` to hold the number unassigned. `available` always clears `dest`. `carrier`, when sent, must name an SMS carrier configured on the platform, listed by `GET /smscarriers`. When the number goes to a user, that user\'s messaging profile gains it.  A number belongs to one domain. A number already held by another domain returns `409`: delete it from that domain first.  A `202` means the number is accepted and applied shortly after. Read it back with `GET /domains/{domain}/smsnumbers/{smsnumber}`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/smsnumbers]

application.description: What the number delivers to: `user` for a user's extension, `callqueue` for a call queue, or `available` for the domain's pool of unassigned numbers. Allowed values: "user", "callqueue", "available"

carrier.description: SMS carrier that sends and receives messages for this number, such as `bandwidth`. It must be a carrier configured on the platform, listed by `GET /smscarriers`. Matched without regard to case and stored as the configured name.

dest.description: Extension or call queue that receives messages to this number. Required in practice for `user` and `callqueue`. Cleared when `application` is `available`.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

notes.description: Free-text note, for example why the number was released.

number.description: SMS number: digits with the country code and no `+`, such as `15555550100`. A number belongs to one domain only. Use digits only, or the number cannot be changed or deleted by its path later.

1c818108186b5a61.description: Update SMS number — Changes the assignment, carrier, or note of an SMS number in the domain in the path.  Requires Office Manager, Site Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Site Manager changes only numbers routed to users in its own site, and can assign them only to users in its site.  Send `application` on every update, even when you change only `carrier` or `notes`. Fields you leave out keep their values. Setting `application` to `available` releases the number to the pool and clears `dest`. Reassigning a number moves it from the old user\'s messaging profile to the new one\'s.  A number that is not in this domain returns `404`. A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after. Read it back with `GET /domains/{domain}/smsnumbers/{smsnumber}`. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/smsnumbers/{smsnumber}]

273c5a55ceda22bf.description: List domain time frames — Returns the domain\'s shared time frames with their entries. Answer rules of every user in the domain can use them.  Any Basic User, Site Manager, or Office Manager in the domain can read its shared time frames. A Reseller can read the domains in its territory, and a Super User any domain.  Each time frame carries its date ranges, days of week entry, or holidays, with the next dates it applies (`timeframe-next-observance-datetime`) and `end_on`. Page with `limit` and `start`; `limit` defaults to `100`. Time frames created before IDs existed are converted on the fly and added after the page. A domain with no time frames returns `[]`.  `GET /domains/{domain}/timeframes/list` returns only names and state, and `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/timeframes` returns a user\'s own time frames. — [GET /domains/{domain}/timeframes]

The `user`, `user_name`, and `owner` values order the per-user rows of `users=all`. Any other value returns `400`. ac97e3f1107fcd2c.description: Create domain time frame — Creates a time frame owned by the domain, shared by every user in it, of the type `timeframe-type` names. Answer rules use it by `timeframe-name`.  Requires Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User. A Basic User can read shared time frames but gets `403` on a write.  The write is published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied a moment later, so the call answers `202` by default. Send `synchronous=yes` to wait up to 10 seconds and get `200` with the time frame instead. The time frame ID is generated from the name and owner, so you do not send one; it is `timeframe-id` in the response.  **Always.** Matches at every moment and has no entries. The call waits about 2 seconds and always answers `200` with the time frame.  **Days of week.** One weekly schedule in `timeframe-days-of-week-array`, with up to 2 periods per day as `hhmm` times. The array is required and holds at most 1 entry. `timeframe-recurrence-type` is `weekly`, or `custom` with the custom interval fields.  **Specific dates.** Date ranges in `timeframe-specific-dates-array`, each with begin and end dates as `YYYYMMDD` and times as `hhmm`. With more than 1 range, all must share one recurrence type, `annual-month-day` or `doesNotRecur`.  **Holiday.** Holidays in `timeframe-holiday-array`, copied from `GET /holidays/{country}/{year}` or `GET /holidays/{country}/{region}/{year}`. Every holiday needs `timeframe-holiday-begin-date` and a `timeframe-recurrence-type`, `never` or `yearlyOnHoliday`, and all must share it. A holiday may appear once. A holiday whose date has already passed answers `422` and nothing is created.  **Custom.** Any mix of the three arrays, without the single-entry and shared-recurrence rules.  Every entry is checked before anything is published, so a `400` or `422` creates nothing. A name the owner already uses returns `400`, and a user that does not exist returns `400` with `Invalid user/domain.` Add entries later with `POST` on the time frame, and change or convert it with `PUT`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/timeframes]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

Requires Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User. A Basic User can read shared time frames but gets `403` on a write.  The write is published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied a moment later, so the call answers `202` by default. Send `synchronous=yes` to wait up to 10 seconds and get `200` with the time frame instead. Entry IDs are generated; do not send `timeframe-id`.  **Specific dates.** New ranges must use the recurrence type the time frame already uses, `annual-month-day` or `doesNotRecur`.  **Holiday.** New holidays must use the time frame\'s recurrence type and must not repeat one already there. A holiday whose date has passed answers `422` and nothing is added.  **Days of week.** A days of week time frame holds 1 entry; once it has one, this returns `400`. Change it with `PUT`.  **Custom.** Any of the three arrays.  Every entry is checked before anything is published. An ID that does not exist, or that belongs to another owner than the path, returns `404` with `Provided \'id\' does not exist.` — [POST /domains/{domain}/timeframes/{id}]

132ab1f594fcbbe8.description: Update domain time frame — Changes a time frame: converts its type, updates some entries, or replaces them all. Requires Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User. A Basic User can read shared time frames but gets `403` on a write.  The call waits up to 10 seconds for the change and answers `200` with the time frame, except a type conversion, which answers `202` as soon as it is published.  **Convert type.** Send `timeframe-type` with a type other than the current one. Converting to `custom` keeps every entry; converting an `always` time frame to `custom` removes its all-day range, so it starts empty. Converting to any other type deletes every entry; send the new type\'s array in the same request to fill it. A `custom` time frame cannot be converted, and the request is treated as an update.  **Update entries.** Send `update-only=yes` with the entries to change, each with its `timeframe-id`. An entry without an ID is created. Nothing is deleted. For a holiday, only its hours, observance options, workweek, and recurrence change; delete it and add the new one to change the holiday itself.  **Replace entries.** Without `update-only`, every entry you do not list by `timeframe-id` is deleted, including every entry of a kind whose array you leave out. Listed entries are updated, and entries without an ID are created.  **Days of week.** A days of week time frame holds 1 entry: send exactly 1. More than 1 returns `400`.  The name cannot be changed. An always time frame has nothing to update; sending `timeframe-type=always` to one does nothing and answers `202`.  Every entry is checked before anything is published, so a `400` changes nothing. An ID that does not exist, or that belongs to another owner than the path, returns `404`. A holiday date that has already passed returns `400`. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/timeframes/{id}]

64f23ac11281e015.description: List holidays by country — Returns the holidays of a country in one year, to fill the holidays of a holiday or custom time frame. Any authenticated token can call it: holiday data is not scoped to a domain, and no scope privilege is checked.  Each holiday gives the values a holiday time frame entry needs: `uuid` becomes `timeframe-holiday-uuid`, `name` `timeframe-holiday-name`, `date` `timeframe-holiday-begin-date`, `country` `country-abbreviation`, and `locations` `holiday-api-location-hint`. `date` is an integer `YYYYMMDD`. `states` is `All`, or a list of the region codes the holiday applies in.  Holidays come from the platform\'s holiday lookup service, a hosted Calendarific proxy the API calls over HTTPS with a 3-second connect and 8-second total limit. Answers are cached for 24 hours per country, region, year, and language; failures are not cached. If the service fails, times out, or answers anything but a holiday list, the call returns `503`; retry later. — [GET /holidays/{country}/{year}]

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code from `GET /holidays/countries`, such as `US`. Matched without regard to case. Anything but 2 letters returns `400`; a 2-letter code the lookup does not know returns `503`.

language.description: Language for `name` and `description`: `en`, `fr`, `es`, `de`, `it`, `pt`, or `nl`, matched without regard to case. Any other value returns `400`. The lookup chooses when you leave it out. Allowed values: "en", "fr", "es", "de", "it", "pt", "nl"

year.description: Year to list, as 4 digits from `2000` to `2099`, such as `2026`. Anything else returns `400`.

3ddda16cf2093138.description: List user time frames — Returns the time frames a user owns, with their entries.  Requires Basic User for your own time frames. An Office Manager can reach any user in its domain, and a Site Manager any user in its own site. A Reseller can reach the domains in its territory, and a Super User any domain. A user outside your reach returns `403` with `Issue with timeframe access`.  Send `include_domain_timeframes` to add the domain\'s shared time frames. Page with `limit` and `start`; `limit` defaults to `100`. Time frames created before IDs existed are converted on the fly and added after the page. A user with no time frames returns `[]`.  `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/timeframes/list` returns only names and state. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/timeframes]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

include_domain_timeframes.description: Any value also returns the domain (shared) time frames, which answer rules of this user can use. Leave it out for the user's own time frames only. Allowed values: "yes"

limit.description: Most time frames to return, a whole number. Defaults to `100`. Anything but digits returns `400`. Legacy time frames that have no ID yet are added after the page, whatever the limit. Default: 100

order.description: Storage order of the time frames before paging: comma-separated `id`, `domain`, `user`, `name`, or `type`, each optionally followed by `asc` or `desc`. Any other value returns `400`. Use `sort` to order the result.

sort.description: Order of the result. `name asc|desc` orders by `timeframe-name`. `ends_on asc|desc` orders by `end_on`, time frames that never end last in ascending order, and also orders each time frame's entries by recurrence end date. The `user`, `user_name`, and `owner` values order the per-user rows of `users=all`. Any other value returns `400`. Allowed values: "name asc", "name desc", "ends_on asc", "ends_on desc", "user asc", "user desc", "user_name asc", "user_name desc", "owner asc", "owner desc"

start.description: Time frames to skip before the first one returned, a whole number. Defaults to `0`. Anything but digits returns `400`. Default: 0

user.description: User who owns the time frames, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to. A user that does not exist returns `404` on a read and `400` on a create.

On a keyed path, `/timeframes/{id}/list`, it returns only that time frame, by ID or by name. **Changed in v46**: rows used to be name strings with the state appended; they are now objects with `selected` and `expired` fields. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/timeframes/list]

bd0e5aff03af46cc.description: Create user time frame — Creates a time frame owned by a user, of the type `timeframe-type` names. Answer rules use it by `timeframe-name`.  Requires Basic User for your own time frames, or Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User for the users you administer. An Office Manager can change any user in its domain, and a Site Manager any user in its own site. A user outside your reach returns `403` with `Issue with timeframe access`.  The write is published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied a moment later, so the call answers `202` by default. Send `synchronous=yes` to wait up to 10 seconds and get `200` with the time frame instead. The time frame ID is generated from the name and owner, so you do not send one; it is `timeframe-id` in the response.  **Always.** Matches at every moment and has no entries. The call waits about 2 seconds and always answers `200` with the time frame.  **Days of week.** One weekly schedule in `timeframe-days-of-week-array`, with up to 2 periods per day as `hhmm` times. The array is required and holds at most 1 entry. `timeframe-recurrence-type` is `weekly`, or `custom` with the custom interval fields.  **Specific dates.** Date ranges in `timeframe-specific-dates-array`, each with begin and end dates as `YYYYMMDD` and times as `hhmm`. With more than 1 range, all must share one recurrence type, `annual-month-day` or `doesNotRecur`.  **Holiday.** Holidays in `timeframe-holiday-array`, copied from `GET /holidays/{country}/{year}` or `GET /holidays/{country}/{region}/{year}`. Every holiday needs `timeframe-holiday-begin-date` and a `timeframe-recurrence-type`, `never` or `yearlyOnHoliday`, and all must share it. A holiday may appear once. A holiday whose date has already passed answers `422` and nothing is created.  **Custom.** Any mix of the three arrays, without the single-entry and shared-recurrence rules.  Every entry is checked before anything is published, so a `400` or `422` creates nothing. A name the owner already uses returns `400`, and a user that does not exist returns `400` with `Invalid user/domain.` Add entries later with `POST` on the time frame, and change or convert it with `PUT`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/timeframes]

A holiday whose date has passed answers `422` and nothing is added.  **Days of week.** A days of week time frame holds 1 entry; once it has one, this returns `400`. Change it with `PUT`.  **Custom.** Any of the three arrays.  Every entry is checked before anything is published. 1a3e15e2d0a2bff2.description: Update user time frame — Changes a time frame: converts its type, updates some entries, or replaces them all. Requires Basic User for your own time frames, or Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User for the users you administer. An Office Manager can change any user in its domain, and a Site Manager any user in its own site. A user outside your reach returns `403` with `Issue with timeframe access`.  The call waits up to 10 seconds for the change and answers `200` with the time frame, except a type conversion, which answers `202` as soon as it is published.  **Convert type.** Send `timeframe-type` with a type other than the current one. Converting to `custom` keeps every entry; converting an `always` time frame to `custom` removes its all-day range, so it starts empty. Converting to any other type deletes every entry; send the new type\'s array in the same request to fill it. A `custom` time frame cannot be converted, and the request is treated as an update.  **Update entries.** Send `update-only=yes` with the entries to change, each with its `timeframe-id`. An entry without an ID is created. Nothing is deleted. For a holiday, only its hours, observance options, workweek, and recurrence change; delete it and add the new one to change the holiday itself.  **Replace entries.** Without `update-only`, every entry you do not list by `timeframe-id` is deleted, including every entry of a kind whose array you leave out. Listed entries are updated, and entries without an ID are created.  **Days of week.** A days of week time frame holds 1 entry: send exactly 1. More than 1 returns `400`.  The name cannot be changed. An always time frame has nothing to update; sending `timeframe-type=always` to one does nothing and answers `202`.  Every entry is checked before anything is published, so a `400` changes nothing. An ID that does not exist, or that belongs to another owner than the path, returns `404`. A holiday date that has already passed returns `400`. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/timeframes/{id}]

Name the transcription with `id`, the `call-intelligence-job-id` from the CDR, and the month of the call with `date`. A transcription finished in the month after the call is found as well. Also send a call ID that belongs to the domain, and to the call the transcription is for: `orig_callid`, `term_callid`, or `by_callid` when you know which side it is, or `callid` to check both originating and terminating sides.  Processing is asynchronous. Until `call-intelligence-processing-status` is `finished`, some fields are empty.  For the whole call as one document, with every leg, recording, and transcript, use `GET /domains/{domain}/vcon/{cdr_id}`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/transcriptions]

callid.description: A call ID of the call, checked against both the originating and terminating sides. Send at least one of `callid`, `orig_callid`, `term_callid`, and `by_callid`; one of them must belong to a call of the domain in that month.

date.description: The month of the call, as 6 digits `YYYYMM`, such as `202609`. Anything else returns `400`.

term_callid.description: The terminating call ID of the call. Send at least one of `callid`, `orig_callid`, `term_callid`, and `by_callid`; one of them must belong to a call of the domain in that month.

Filters combine, so `site` and `department` together return the users in that site and department. Page with `limit` and `start`. `GET /domains/{domain}/users/count` takes the same filters and returns the total.  By default the response includes system users, such as call queues and auto attendants, and leaves out the rows that represent sites and departments. Use `filter_users` to change that.  The voicemail PIN is masked unless you send `include-secret=yes`.  The named examples show these uses:  - `All users`: no query parameters - `By site`: `?site=Main Office` - `By department`: `?department=Support` - `Search by last name`: `?name-last-name=Desk` - `By scope`: `?user-scope=Office Manager,Site Manager` - `Find by email`: `?email=user1001@example.com` - `People only`: `?filter_users=departments,sites,system` - `Paged and sorted`: `?limit=2&start=2&sort=user desc` - `Selected fields`: `?fields=user,name-first-name,name-last-name,email` - `PIN revealed`: `?include-secret=yes&site=Branch Office` — [GET /domains/{domain}/users]

An empty `password-hash` resets the account: it removes the user\'s single sign-on links and signs the user out. - **The masked PIN.** Sending back the masked `voicemail-login-pin` from a read leaves the PIN unchanged.  The response is `202`: the change is accepted and applied shortly after. 2a9477923d4e6b43.description: Read access log — Returns the compliance log: who signed in, who changed configuration, who read personal data or a credential, and what data left the platform, newest first. Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope. A Reseller sees only entries about data in the domains of its territory.  **Choose the entries with `event-category`.** Without it you get sign-ins and sign-outs (`session`) from the last 7 days. Send `access`, `disclosure`, or `all` for data reads and disclosures. Sign-in and change entries carry fewer fields: the filters marked "access and disclosure entries only" do not apply to them.  **Two common questions.** "What did this account read" is `by-user` with a date range. "Who read this record" is `record-id` with `target-object`. Add `credential=yes` to see every read that returned a secret.  **Data subjects are listed, not filterable.** Each entry names the people whose data it disclosed in `data-subjects`. To find who accessed data about one person, contact support.  **What counts as a disclosure depends on the regime.** `actor-tier` records where the reader sat relative to the data, and `exclude` removes categories. A HIPAA accounting of disclosures is `exclude=own-organisation`. GDPR excludes nothing.  Access entries are read from at most the 6 most recent months of the date range. Every page you read is itself recorded in the log. `GET /accesslog/count` returns the number of matching entries as `{"total": N}`. — [GET /accesslog]

action-type.description: Entries with this action, such as `read`, `list`, `search`, `play`, `download`, `export`, `login`, or `logout`. Exact match. `download` and `export` are the disclosure actions.

actor-tier.description: Entries where the reader was in this tier. To leave a tier out instead, use `exclude`. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries. Allowed values: "self", "reseller", "platform"

auditlog-details.description: Sign-in and change entries only: entries whose details contain this text. Applied only when `datetime-start` is also sent.

by-client.description: Entries from this application. Exact match.

by-domain.description: Entries where the reader belongs to this domain. It does not widen your scope: entries are still limited to data in domains you manage.

by-ip.description: Entries from this IP address. Exact match.

by-scope.description: Entries where the reader held this scope, such as `Office Manager`. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

by-user.description: Entries recorded against this reader, as a bare extension. Exact match.

credential.description: `yes` returns only entries whose response carried a secret, such as a SIP registration password, a provisioning password, a client secret, or a PIN. `no` returns the rest. `true`, `1`, and `on` also mean yes. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

datetime-end.description: Entries at or before this time, in the same formats as `datetime-start`. Defaults to now. Access entries are read from at most the 6 most recent months of the range.

datetime-start.description: Entries at or after this time, as an RFC 3339 date-time such as `2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00`. A trailing time zone name in brackets, such as `[America/New_York]`, and `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC are also accepted. Without it, sign-in and change entries start 7 days ago, and access entries start at the beginning of the month of `datetime-end`.

event-category.description: The kinds of entry to return, separated by commas: `session` (sign-ins and sign-outs), `change` (configuration changes), `access` (reads of personal data or a credential), `disclosure` (data that left the platform on its own, such as a served export file), or `all`. Defaults to `session`. An unrecognized value falls back to the default. Asking for `access` alone leaves out disclosures, and the other way around.

exclude.description: Leave out entries by the reader's relationship to the data, separated by commas: `own-user` (the reader is the person the data is about), `own-domain` (the reader is in the same domain), `own-organisation` (the same organization; `own-organization` also works), `reseller` (an intermediary), or `platform` (platform staff). Nothing is excluded by default, and an unrecognized value is ignored. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

gdpr-covered.description: `yes` returns entries where the data was subject to GDPR when read; `no` returns the rest. `gdpr` is also accepted as the name. `true`, `1`, and `on` also mean yes; any other value means no. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

hipaa-covered.description: `yes` returns entries where the data was subject to HIPAA when read; `no` returns the rest. `hipaa` is also accepted as the name. `true`, `1`, and `on` also mean yes; any other value means no. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

limit.description: The most entries to return. Defaults to 100. There is no upper limit. `0` or a negative number returns 1 entry. Default: 100

mask-chain.description: Entries where this account started a masquerade. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

part2-covered.description: `yes` returns entries where the data was subject to 42 CFR Part 2 when read; `no` returns the rest. `part2` is also accepted as the name. `true`, `1`, and `on` also mean yes; any other value means no. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

recipient.description: Entries where the data went to this destination rather than to the reader, such as a scheduled export's host. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

record-id.description: Entries about this one record, such as a CDR ID or a phone MAC address. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

schema-version.description: Entries written under this set of fields, such as `1.1`. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

target-domain.description: Entries about data in this domain. Repeat the parameter to name several. Every domain named must be inside your scope, or the request returns `403`. A blank value or `*` means no filter.

target-host.description: Entries recorded by this server. Exact match.

target-object.description: Entries about this kind of object. Takes the object name or the display label, so `user` and `Subscriber` match the same entries. Credential reads use the object name, such as `device`, `phoneconfiguration`, or `connection`.

target-user.description: Entries about this person, as a bare extension. Qualify it with `target-domain`.

ticket-reference.description: Entries recorded under this support ticket. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

1afab94326a55119.description: List server applications — Returns the applications registered on every server on the platform, one row per application per server, with addresses, version, and status. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.  Filter with `appinfo-element-id` and `appinfo-hostname`, and choose columns with `fields`. Every matching row is returned: this endpoint does not page or sort, so `limit`, `start`, and `sort` have no effect.  For the same inventory with paging, sorting, and more filters, use `GET /processes`. — [GET /appinfo]

appinfo-element-id.description: Return only rows for this application, such as `sipbx`. Exact match. Also accepted as `element_id`. A blank value matches nothing.

appinfo-hostname.description: Return only rows for this server. Exact match. Also accepted as `hostname`. A blank value matches nothing.

fields.description: The fields to return, separated by commas. Use the response names, such as `appinfo-hostname`, or the column names: `element_id`, `hostname`, `mac_address`, `ip_address`, `domain_db`, `element_type`, `element_version`, `element_status`, `element_start_time`, `status_update_time`, `app_address`, `app_address_v6`, `wan_address`, and `subnet_mask`. The response always uses the response names. An unknown name returns `400`. Omit it for whole rows.

1afab94326a55119.title: List Appinfo

5486f4ca2eda1510.description: List audit log entries — Lists configuration changes made on the platform, newest first: who made each change, from where, and to which domain, user, and object. With no dates it covers the last 7 days, and it returns up to 100 entries unless you set `limit`.  Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope. A Reseller sees only entries for domains in its own territory, in the change log and the access log alike, and naming any other domain in `target-domain` returns `403`.  Every filter is an exact match. Dates in the request are converted to UTC from any offset; dates in the response are in UTC. Credentials in `auditlog-details` are shown as `********`.  `event-category` chooses other kinds of entries: `session` returns sign-ins and sign-outs instead of changes, `change,session` returns both, and `access`, `disclosure`, or `all` return entries from the access log, described under `GET /accesslog`.  Send only the filters listed here. A query-builder key such as `OR` or `joins`, or a filter name that is not a plain field name, returns `400`. — [GET /auditlog]

action-type.description: Only entries of this kind, such as `create`, `update`, or `delete`, or `login` or `logout` with `event-category=session`.

auditlog-details.description: Only changes whose recorded details contain this text. Applies only when `datetime-start` is also set.

by-client.description: Only changes made through this client, such as `api` or `api-` followed by an OAuth client ID.

by-domain.description: Only changes made by users of this domain.

by-ip.description: Only changes made from this IP address.

by-user.description: Only changes made by this user, by extension, such as `1001`.

datetime-end.description: End of the time window, in the same forms as `datetime-start`. Defaults to now.

datetime-start.description: Start of the time window, in RFC 3339, such as `2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00`. An offset or a `[Zone]` suffix is converted to UTC, and `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` is read as UTC. Defaults to 7 days ago.

event-category.description: Kinds of entries to return, as a comma-separated list of `change`, `session`, `access`, and `disclosure`, or `all`. Leave it out for configuration changes alone. `session` alone returns sign-ins and sign-outs. An unrecognized value is ignored.

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page. Default: 100

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

target-domain.description: Only entries for this domain. To match any of several domains, repeat it with brackets: `target-domain[]=example.com&target-domain[]=example.net`. A Reseller may name only domains in its own territory.

target-host.description: Only changes recorded by this server.

target-object.description: Only changes to this kind of object, by the name the entries show, such as `Subscriber` or `Call Queue`.

target-user.description: Only changes to this user, by extension, such as `1002`.

cd976bad43596b04.description: Delete auto attendant — Deletes one auto attendant: the `{prompt}` tier with its submenus and intro greetings.  Requires Office Manager, Site Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Site Manager can delete only attendants of users in their site.  Every answering rule of the user that sent calls to the attendant stops forwarding, so its calls go to the user\'s other settings again. The rest of the user\'s dial plan, its other attendants, and the user itself are not changed. A submenu that another attendant also starts at is kept. Naming a submenu\'s tier deletes that submenu only, and the key that opened it stays: change the key with **Update auto attendant**. A `PUT` or `DELETE` on `/domains/{domain}/autoattendants`, without the user and tier in the path, returns `405`.  The response is `202`: the deletion is accepted and applied shortly after. — [DELETE /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/autoattendants/{prompt}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

prompt.description: Tier to change, `Prompt_<n>`, such as `Prompt_100`. Use the attendant's `starting-prompt` from **List auto attendants in domain**, or a submenu's tier. Any other value, or a tier the user does not have, returns `404`.

user.description: Extension that answers as the auto attendant, such as `8000`. It is the `user` in the attendant's `read-path`. `~` means your own user.

cd976bad43596b04.title: Delete Domains Domain Users User Autoattendants Prompt

3ff9d2d558f90236.description: Read avatar image — Serves an avatar image of at most 48 by 48 pixels: a user\'s, a contact\'s, or a generic one. `path`, `path-small`, and `path-large` in the avatar reads point here. No authentication is needed, so an `` tag can load it directly. Anyone who has the filename can load the image. Images are stored as WebP. Ask for the same name with `.jpg` or `.png` and you get a JPEG or PNG copy, converted on first request and kept on disk; a JPEG has a white background in place of transparency. The answer carries `Cache-Control: public, max-age=2592000` (30 days), `Expires`, `Last-Modified`, and a strong `ETag`. Send `If-None-Match` or `If-Modified-Since` to get a bodyless `304` while your copy is current. A filename never changes content, so a new avatar has a new filename; a deleted avatar returns `404` here, but copies already cached by browsers or proxies can outlive it by up to 30 days. For the image of at most 256 by 256 pixels, call `GET /avatar/256/{filename}`. — [GET /avatar/{filename}]

filename.description: Avatar filename: the stored name, 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters plus `.webp`, as `filename` in the avatar reads. Send the same name with `.jpg` or `.png` instead for a JPEG or PNG copy. Any other form is not an image request: without a token it returns `401`.

6a7faa15bdd34f84.description: Restore domain from backup by path — Restores the domain in the path from one of its backups. This overwrites the domain\'s current data: the backup\'s database files are imported, the domain\'s stored files are restored, and the domain is reloaded.  Requires Reseller or Super User scope.  List the restore points with `GET /domains/{domain}/restore` first. Send the chosen point\'s server as `hostname`, its `type`, its `day` as `index`, and its `confirmation-value` in the body. A missing field returns `400` naming it. Values that do not identify exactly one current restore point also return `400`.  The call waits for the restore to finish, which can take up to 5 minutes. With `geo` set to `yes`, the restore is queued instead, and the response carries only `logs`. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/restore]

confirmation-value.description: The restore point's `confirmation-value`, from the restore-point list. It proves you picked the point that exists now.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

geo.description: `yes` queues the restore and answers at once, without waiting for it to finish. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

hostname.description: Server that holds the backup, as keyed in the restore-point list.

index.description: Restore point to restore, from its `day`. Nightly backups use `0` to `6`. Manual backups use the `backup-index` the backup returned.

type.description: Kind of backup, from the restore point's `type`. Allowed values: "nightly", "manual"

Each entry names the brand it came from in `source-hostname`, `source-reseller`, `source-domain`, and `source-brand-name`. `matched-hostname` is the hostname of the brand returned, which is `*` when a hostname-wide brand matched. — [GET /resellers/{reseller}/brands/{hostname}/active]

7117e9756fb45f4c.description: Read agent status — Returns an agent\'s current call center status, one value across every queue they are on, so a client can restore its status control after a reload.  Call Center Agent, Basic User, Advanced User, and Simple User read only their own status: use `~` as the agent. Site Manager reads agents who are users at its own site. Call Center Supervisor, Office Manager, Route Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only read any agent in the domain (Reseller within its territory).  Three fields describe the status, because three names exist for one state: `callqueue-agent-status` is what the agent log stores (`Auto`), `callqueue-agent-status-action` is the action path to call to return to it (`login`), and `callqueue-agent-status-label` is what the portal shows (`Online`). Match your control on `-action` and show `-label`. User and agent reads also carry the stored value as `callqueue-agent-state`, but only an action on every queue (`all`) sets it. This read takes the agent\'s latest logged action, including a login or logout on one queue, and adds the action, label, and time. The user\'s `status-message` only carries an offline reason.  An agent who has never logged a status and is on no queue returns `404`, as does an agent id that names another domain or a device address nobody owns. — [GET /domains/{domain}/agents/{callqueue-agent-id}/status]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

11a25c2f0596630d.description: Set agent offline — Takes an agent offline on one call queue, or on every queue with `all`, without ending their shift: availability becomes `manual` and no calls are dispatched until they log in again. The agent log records `Manual`, shown as Offline.  Call Center Agent, Basic User, Advanced User, and Simple User act only on their own agent entries: use `~` as the agent. Site Manager acts on agents who are users at its own site; on a named queue, the queue must be at its site too. Call Center Supervisor, Office Manager, Route Manager, Reseller, and Super User act on any agent in the domain. Office Manager Read-Only and Super User Read Only get `403`.  `202` means the change was published over the service bus (SBUS), not yet applied. The action is also written to the agent log, which `GET /domains/{domain}/agents/{callqueue-agent-id}/status` reads back. `PUT` on this path does the same as `PATCH`; other methods return `405`. The request has no body. To give a reason such as Break or Lunch, use `PATCH /domains/{domain}/callqueues/all/agents/{callqueue-agent-id}/{status}` instead. — [PATCH /domains/{domain}/callqueues/{callqueue}/agents/{callqueue-agent-id}/manual]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

a message was left. | | Wrong Number | both | no | negative | The caller or number reached the wrong business. | | Not Interested | outbound | no | negative | The contact declined the offer or conversation. | | Abandoned in Queue | inbound | yes | negative | The caller hung up before an agent answered. | | No Answer | both | yes | negative | The call rang out with nobody picking up. | | Line Busy | outbound | yes | negative | The number was busy. | | Call Failed | both | yes | negative | The call could not be connected (network or number error). |  **Call reasons** (all `system-applied` `no`, `classification` `none`) | name | direction | description | |---|---|---| | Sales Inquiry | inbound | A prospect asking about products, pricing or availability. | | Sales Outreach | outbound | Calling a prospect or customer to sell or upsell. | | Order Status | both | Checking where an order, shipment or delivery is. | | Billing or Payment | both | Invoices, charges, refunds or taking a payment. | | Technical Support | both | Help with a product or service that isn\'t working as expected. | | Appointment or Scheduling | both | Booking, moving or cancelling an appointment. | | Complaint | inbound | The customer is unhappy and wants it put right. | | General Information | inbound | Hours, locations, policies and other general questions. | | Collections | outbound | Following up on an overdue balance. | | Survey or Feedback | outbound | Asking the customer about their experience. | — [POST /domains/{domain}/callcenter-codes/seed]

Send the `revision` you read to make sure you are not overwriting someone else\'s change: if the report has changed since, the request is refused with `409`. 4ae3ca0bb9b42a11.description: List abandoned calls — Returns one row per abandoned call queue call in the domain over a time window, with the caller, the queue, and the timings. Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Site Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Reseller reads the domains in its territory.  A call counts as abandoned when the caller hung up in the queue, or the call left the queue unanswered by a transfer, a retrieve, or no answer. Calls that went to voicemail are not counted. Calls count when they entered the queue between `datetime-start` and `datetime-end`, both included. Rows are ordered by the hour the call entered the queue. `queue_list` limits the queues.  The response is not paged and every row is returned, so keep the window short. — [GET /domains/{domain}/callqueuereport/abandoned]

datetime-end.description: The end of the time window, RFC 3339 with an offset, for example `2026-09-02T00:00:00-07:00`. It must be later than `datetime-start`. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (read as UTC) and `YYYY-MM-DD` (end of that day, UTC) are also accepted.

datetime-start.description: The start of the time window, RFC 3339 with an offset, for example `2026-09-01T00:00:00-07:00`. The window includes this moment. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (read as UTC) and `YYYY-MM-DD` (start of that day, UTC) are also accepted.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

queue_list.description: A comma-separated list of call queue extensions. Returns only calls to these queues. Left out, every queue your user may view in the domain is used.

range_interval.description: Shifts both ends of the window by a relative amount, for example `-5 hour`. Kept for older integrations: give the offset in `datetime-start` and `datetime-end` instead.

synchronous.description: `yes` waits up to 2 seconds for the park to be created and answers `200` with it. 9e84bdc2579bab83.description: Get cradle to grave by CDR ID — Summarizes one call\'s progress from start to finish, step by step: the call, each ring, answer, transfer, and release. The call IDs, window, and server come from the CDR, so you send only its ID.  Super User and Super User Read Only see every trace. A Reseller sees calls that have a party domain (originating, terminating, or `by`) in its territory. Office Manager and the other domain-tier scopes see calls that have their own domain as a party domain. User-tier scopes see only calls where their own user is the originating or terminating party. A call outside your scope answers the same `404` as a call that does not exist. A scope without the call-trace privilege gets `403`; by default Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only hold it. The CDR must also name `{domain}` as a party domain, or the answer is `404`.  Steps outside your scope are removed: a Reseller keeps the steps whose domain is in its territory, and the other scopes below Super User keep the steps of their own domain. Super User and Super User Read Only see every step.  This is `GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/sipflow?type=cradle_to_grave`. The route fixes `type`, so a `type` you send is ignored. Push-notification events are not call progress, so they do not appear. — [GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/cradle2grave]

date.description: Month the call was made in, as `YYYYMM` or any date, to pick which monthly CDR table to search first. Without it, the current and previous months are searched.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

id.description: ID of the call's CDR, as `id` in `GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs`. Letters and digits only.

show_attendees.description: `yes` to follow a conference bridge and include every attendee's legs. Defaults to the platform setting, `no` unless changed. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

9e84bdc2579bab83.title: Get Cradle2grave ID

ca22c9faed811215.description: Get call trace by CDR ID — Builds the trace of one call from its CDR and returns it in the rendering you pick with `type`. The call IDs, time window, and server come from the CDR, so you send only its ID. The default rendering is `call_trace_details`, structured JSON for your own viewer, with no `event` envelope.  Super User and Super User Read Only see every trace. A Reseller sees calls that have a party domain (originating, terminating, or `by`) in its territory. Office Manager and the other domain-tier scopes see calls that have their own domain as a party domain. User-tier scopes see only calls where their own user is the originating or terminating party. A call outside your scope answers the same `404` as a call that does not exist. A scope without the call-trace privilege gets `403`; by default Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only hold it. The CDR must also name `{domain}` as a party domain, or the answer is `404`.  The CDR is looked up in the current and previous months\' tables unless you send `date`. The trace follows transfers, forks, and bridges. A trace holds both parties\' numbers and the raw SIP messages, so treat it as call metadata. In `cradle_to_grave`, steps outside your scope are removed.  The documented response is JSON. The other renderings answer a file of their own media type:  - `type=csv&download=yes`: a CSV file (`text/csv`) - `type=call_trace&download=yes`: the SVG diagram (`image/svg+xml`) - `type=call_trace_html`: an HTML viewer page (`text/html`); add `download=yes` for `sip_flow_<id>.html` - `type=call_trace_text`: plain text (`text/plain`)  In `call_trace_text`, each block header shows its time as `YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS` in UTC, and `csv` rows show the same form, with the millisecond Unix time in `UnixTsm`.  `GET /domains/{domain}/sipflow/{id}` is the same call. To share the trace with someone who has no token, use `POST /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/sipflow/store`. For the call-progress summary alone, use `GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/cradle2grave`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/sipflow]

date.description: Month the call was made in, as `YYYYMM` or any date, to pick which monthly CDR table to search first. The neighbouring months are searched too. Without it, the current and previous months are searched, so send it for an older call.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

download.description: `yes` to receive the rendering as a file attachment. An HTML download is named `sip_flow_<id>.html`. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

id.description: ID of the call's CDR, as `id` in `GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs`. Letters and digits only.

show_attendees.description: `yes` to follow a conference bridge and include every attendee's legs. Defaults to the platform setting, `no` unless changed. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

type.description: Rendering to return. Defaults to `call_trace_details`. - `call_trace_details`: devices and messages as JSON - `call_trace`: the ladder diagram as a base64 SVG in `svg` - `call_trace_html`: a self-contained HTML viewer (`text/html`) - `call_trace_text`: the raw SIP messages and log lines (`text/plain`) - `cradle_to_grave`: the call-progress summary in `cradle` - `csv`: the event rows, encoded in `csv`, or a `text/csv` file with `download=yes`. Allowed values: "call_trace", "call_trace_details", "call_trace_html", "call_trace_text", "cradle_to_grave", "csv". Default: "call_trace_details"

ca22c9faed811215.title: Get SIP Flow ID

f97a3d3ab7ee7027.description: Share call trace by CDR ID — Stores a copy of one call\'s trace and returns a key that opens it without a token, for passing to support or pasting into a ticket. The call is taken from its CDR ID, the same way as for the by-CDR read.  Requires the `create` privilege on call traces: by default Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User. Super User Read Only and scopes without the privilege get `403`. You can share only a call in your scope: Super User any call, a Reseller calls with a party domain in its territory, a domain-tier scope calls with its own domain as a party domain, and a user-tier scope calls where its user is the originating or terminating party. A call outside your scope answers the same `404` as one that does not exist. The CDR must also name `{domain}` as a party domain.  Every share expires: after `ttl` seconds, capped at `NsTraceShareMaxTtl` (30 days by default), or after `NsTraceShareTempTtl` (15 minutes by default) when you send no `ttl`. The answer gives the moment it stops working twice: `expires` as a Unix time and `expires-datetime` as RFC 3339. Revoke a share early with `DELETE /sipflow/share/{k}`. Until then, anyone with the key can read the whole trace, read-only, including other parties\' numbers and the raw SIP messages. Open it with `GET /sipflow?k=<key>` in any rendering, or `GET /sipflow/download/<key>.txt` for plain text.  The copy is stored on the server you call, named in `store-location`, before the answer is sent: `200` means the link works now. Only `POST` is served on this path; any other method gets `405`. `POST /domains/{domain}/sipflow/{id}/store` is the same call. — [POST /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/sipflow/store]

date.description: Month the call was made in, as `YYYYMM`, to pick which monthly CDR table to search first.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

id.description: ID of the call's CDR, as `id` in `GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs`. Letters and digits only.

temp.description: Accepted for older clients. `true` means the same as sending no `ttl`. Allowed values: "true", "false"

ttl.description: Lifetime of the share, in seconds. Without it, the share lives for `NsTraceShareTempTtl`, 900 seconds (15 minutes) by default. A value above `NsTraceShareMaxTtl`, 30 days by default, is lowered to it. A value that is not a positive number is ignored.

f97a3d3ab7ee7027.title: Create CDR Call Trace Share

896fc25ef4cf78af.description: Revoke call trace share in domain — Revokes a call trace share, so its key stops working at once, before it would expire. Use it when a share link went somewhere it should not.  Requires the `delete` privilege on call traces: by default Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User. Super User Read Only and scopes without the privilege get `403`. A share key never authorizes a revoke; you always need a token. Below Super User, the shared call must name `{domain}` as a party domain and be in your scope: Super User any call, a Reseller calls with a party domain in its territory, a domain-tier scope calls with its own domain as a party domain, and a user-tier scope calls where its user is a party. A key that does not exist, has expired, or is for a call outside your scope answers the same `404`.  The share is removed at once from the server you call: call the server named in the share\'s `store-location`. `200` means the share is gone. Only `DELETE` is served on this path; any other method gets `405`.  `DELETE /sipflow/share/{k}` is the same call without the domain. — [DELETE /domains/{domain}/sipflow/share/{k}]

99ad41c17fb82df4.description: Share call trace — Stores a copy of one call\'s trace and returns a key that opens it without a token. The call is taken from its CDR ID.  Requires the `create` privilege on call traces: by default Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User. Super User Read Only and scopes without the privilege get `403`. You can share only a call in your scope: Super User any call, a Reseller calls with a party domain in its territory, a domain-tier scope calls with its own domain as a party domain, and a user-tier scope calls where its user is the originating or terminating party. A call outside your scope answers the same `404` as one that does not exist. The CDR must also name `{domain}` as a party domain.  Every share expires: after `ttl` seconds, capped at `NsTraceShareMaxTtl` (30 days by default), or after `NsTraceShareTempTtl` (15 minutes by default) when you send no `ttl`. The answer gives the moment it stops working twice: `expires` as a Unix time and `expires-datetime` as RFC 3339. Revoke a share early with `DELETE /sipflow/share/{k}`. Until then, anyone with the key can read the whole trace, read-only, including other parties\' numbers and the raw SIP messages. Open it with `GET /sipflow?k=<key>` in any rendering, or `GET /sipflow/download/<key>.txt` for plain text.  The copy is stored on the server you call, named in `store-location`, before the answer is sent: `200` means the link works now. Only `POST` is served on this path; any other method gets `405`. It is the same call as `POST /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/sipflow/store`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/sipflow/{id}/store]

ttl.description: Lifetime of the share, in seconds. Without it, the share lives for `NsTraceShareTempTtl`, 900 seconds (15 minutes) by default. A value above `NsTraceShareMaxTtl`, 30 days by default, is lowered to it. A value that is not a positive number is ignored.

bc51cbe8c5024c48.description: Inject event into call trace — Writes one event row into a call\'s trace, so another application can place what it knows about the call in the same timeline as the SIP messages: an IVR choice, a media decision, or a push notification. The event appears in every rendering of the trace except `cradle_to_grave`.  Requires Super User scope. Super User Read Only gets `403`, because this is a write.  The row is written right away to the event log of the server you call; it is not published to the cluster. `201` means it is stored. A trace is read from the event logs of the servers its CDR names, so call the server that handled the call, or the event does not show. The day\'s event table is created by the SIP server, never by the API: an `event_time` whose day has no table returns `409`. A trace that has already been built is cached and does not show a new event until the cache expires, so write events before the trace is first viewed.  Stamp `event_time` when the event happens, not when you send it, as RFC 3339 with an offset (converted to UTC) or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC, and include milliseconds. The trace sorts on that time, so a delivery delay cannot move the event. The answer\'s `event-time` is RFC 3339 in UTC, to the second; the milliseconds are in `event-ts`. — [POST /sipflow/event]

event_text.description: Body of the event, rendered as written with line breaks kept. At most 60,000 bytes. A longer value is refused, never shortened.

event_time.description: When the event happened. Send RFC 3339 with an offset, which is converted to UTC, or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, read as UTC. Defaults to now. Include milliseconds so the event sorts into place. An impossible date, such as `2026-02-30`, returns `400`. It also picks the day's event table.

event_ts.description: Sort key, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Defaults to `event_time`. Send `event_time` instead: a backdated `event_ts` with the default `event_time` can fall outside the trace window, and then the event does not show.

event_type.description: Label for the event, such as `app`, `ivr`, `media`, or `push`. `push` rows are drawn on a push-notification lifeline. No control characters.

hostname.description: Hostname stamped on the event. Defaults to the hostname of the server you call. It also picks the `<hostname>_event_YYYYMMDD` table when there is no plain `event_YYYYMMDD` table. It never sends the event to another server.

orig_callid.description: SIP call ID of the call the event belongs to. No control characters.

servedCallId.description: Second call ID to file the event under. Defaults to `orig_callid`. The trace finds the event under either one.

81a9644b107f8317.description: Search raw call trace events — Searches the raw event rows that call traces are built from. Where the other trace endpoints render one call, this one returns matching rows as they were logged: by call ID, by text inside the event (a SIP header, a number, an IP address), by event type, or by time alone.  Each core server keeps only its own events. By default every core server is searched at the same time and the rows are merged into one list, newest first. Set `hostname` to search one core server. Each row\'s `server` says which server it came from.  Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope. The rows are raw SIP messages from every domain.  The search is limited so it cannot overload the event database:  - **Window**: at most 6 hours. With no `datetime-start` or `datetime-end`, it covers the 30 minutes before the request. A longer window returns `400`; it is never shortened for you. - **Query time**: each server stops its search after 10 seconds. - **Request time**: the whole request, including collecting rows from every server, stops after 15 seconds. A server that has not connected within 2 seconds, or answered within 15, is left out. - **Rows**: `limit`, 1000 by default and 10000 at most, across all servers. When there are more matches, `X-NS-Result-Truncated` is `true`.  When some servers do not answer, you still get `200` with the rows from the ones that did, and `X-NS-Fanout-Missing` names the ones left out. When none answer, you get `504` if they all ran out of time, otherwise `502`. — [GET /sipflow/events]

callid.description: Call IDs to match, comma-separated, up to 50. A row matches when its `orig-callid` or `served-callid` is one of them.

datetime-end.description: End of the window, exclusive. Same formats as `datetime-start`. Defaults to now. Must be after `datetime-start` and no more than 6 hours later.

datetime-start.description: Start of the window, inclusive. RFC 3339 with an offset (converted to UTC), or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC. Defaults to 30 minutes before `datetime-end`.

event-type.description: Event types to match, comma-separated, up to 20.

hostname.description: Core server to search. Leave blank or set `all` to search every core server and merge the rows. Any other value must be the name of a core server in this cluster.

limit.description: Most rows to return, 1 to 10000. Defaults to 1000. Default: 100

search.description: Text to find anywhere in `event-text`, up to 255 characters. Matched as written, including `%` and `_`.

sort.description: `desc` for newest first (default) or `asc` for oldest first. Allowed values: "desc", "asc". Default: "desc"
