export_format.description: `image` for the SVG diagram (`image/svg+xml`, the default), `csv` for a CSV file of the event rows (`text/csv`), or `base64` for the raw rows in the form the cluster's servers exchange (`text/plain`). Allowed values: "image", "csv", "base64". Default: "image"

k.description: Share key. Exports the stored trace it opens, with no token needed, read-only; the search fields are then ignored.

margin.description: Seconds added before `start_time` and after `end_time` when reading events. Default: 10

search_callids.description: `no` to trace only the call IDs you sent, without following related calls. `false` and `0` also turn it off. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "yes"

servers.description: Comma-separated hostnames of cluster servers to read, used with `search_callids=no`.

show_attendees.description: `yes` to follow a conference bridge and include every attendee's legs. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

start_time.description: Start of the window to search, RFC 3339. A legacy `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` value is also accepted. Required unless `k` is sent.

47f05e7b29bea526.title: Export Call Trace

9ed20382d0939e26.description: Revoke call trace share — Revokes a call trace share, so its key stops working at once, before it would expire. Use it when a share link went somewhere it should not.  Requires the `delete` privilege on call traces: by default Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User. Super User Read Only and scopes without the privilege get `403`. A share key never authorizes a revoke; you always need a token. The shared call must be in your scope: Super User any call, a Reseller calls with a party domain in its territory, a domain-tier scope calls with its own domain as a party domain, and a user-tier scope calls where its user is a party. A key that does not exist, has expired, or is for a call outside your scope answers the same `404`.  The share is removed at once from the server you call: call the server named in the share\'s `store-location`. `200` means the share is gone. Only `DELETE` is served on this path; any other method gets `405`.  `DELETE /domains/{domain}/sipflow/share/{k}` is the same call, confined to one domain. — [DELETE /sipflow/share/{k}]

k.description: Share key to revoke, the `key` a share answer gave: 8 digits, then 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

9ed20382d0939e26.title: Delete Call Trace Share

73699323e3098f39.description: Share call trace without domain — Stores a copy of one call\'s trace and returns a key that opens it without a token. The call is taken from its CDR ID. The path names no domain, so the call only has to be in your scope.  Requires the `create` privilege on call traces: by default Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User. Super User Read Only and scopes without the privilege get `403`. You can share only a call in your scope: Super User any call, a Reseller calls with a party domain in its territory, a domain-tier scope calls with its own domain as a party domain, and a user-tier scope calls where its user is the originating or terminating party. A call outside your scope answers the same `404` as one that does not exist.  Every share expires: after `ttl` seconds, capped at `NsTraceShareMaxTtl` (30 days by default), or after `NsTraceShareTempTtl` (15 minutes by default) when you send no `ttl`. The answer gives the moment it stops working twice: `expires` as a Unix time and `expires-datetime` as RFC 3339. Revoke a share early with `DELETE /sipflow/share/{k}`. Until then, anyone with the key can read the whole trace, read-only, including other parties\' numbers and the raw SIP messages. Open it with `GET /sipflow?k=<key>` in any rendering, or `GET /sipflow/download/<key>.txt` for plain text.  The copy is stored on the server you call, named in `store-location`, before the answer is sent: `200` means the link works now. Only `POST` is served on this path; any other method gets `405`. Prefer `POST /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/sipflow/store`, which names the domain. — [POST /sipflow/{id}/store]

date.description: Month the call was made in, as `YYYYMM`, to pick which monthly CDR table to search first.

id.description: ID of the call's CDR, as `id` in `GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs`. Letters and digits only.

temp.description: Accepted for older clients. `true` means the same as sending no `ttl`. Allowed values: "true", "false"

ttl.description: Lifetime of the share, in seconds. Without it, the share lives for `NsTraceShareTempTtl`, 900 seconds (15 minutes) by default. A value above `NsTraceShareMaxTtl`, 30 days by default, is lowered to it. A value that is not a positive number is ignored.

73699323e3098f39.title: Create Call Trace Share

b891519769197ede.description: Transfer call peer — Transfers the other party on the user\'s call, the peer, to a new destination or to a free call park.  Requires Basic User scope for your own user, Office Manager scope for a user in your own domain, Site Manager scope for a user in your own site, or Reseller or Super User scope.  Send `destination` for a blind transfer. Send `valid` instead to park the peer: the first call park in the list that is a call park of the domain and holds no call is used, and the response is `200` with the call park the peer was sent to.  The user in the path must be a party on the call, on any leg; otherwise the request returns `404`. The call is looked up for about a second before `404` is returned, so a control sent right after the call starts still finds it. A call that has not reached the platform by then also returns `404`. — [PATCH /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/calls/{callid}/transferPeer]

callid.description: Call ID of any leg of the call: the value of `call-orig-call-id`, `call-term-call-id`, or `call-through-call-id` on an active call, or the `call-id` you sent when you started it.

destination.description: Transfer destination: an extension, a number, or a SIP URI, such as `sip:1002@example.com`. `PLUS` in the value is sent as `+`.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

prefix.description: Text put before the chosen park name to form the transfer destination. Used only with `valid`.

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

valid.description: Comma-separated list of call park names to choose from, such as `701,702`. Used when `destination` is not sent.

b891519769197ede.title: Patch Domain User Call Transfer Peer

7c80eedd692cc874.description: Report concurrent calls — Returns the number of calls in progress over a time window, in buckets of one minute to one day, broken down by `group_by`.  Requires Super User, Super User Read Only, or Reseller scope. A Super User sees the whole platform. A Reseller sees only its own territory: its domains, sites, groups, and connections, and only a `domain` in its territory. `group_by=hostname` is for Super User scopes only.  Only `POST` is accepted; `GET` returns `405`.  Minute buckets cover only the last 3.5 hours and hourly buckets the last 15 days. A window outside that returns `400`; use a larger `report_by`. For a simple series for one domain or reseller, use **List active call history for domain** or **List active call history**. — [POST /calls/report]

domain.description: Domain to report on. Required with `group_by` `huntgroup` or `callswaiting`. A domain that does not exist, or for a Reseller one outside its territory, returns `403`.

end_date.description: End of the report window, in the same form as `start_date`.

group_by.description: What to break the report down by. `huntgroup` and `callswaiting` report the call queues of `domain` and need it. `hostname` breaks it down by core server and is for Super User scopes only. Any other value returns `400`. Allowed values: "domain", "reseller", "hostname", "group", "site", "connection", "huntgroup", "callswaiting"

report_by.description: Bucket size: one minute, ten minutes, one hour, or one day. Minute data is kept for about 3.5 hours and hourly data for 15 days. Any other value returns `400`. Allowed values: "min", "tens", "hour", "day". Default: "day"

start_date.description: Start of the report window, such as `2026-09-01 00:00:00`. Any date and time PHP can parse is accepted. Must be before `end_date`.

type.description: Which calls to count: calls between users on the platform, calls to or from outside it, or both. Any other value returns `400`. Allowed values: "onnet", "offnet", "all". Default: "onnet"

value_offset.description: For `huntgroup` and `callswaiting`, hours to subtract from each bucket time, such as `5 HOUR`. Ignored with `report_by=day`.

7c80eedd692cc874.title: Post Calls Report

2e1739505f13094f.description: List active call history — Returns how many calls were in progress over a recent window, for your territory or the whole platform, as a series of buckets ending now.  Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope. A Reseller always gets its own territory, and `reseller` and `domain` are ignored. A Super User gets the whole platform, or one reseller with `reseller`, or one domain with `domain`.  The platform-wide series counts all calls and ignores `type`. Only `GET` is accepted. — [GET /calls/active-history]

domain.description: Super User only. Domain to report on, such as `example.com`. Takes precedence over `reseller`. Ignored for a Reseller token.

period.description: Bucket size. Defaults to `minute` for `1h` and `3h`, `hour` up to `7d`, and `day` for `28d`. Minute buckets are kept for about 3.5 hours and hourly buckets for 15 days: a size that does not cover `range` returns `400`. Allowed values: "minute", "hour", "day"

range.description: Window to cover, ending now. Defaults to `24h`. Allowed values: "1h", "3h", "6h", "12h", "24h", "2d", "7d", "28d". Default: "24h"

reseller.description: Super User only. Reseller to report on, such as `example-reseller`. Ignored for a Reseller token.

type.description: Which calls to count: calls between users on the platform (`onnet`), calls to or from outside it (`offnet`), or both. Defaults to `all`. Ignored for the platform-wide series. Allowed values: "onnet", "offnet", "all". Default: "all"

2e1739505f13094f.title: List Calls Active History

745ecc7344b4db83.description: Run call action — Runs a call control action, named in the path, on one of the user\'s calls in progress. `PATCH` on the same path does the same.  Requires Basic User scope for your own user, Office Manager scope for a user in your own domain, Site Manager scope for a user in your own site, or Reseller or Super User scope.  The actions:  - `answer`: answer a ringing call on the device in `call-term-user` - `hold` and `unhold`: hold or resume the other party - `transfer` (or `xfer`): blind transfer to `call-term-user`, or attended with `hostname` and `call-destination-session-id` - `transferPeer`: transfer the other party to `call-term-user`, or park it with `valid` - `recording`: set call recording to `state` - `reject` and `disconnect`: turn away a ringing call, or end the call  Each action also has its own page with its fields. Any other action returns `400`. `GET` on this path returns `405`, and `DELETE` is accepted only for `reject` and `disconnect`.  The user in the path must be a party on the call, on any leg; otherwise the request returns `404`. The call is looked up for about a second before `404` is returned, so a control sent right after the call starts still finds it. A call that has not reached the platform by then also returns `404`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/calls/{callid}/{action}]

action.description: Call control action to run. Allowed values: "answer", "hold", "unhold", "transfer", "xfer", "transferPeer", "recording", "reject", "disconnect"

call-destination-session-id.description: For an attended `transfer`, the `call-session-id` of the call to merge in. Send it with `hostname`.

call-term-user.description: For `answer`, the device that answers, such as `sip:1001wp@example.com`. For `transfer`, `xfer`, and `transferPeer`, the transfer destination. Required for `answer`.

callid.description: Call ID of any leg of the call: the value of `call-orig-call-id`, `call-term-call-id`, or `call-through-call-id` on an active call, or the `call-id` you sent when you started it.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

hostname.description: For an attended `transfer`, the core server that holds the call to merge in, from its `core-server`. Send it with `call-destination-session-id`.

prefix.description: For `park` and `transferPeer` with `valid`, text put before the chosen park name to form the destination.

state.description: For `recording`, the recording state to set. Required for `recording`. Allowed values: "on", "off", "pause", "resume"

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

valid.description: For `park` and `transferPeer`, a comma-separated list of call park names to choose from. The first free one is used.

745ecc7344b4db83.title: Perform Call Action For User

f08541d78a5482dd.description: Update CDR — Sets the disposition fields on one call detail record (CDR): `notes`, `disposition`, `reason`, `pac`, and `time_disp`. Requires Reseller or Super User scope, and a Reseller updates only calls in its territory.  The path\'s `{callid}` picks the record. The record must be from this month or last month, and within your scope. Send only the fields to change; the other fields of the record are never written. `call-disposition-submitted-datetime` takes RFC 3339 or Unix seconds and is stored as Unix seconds. The v1 names (`notes`, `disposition`, `reason`, `pac`, `time_disp`) are accepted as the same fields.  A `202` means the change was published over the service bus (SBUS), not that it is applied: read the record back to see it. A body with none of the five fields returns `400`, and so does a body `call-parent-cdr-id` that differs from the path. A record that is not found, or not within your scope, returns `404`. — [PUT /cdrs/{callid}]

call-disposition.description: Disposition to set, such as a wrap-up code

call-disposition-notes.description: Notes to record with the disposition. Stored as text with no practical length limit.

call-disposition-reason.description: Reason to record with the disposition

call-disposition-submitted-datetime.description: When the disposition was submitted. RFC 3339, or Unix seconds. Stored as Unix seconds.

call-parent-cdr-id.description: Id of the record. Optional: the path names it, and a different value returns `400`.

callid.description: Id of the call record to change: its `call-parent-cdr-id`. Despite the name, this is not a SIP Call-ID. A `call-parent-cdr-id` in the body is optional, and one that differs from the path returns `400`.

f08541d78a5482dd.title: Update Cdrrecord

0dfc83c5f45fb9bb.description: Read call quality — Returns the audio quality of each leg of one call: MOS, jitter, and packet loss in both directions, with links to the quality monitor that captured it. Requires Super User, Super User Read Only, Super User CDR, or Reseller scope, and a Reseller reads only calls that involve a domain in its territory. A call outside your scope, or one that does not exist, returns `404`, so an id cannot be used as an existence probe. Other scopes get `403`; use `GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/quality`.  `{id}` is the call\'s `call-parent-cdr-id`. By default this month and last month are searched; for an older call, send `date`, which also searches the months either side. `side` returns one leg.  Each entry has both audio directions of its leg. `call-quality-direction-a` is audio from `call-quality-caller` to `call-quality-called`, and `call-quality-direction-b` is the reverse. `voipmonitor-url` opens the capture on the monitor that recorded it, and `voipmonitor-search-url` searches that monitor by SIP Call-ID; both need a monitor login.  An empty array means the call exists but has no quality data: it predates quality scanning, scanning is off on this cluster, or the call ended less than about 30 seconds ago. A metric that was not measured is left out rather than reported as `0`, and the `rtcp-*` metrics are left out until RTCP capture is on. The summary MOS of each leg is also on the CDR as `call-audio-quality-orig-mos` and `call-audio-quality-term-mos`. — [GET /cdrs/{id}/quality]

date.description: Month to search first, as `YYYYMM`, such as `202609`, or a date in that month, such as `2026-09-01`. The months before and after are searched too, because the monthly tables are split by UTC month. A value that cannot be read returns `400`.

id.description: Id of the call record: its `call-parent-cdr-id`, from a CDR read. Letters, digits, `-`, and `_`.

side.description: Return one leg only: `orig` or `term`. Omitted or empty returns both. Any other value returns `400`. Allowed values: "orig", "term"

0dfc83c5f45fb9bb.title: Read CDR Call Quality

The v1 names (`notes`, `disposition`, `reason`, `pac`, `time_disp`) are accepted as the same fields.  A `202` means the change was published over the service bus (SBUS), not that it is applied: read the record back to see it. A body with none of the five fields returns `400`, and so does a body `call-parent-cdr-id` that differs from the path. A record that is not found, or not within your scope, returns `404`. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{callid}]

call-disposition-notes.description: Notes to record with the disposition. Stored as text with no practical length limit.

call-disposition-reason.description: Reason to record with the disposition

call-disposition-submitted-datetime.description: When the disposition was submitted. RFC 3339, or Unix seconds. Stored as Unix seconds.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

36f4706c6b8d939a.description: Count domain CDR schedules — Returns how many CDR export schedules are filed under one domain, counted the same way `GET /domains/{domain}/schedule` selects them. The same scopes can call it: Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only count the whole domain, and every other scope counts only its own schedules.  Narrow the count with `schedule-name` or `user`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/schedule/count]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

user.description: Only schedules scoped to this extension. For a scope limited to its own schedules, your own extension always applies.

36f4706c6b8d939a.title: Get Domains Domain Schedule Count

93298a13853b1daa.description: Count reseller CDR schedules — Returns how many CDR export schedules belong to one territory, counted the same way the reseller list selects them. Requires Reseller scope for your own territory, Super User, or Super User Read Only.  A reseller read returns schedules whose `reseller` is this territory, plus older schedules stored with `reseller` `*` whose domain the territory owns. A platform-wide schedule, with both `reseller` and `domain` set to `*`, is never included. — [GET /resellers/{reseller}/schedule/count]

reseller.description: Reseller (territory) name, such as `example-reseller`. `~` means your own territory.

93298a13853b1daa.title: Get Resellers Reseller Schedule Count

5e694c9909d1929c.description: Count domain CDR schedules by name — Returns `1` when the domain has a schedule with this name that you can see, and `0` when it does not. Use it to test for a schedule without reading its fields. Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only see every schedule in the domain. Every other scope sees only its own. — [GET /domains/{domain}/schedule/{schedule_name}/count]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

schedule_name.description: Schedule name. Names are unique across the whole platform, not per domain.

5e694c9909d1929c.title: Get Domains Domain Schedule Schedule Name Count

569fc90e76904ca7.description: List domain CDR schedule names — Returns only the name and owner fields of a domain\'s CDR schedules: `schedule-name`, `domain`, `user`, `schedule-user-export-scope`, and `reseller`. Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only see every schedule in the domain. Site Manager and every other scope see only their own schedules.  There is no default page size: without `limit`, every matching schedule is returned. Read a full schedule with `GET /domains/{domain}/schedule/{schedule_name}`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/schedule/list]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

limit.description: Most schedules to return. With no `limit`, `/list` returns every matching schedule. Default: 100

sort.description: Sort order: one or more comma-separated field names, each optionally followed by `ASC` or `DESC`. Takes the v2 name (`schedule-next-run-datetime`) or the column name (`next_run_time`). Defaults to `schedule-name` ascending. An unknown field, or `export-password`, returns `400`. Default: "schedule_name ASC"

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

user.description: Only schedules scoped to this extension. For a scope limited to its own schedules, your own extension always applies.

569fc90e76904ca7.title: List Cdrschedules List

a28a46cf8055ebd2.description: List domain CDR schedules — Returns the CDR export schedules filed under one domain, with every stored field. Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only see every schedule in the domain, and a Reseller only in its own territory. Every other scope, including Basic User, Call Center Agent, and Site Manager, sees only its own schedules, and only through its own domain: another domain, a reseller path, or `/schedule` returns `403`.  Filter with `schedule-name` or `user`. Page with `start` and `limit`, 100 schedules by default. Use `GET /domains/{domain}/schedule/count` for a total and `GET /domains/{domain}/schedule/list` for the names and owners only.  `export-password` is masked. Super User can send `include-secrets=yes` for the plain text. — [GET /domains/{domain}/schedule]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

include-secrets.description: `yes` returns `export-password` in plain text instead of masked. Super User only, and every use is audit-logged. Any other scope gets `403`. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page. Default: 100

schedule_name.description: Only the schedule with this name. `schedule-name` is accepted too.

sort.description: Sort order: one or more comma-separated field names, each optionally followed by `ASC` or `DESC`. Takes the v2 name (`schedule-next-run-datetime`) or the column name (`next_run_time`). Defaults to `schedule-name` ascending. An unknown field, or `export-password`, returns `400`. Default: "schedule_name ASC"

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

84021d31a48565ec.description: Create domain CDR schedule — Creates a CDR export schedule for one domain. At each `schedule-next-run-datetime`, the CDR export service collects the calls that ended between `schedule-last-run-datetime` and `schedule-next-run-datetime`, keeps the directions the `export-*-calls-enabled` flags select, writes a CSV, and delivers it by `export-method`. It then moves both times forward by `schedule-repeat-interval`. Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Basic User, Call Center Agent, and Site Manager can create one for themselves only: the schedule is stamped with their own extension, and a `user` naming someone else returns `403`.  `schedule-preset` is required. `Daily`, `Weekly`, and `Monthly` set `data-lookup-window` and `schedule-repeat-interval` for you. `Weekly` needs `schedule-weekly-day-of-week` and `schedule-start-time`, `Monthly` needs `schedule-monthly-day-of-month`, and `Custom` needs `time-zone` and `data-lookup-window`. Send `schedule-next-run-datetime` in RFC 3339 (`2026-09-02T09:00:00-04:00`) or as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in `time-zone`. It is stored in UTC, and leaving it out means now. With `Daily`, `Weekly`, or `Monthly`, only its date is used: the time comes from `schedule-start-time`, or is midnight for `Monthly`. The owning reseller is filled in from the domain when you leave `reseller` out. A `reseller` that does not own the domain returns `400`. `schedule-user-export-scope` is set from your scope and cannot be sent.  The schedule was published over the service bus (SBUS) and is created when each server applies it. The body is `{"code": 202}`. Read the schedule back to confirm it.  A name already used anywhere on the platform returns `409`. A missing or invalid field returns `400` naming it, including an unknown `time-zone`, an unparseable date, a bad `schedule-start-time`, a name that breaks the pattern, `export-method` `scp copy`, and a masked-looking `export-password`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/schedule]

7e2a075ff993db03.description: List CDR schedule exports — Lists the files a CDR schedule has produced, newest first. Each run of the schedule makes one export, covering one export window.  Every export carries `file-access-url`, a signed link that downloads the file with no token for 60 minutes. Each read returns fresh links. To download with your token instead, call the export\'s `download` path.  Returns 100 exports unless you set `limit`; `limit=0` returns every export in the retention window. Page with `start`. Exports whose window ended more than 100 days ago are not listed. A schedule that has not run yet returns an empty array. Times are in UTC (`+00:00`). 28e53641b409eefc.description: Download CDR schedule export — Downloads the CSV file (`text/csv`) of one export of a CDR schedule.  Call it one of two ways:  - **With a token.** Send a bearer token. Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only can reach the exports of any schedule in the domain. Every other scope can reach only the exports of a schedule it owns in its own domain. A schedule you cannot see, or one that belongs to another domain, returns `404`. - **With a signed link.** Every list or read of an export returns `file-access-url`, which is the system-wide form of this path with `expires` and `signature` added. Anyone holding the link can download that one file, with no token, until it expires (60 minutes by default). Treat the link like the file itself.  The file is kept on the server that ran the export. When you call a different server, it answers `302` with a short-lived signed link to the server that holds the file; follow the redirect.  Every download is recorded in the access log. The response is never cached by a shared cache. — [GET /domains/{domain}/schedule/{schedule_name}/exports/{export_id}/download]

schedule_name.description: Schedule name. Names are unique across the whole platform, not per domain.

signature.description: The signature of a signed link, from `file-access-url`. With it the call needs no token, and it downloads only the export the path names until `expires`. domain.description: Leave it out. On `PUT /schedule/{schedule_name}` and the reseller form it must equal the schedule's domain, or the update returns `404`. On the domain form the path sets it.

email.description: Where the export or its notification is emailed. Required in practice when `export-method` is `email`.

export-cdr-format.description: CSV layout. Defaults to `Advanced`, the short layout of 13 columns. `Standard` is the full layout. Allowed values: "Standard", "Advanced"

export-hostname.description: Host for `ftp upload` or `sftp`, with an optional `:port`. Required for those methods.

export-inbound-calls-enabled.description: Whether inbound calls are exported. Defaults to `No`. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-include-headers-enabled.description: Whether the CSV starts with a header row. Defaults to `No`. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-last-sequence-number.description: Stored for older clients. The export service does not use it.

export-method.description: How the file is delivered. `email` attaches it (9 MB or smaller; larger files get a download link), `ftp upload` and `sftp` upload it, `backup locally` keeps it on the server that ran it, and `do nothing` delivers nothing. `scp copy` returns `400`. Allowed values: "email", "scp copy", "ftp upload", "sftp", "backup locally", "do nothing"

export-notify-email-enabled.description: Send `yes` to have `email` notified after an upload. Defaults to `no`, and is always `yes` when `export-method` is `email`.

export-offnet-calls-enabled.description: Whether off-net calls are exported. Defaults to `No`. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-outbound-calls-enabled.description: Whether outbound calls are exported. Defaults to `No`. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-password.description: Password for `ftp upload` or `sftp`. Stored in plain text and masked on read. A value that looks masked returns `400`, except the exact mask a read returned for this schedule, which keeps the stored password.

export-remote-path.description: Directory on the remote host. Defaults to empty.

export-username.description: Login for `ftp upload` or `sftp`. Required for those methods.

language-token.description: Language of the notification email, such as `en_us`. Defaults to `en_us` when empty.

post-export-script-enabled.description: Stored for older clients. The export service does not run a script. Defaults to `No`.

post-export-script-path.description: Stored for older clients. Defaults to `n/a`.

reseller.description: Leave it out. On the reseller form it must equal the path territory. An older schedule stored with `*` is given its domain's territory on update.

schedule-monthly-day-of-month.description: Day of the month, `1` to `31`. Required for `Monthly`. The API stores it without checking the range.

schedule-name.description: Ignored: the path names the schedule, and a schedule cannot be renamed.

schedule-next-run-datetime.description: New next run, in RFC 3339 or as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` read in `time-zone` (UTC when there is none). Stored in UTC. `schedule-last-run-datetime` is reset to one `data-lookup-window` earlier. An unparseable value returns `400`.

schedule-preset.description: Recurrence preset. Send one: a schedule without a preset is never run. `Daily`, `Weekly`, and `Monthly` set `data-lookup-window` and `schedule-repeat-interval` for you. `Custom` needs `time-zone`, `data-lookup-window`, and `schedule-repeat-interval`. Allowed values: "Monthly", "Weekly", "Daily", "Custom"

schedule-repeat-interval.description: Time between runs, such as `1 hour`, `1 Day`, or `1 Month`. `No Repeat` runs once. Set by the `Daily`, `Weekly`, and `Monthly` presets. Defaults to `1 day`.

schedule-run-immediately.description: Send `yes` to run the schedule now, over the window that ends now, without moving its regular times. Allowed values: 0, 1

schedule-start-time.description: Time of day as `HH:MM` in `time-zone`. Required for `Weekly`, and used by `Daily` when `time-zone` is set. A value that is not a time returns `400`.

schedule-status.description: Leave it out. Defaults to `waiting`, and the export service manages it after that.

schedule-user-export-scope.description: Read-only. Ignored if sent: the API records your scope on create and never changes it on update.

schedule-weekly-day-of-week.description: Day of the week, such as `Monday`. Required for `Weekly`.

schedule_name.description: Schedule name. Names are unique across the whole platform, not per domain.

time-zone.description: IANA time zone name, such as `America/New_York`. Required for `Custom`. An unknown name returns `400`.

user.description: Extension to limit the export to. A scope limited to its own schedules cannot name another extension: that returns `403`.

Returns 100 exports unless you set `limit`; `limit=0` returns every export in the retention window. Page with `start`. Exports whose window ended more than 100 days ago are not listed. A schedule that has not run yet returns an empty array. Times are in UTC (`+00:00`).  Requires Super User scope. 8368bc7f10156e3c.description: Download CDR schedule export (system-wide) — Downloads the CSV file (`text/csv`) of one export of a CDR schedule.  Call it one of two ways:  - **With a token.** Send a bearer token. Requires Super User scope. Every other scope, Super User Read Only included, gets `403`; use the domain or reseller path instead. - **With a signed link.** Every list or read of an export returns `file-access-url`, which is the system-wide form of this path with `expires` and `signature` added. Anyone holding the link can download that one file, with no token, until it expires (60 minutes by default). Treat the link like the file itself.  The file is kept on the server that ran the export. When you call a different server, it answers `302` with a short-lived signed link to the server that holds the file; follow the redirect.  Every download is recorded in the access log. The response is never cached by a shared cache. — [GET /schedule/{schedule_name}/exports/{export_id}/download]

expires.description: The expiry of a signed link, in Unix seconds. Copy it from `file-access-url`; never set it yourself. Leave it out when you call with a token.

schedule_name.description: Schedule name. Names are unique across the whole platform, not per domain.

signature.description: The signature of a signed link, from `file-access-url`. With it the call needs no token, and it downloads only the export the path names until `expires`. An expired link answers `403` with `Link has expired`; a changed path or expiry answers `403` with `Invalid signature`. Leave it out when you call with a token.

4b317c913f406fa1.description: Install packages on server — Installs or upgrades one or more NetSapiens packages on one server, to the newest version or to the version you name.  Requires Super User scope.  `packages` must be a non-empty list, every name in it must start with `netsapiens-`, and `version` must be a Debian package version. Anything else is refused with `400` before apt runs. A `version` applies to every package in the request and allows a downgrade. Pick versions from `all_options` in `GET /apt/installed/{hostname}`.  The response streams apt output as plain text. A failed install still answers `200`: read the last line. If another apt operation is running on the server, this one waits for it, up to 20 minutes, then answers `409`. When a package restarts the web server or the apt manager itself, that restart waits until the response has finished, so the stream is not cut off. — [POST /apt/install/{hostname}]

hostname.description: The cluster server to act on, as the hostname it is listed under in `GET /apt/servers`. A name not in that list, a malformed name, or a bare IP address is refused with `400` before anything runs. When it names a server other than the one you called, the request is forwarded there with your token.

packages.description: Packages to install. Every name must start with `netsapiens-` and use only letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `+` and `-`, or the request is refused with `400` before apt runs. Name the release channel in the package name, such as `netsapiens-api-beta`

31ef44e069c8c536.description: List installed packages across cluster — Lists the NetSapiens packages installed on every cluster server, grouped by package, with the version on each server.  Requires Super User scope.  The server you call asks every server in `GET /apt/servers` in parallel and waits up to 3 seconds for each. A server that fails or does not answer in time is left out, and the call still answers `200`. A package missing from a server can mean that server did not answer: use `GET /apt/installed/{hostname}` to ask it directly.  Each server answers from a cache that is cleared after every apt change. Set `skipcache` to `true` to make every server read apt again, which is slower. The per-server records leave out `all_options`. — [GET /apt/installed]

skipcache.description: `true` makes every server read apt again instead of answering from its cache. Any other value, or none, uses the cache. Allowed values: "true", "false"

2fe9fbb8f38b0338.description: List installed packages on server — Lists the NetSapiens packages installed on one server, with every version you could install instead.  Requires Super User scope.  The answer comes from a cache that is cleared after every apt change on that server. Set `skipcache` to `true` to read apt again, which is slower.  The list ends with one entry whose `application` is `repo`. It is not a package: its `version` is the highest repository version configured on the server, and `upgradable` says whether a newer repository version is published. Use `GET /apt/repos/{hostname}` for the details.  Use `all_options` to pick a version for `POST /apt/install/{hostname}`.  When the request is forwarded and the named server answers with an error, that server\'s status and body are passed through unchanged. — [GET /apt/installed/{hostname}]

Requires Office Manager scope for your own domain, or Reseller or Super User scope. A Basic User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, or Route Manager can create only an owned conference for their own extension.  There are two kinds of conference:  - **owned**, the default: a personal bridge for an existing user. `conference-direct-dial-number` is required, and a dial rule sends that number to the bridge. The conference\'s key becomes `conference-owner-user` - **dedicated**: a bridge with its own extension, `conference`. When the extension has no user yet, a system user with an answering rule and a dial rule is created for it  Setting `conference-leader-pin` also requires `conference-participants-pin`, and `conference-require-leader-to-start` requires a leader PIN. Send PINs and the SIP password themselves: a masked value returns `400`.  A `202` means the conference was accepted and is applied shortly after. A conference that already exists, an extension already taken by a user, or a direct-dial number already in use returns `409`. A `conference-sip-uri` or `conference-owner-user-id` in another domain returns `403`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/conferences]

8d3d249076c33496.description: Update configuration — Changes the value of an existing configuration row. The name comes from the path; name the rest of the key in the body, as the list returns it. Each key part you leave out is `*`, except that below Reseller your own domain and user fill in. A key that matches no row returns `404`; to add a row, call `POST /configurations`. `PUT` /configurations` without a name answers `405`.  Who can write:  - Super User writes any row, including system rows, for any name. - Reseller writes rows for its own territory or a domain in it. With neither `reseller` nor `domain`, the row is stored for your territory. - Office Manager and Route Manager write their own domain\'s rows. `domain` left out means your domain. - Other scopes with write rights write only their own user\'s rows in their own domain. `user` and `domain` left out mean yours. - Super User Read Only, Route Manager Reseller, Call Center Supervisor, Site Manager, and Office Manager Read-Only are read-only and get `403`.  Below Super User, the setting must have a definition whose `config-def-allow-reseller-access` is `yes`. A key outside your tier returns `403`.  For a secret-named setting, the masked value read back and sent unchanged keeps the stored value. The change is checked, then published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied on every server shortly after, so `202` means accepted, not yet stored. Send `domain`, `reseller`, and `user` in the body: in the query string they\'re ignored. — [PUT /configurations/{config-name}]

config-name.description: Name of the setting, such as `PORTAL_SHOW_SHARED_CONTACTS`. `*` returns `400` here.

config-value.description: Value of the setting. Stored and returned as a string; send flags as `yes` or `no`. Not checked against the definition's `data-type`. For a secret-named setting, the masked value read back and sent unchanged keeps the stored value; a mask sent for a new row returns `400`

domain.description: Domain the row applies to, or `*` for every domain. Default: "*"

reseller.description: Territory the row applies to, or `*` for every territory. Default: "*"

user.description: User (extension) the row applies to, or `*` for every user. Default: "*"

8169a4b47645e0d5.description: List archive policies — Lists the recording archive and retention policies (`archive_config`) from every recording server: where archived media goes, what is deleted after archiving, and how long it is held.  Requires Super User or Super User Read Only.  A policy\'s key is `acc-elm`, `case-id`, and `status` together. `status` `*` is the wildcard policy that applies whatever the recording\'s status; it is a stored value, not a pattern, so `*` matches only a row stored as `*`.  Reads fan out to every recording server like `GET /recordings/config`, one row per policy and server, each with `archive-config-server`. `local-only=yes` reads only the database the serving server is connected to. `limit` and `start` apply to each server.  `archive-config-in-sync` compares the policy fields only: `last-date-datetime` and `last-poll-datetime` record each server\'s own archive runs and never count as drift. `yes` needs every expected server to answer; compare `archive-config-servers-reporting` with `archive-config-servers-expected`. An inventory of exactly one recording server gives `yes` when that server answers. `no` means the policies differ, or some servers hold the policy and others do not. `unknown` means not every server answered, `local-only=yes` was sent, or an inventory entry is not a valid hostname.  `last-date-datetime` and `last-poll-datetime` are stored as text and returned in RFC 3339 with the `+00:00` offset; a policy that has never run returns `null`.  Every read that returns policies is recorded in the access log, naming the case IDs returned, because `case-id` names a subscriber. — [GET /recordings/archive-configs]

acc-elm.description: Returns only policies with this `acc-elm`. Exact match; `*` matches only the stored value `*`.

case-id.description: Returns only policies with this case ID. Exact match.

enabled.description: Returns only enabled (`yes`) or disabled (`no`) policies. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

limit.description: Most rows to return from each server, 1 to 100000, so a cluster of 3 servers can return up to 3 times this many. Defaults to `1000` on `/list` and `100` otherwise. Anything else returns `400` (`limit must be a whole number from 1 to 100000`). Default: 100

local-only.description: `yes` reads only the database the server that takes the request is connected to, labeled with that server's hostname, instead of every recording server. feb94db9815e8177.description: Create recording configuration entry — Creates a key in the recording configuration table (`config_config`) and publishes it to every recording server. f3e4d2c6b741f780.description: List NMS configuration entries — Lists entries of the NMS key/value configuration table (`config_config`) from every core server, one row per key and server, and says whether the servers agree on each key.  Requires Super User or Super User Read Only. `include-secrets=yes` requires Super User.  **Reads fan out to every core server by default.** `config_config` is held by each core server and kept in step over the service bus (SBUS), so the useful question is whether the servers agree. Every row carries `config-server`, and one row comes back per key and server. A server that does not answer within 3 seconds is left out. Send `local-only=yes` to read only the server that takes the request; `GET /nsconfigs` has the opposite default.  `limit` and `start` apply to each server, so a cluster of 3 servers can return up to 3 times `limit` rows. The response is grouped by key, then server. For names without values, append `/list`; for one server\'s total, append `/count`.  `config-in-sync` compares the servers in this response:  - `yes`: every expected server answered and all hold the key with the same value. Compare `config-servers-reporting` with `config-servers-expected`. A cluster whose inventory holds exactly one server gives `yes` when that server answers. - `no`: the values differ, or some servers hold the key and others do not, and the difference is visible in this response. A deliberate `config-server` override looks the same as drift. - `unknown`: agreement cannot be shown. A server did not answer, `local-only=yes` was sent, an inventory entry is not a valid hostname, the values are masked, one server masked the value and another did not, the values differ only as text (`1.10` and `1.1`), or a key is missing from a server whose page was full or started past `start=0`. - `not-expected`: the key describes the server rather than the platform and is meant to differ. `NsNmsconfigPerServer` lists these keys; by default `SystemStartTime`, `NatWanIP`, and `Send503ToAll`.  `include-secrets=yes` compares the stored values instead of masks, so masked keys get a definite answer.  **Values whose key looks like a credential are masked.** The key name is the only signal, so any key containing `password`, `secret`, `key`, `token`, `auth`, `smtp`, `license`, `cert`, or a similar keyword is masked and carries `config-value-redacted: yes`. A value of 8 characters or fewer becomes the same number of asterisks (at least 4); a longer one keeps its first 2 and last 2 characters. Two settings narrow the match:  - `NsNmsconfigMaskExempt` names keys that are never masked. By default it covers `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_UID`, `SMTP_USER`, and `SMTP_USERNAME`, so `SMTP_PWD` is the SMTP setting that stays hidden. - `NsNmsconfigMaskMinLength` (default `4`) returns shorter values in the clear, so a `yes` or `no` under a key that only matches by accident stays readable.  Each server masks its own rows with its own settings.  `config-value` is returned exactly as stored, so a leading or trailing zero survives.  To see which servers answered and how many keys each disagrees on, call `GET /nmsconfig/servers`. — [GET /nmsconfig]

Requires Super User or Super User Read Only.  The list comes from the cluster inventory (`element_domain`), not from the servers that answered, so a server that is down appears with `config-server-reachable: no` and `null` counts instead of vanishing or reading as empty. A server has 3 seconds to answer.  The counts cover the server\'s whole table, not a page. `config-server-out-of-sync-count` counts the server\'s keys whose `config-in-sync` is `no`, including keys other servers lack; keys that are `not-expected` or `unknown` are left out, so a non-zero count is always worth a look. 6ad225a73e40ff9d.description: List config file settings — Lists the settings in the API and portal config files. Config file settings are the entries in each server\'s API and portal config files: `/etc/netsapiens/api_config (PHP)` (`config-type` `api`) and `/etc/netsapiens/portal_config (PHP)` (`portal`). They override the defaults the software ships, per server, and take effect on the next request that server handles.  Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope. A request from the server itself (localhost) may read without a token. Every other scope gets `403`.  Send `include-api=true`, `include-portals=true`, or both: with neither, the list is empty. By default only the answering server\'s files are read. `local-only=false` also asks every other server, with your token, and adds their settings; each row names its server in `config-server`. A server that cannot be read is left out and named in a `Warning` response header.  Values of settings whose names contain a secret keyword (`password`, `secret`, `key`, `token`, `smtp`, and others) are masked for every scope, Super User included. Settings with a string, number, boolean, or array value are listed; one set by an expression is not. — [GET /nsconfigs]

include-portals.description: `true` reads the portal config file. Defaults to `false`. Default: false

local-only.description: `false` also reads every other server's files. Defaults to `true`. Default: true

6ad225a73e40ff9d.title: Read All Ns API Configurations

829464986357fa67.description: Create config file setting — Sets a setting in a server\'s API or portal config file, adding it when the file does not have it. Config file settings are the entries in each server\'s API and portal config files: `/etc/netsapiens/api_config (PHP)` (`config-type` `api`) and `/etc/netsapiens/portal_config (PHP)` (`portal`). They override the defaults the software ships, per server, and take effect on the next request that server handles.  Requires Super User scope, with a token. Every other scope gets `403`.  `config-name`, `config-value`, and `config-type` are required. POST and PUT do the same thing (see `PUT /nsconfigs`). `config-comment` left out keeps the existing comment.  `config-server` picks where the change goes: left out or this server\'s hostname changes this server, another cluster server\'s hostname changes only that server, and `geo` changes this server and then every other server. Any other value returns `404`. Other servers are reached from this one with your token.  The file is edited under a lock, checked, and replaced in one step. Nothing is written when the setting shares its line with other code, when the edit would drop the opening `<?php` tag or change any other setting (`409`), or when the result would not parse (`500`).  `202` means this server\'s file was written, where this server is a target. A server that could not be reached or refused the change is listed in `warnings`, and the answer is still `202`: check `warnings`, or read back with `GET /nsconfigs?local-only=false`.  `config-value-type` decides how the value is written: `string` (the default), `boolean`, `integer`, `float`, or `array`. Send `boolean` for an on/off setting, since the string `false` counts as true. A masked value from `GET /nsconfigs`, sent back unchanged, keeps the stored value; a mask sent for a new secret-named setting returns `400`. — [POST /nsconfigs]

config-comment.description: Comment written after the setting. Left out keeps the existing comment. A comment with a line break, a control character, `?>`, or `<?` returns `400`

config-name.description: Name of the setting: a PHP identifier, optionally dot-delimited, such as `NsSlowQueryThresholdMs` or `NsAllowedRedirectUris.100`. Anything else returns `400`

config-server.description: Where to apply it: `geo` for this server and every other server in the cluster, this server's own hostname, or another cluster server's hostname (only that server is changed). Left out means this server. Any other value returns `404`

config-type.description: File to change: `api` is `/etc/netsapiens/api_config (PHP)`, `portal` is `/etc/netsapiens/portal_config (PHP)`. Allowed values: "api", "portal"

config-value.description: New value. Must match `config-value-type`. A string is up to 4,096 characters with no line breaks or control characters (tab is allowed). A `boolean` takes `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. An `array` is a JSON array or object of strings, numbers, booleans, or null, nested up to 5 deep and up to 4,096 characters as JSON; it is written on one line. For a secret-named setting, the masked value read back and sent unchanged keeps the stored value

config-value-type.description: How the value is written into the file. Defaults to `string`. Send `boolean` for an on/off setting: the string `false` is true in PHP. Allowed values: "string", "boolean", "integer", "float", "array". Default: "string"

e6ec5a9fdcf0ac61.description: Read connection — Returns one connection by `connection-id`, without naming its domain. Requires Office Manager, Route Manager, Call Center Supervisor, or Office Manager Read-Only scope in the connection\'s domain, Reseller scope in its territory, or Super User or Super User Read Only scope.  An id that names no connection returns `404`, and so does a route profile\'s id; read those with `GET /routeprofiles/{connection-id}`. One in a domain your scope does not cover returns `403`. — [GET /connections/{connection-id}]

connection-id.description: The connection's `connection-id`, as a list returns it: base64url, without padding, of `connection-orig-match-pattern`. The raw `connection-orig-match-pattern` is also accepted.

e6ec5a9fdcf0ac61.title: Read Connection

621873e4f248df5e.description: Update connection — Changes a connection by `connection-id`, without naming its domain. Requires Super User or Reseller scope. A Reseller can change only a connection in its own territory; other scopes use `PUT /domains/{domain}/connections/{connection-id}`. The API publishes the change on the service bus (SBUS) `connection_events` channel, and each server applies it when the event arrives, so `202` means published, not applied.  The path identifies the connection. A `domain` or `connection-orig-match-pattern` in the body is ignored, so the key cannot be renamed. An id that names no connection, or one outside your territory, returns `404`. A route profile\'s id keeps its route-name address and its `route_profile` type: a different `connection-connectivity-type` returns `400`, and a different `connection-address` is ignored with a `Warning` header. Send only what changes. Omitted fields keep their stored values, the call-processing fields such as `connection-sip-transport-protocol` included. Changing `connection-connectivity-type` also sets `connection-sip-authenticate-as-client-enabled` and reformats `connection-address` to suit the type. An invalid `connection-connectivity-type`, `connection-require-encrypted-audio-enabled`, or `connection-sip-session-timer-enabled` returns `400`. Sending `call-routing` returns `404`: change a route profile\'s route through the route-profile endpoints. `synchronous` is ignored. — [PUT /connections/{connection-id}]

connection-id.description: The connection's `connection-id`, as a list returns it: base64url, without padding, of `connection-orig-match-pattern`. The raw `connection-orig-match-pattern` is also accepted.

621873e4f248df5e.title: Update Connection 2

5615fafb3c7c5b91.description: Delete connection — Deletes a connection by `connection-id`, without naming its domain. Requires Office Manager, Route Manager, or Call Center Supervisor scope in the connection\'s domain, Reseller scope in its territory, or Super User scope. The API publishes the delete on the service bus (SBUS) `connection_events` channel, and each server removes the row when the event arrives, so `202` means published, not deleted.  An id that names no connection returns `404`. One in a domain your scope does not cover returns `403`. A route profile\'s id deletes the profile with its route and route connections.  Read the connection back to confirm it is gone. A connection that another platform service keeps registering, most often an `outbound_registration` one, can be written back about 30 to 60 seconds after the delete. If it keeps coming back, contact support. — [DELETE /connections/{connection-id}]

connection-id.description: The connection's `connection-id`, as a list returns it: base64url, without padding, of `connection-orig-match-pattern`. The raw `connection-orig-match-pattern` is also accepted.

5615fafb3c7c5b91.title: Delete Connection

0096af0eb4ec2fe1.description: Create domain connection — Creates a connection in the domain. Requires Office Manager, Route Manager, or Call Center Supervisor scope in the domain, Reseller scope in its territory, or Super User scope. The API publishes the connection on the service bus (SBUS) `connection_events` channel, and each server writes it when the event arrives, so `202` means published, not applied.  `connection-orig-match-pattern` is required. The domain comes from the path, and a `domain` in the body is ignored. `connection-orig-match-pattern` is the connection\'s key and must be unique across the platform, not only the domain: a value any connection already uses returns `409`. `connection-term-match-pattern` defaults to it, and `connection-translation-request-host` and `connection-translation-destination-host` default to `connection-address`, as the API formats it for the connectivity type. `connection-source-ip-checking-enabled` and `connection-include-server-header-enabled` default to `no`. `connection-connectivity-type` defaults to `header_ip_match` and sets `connection-sip-authenticate-as-client-enabled`: `yes` for `outbound_registration`, `no` for every other type. A value you send that contradicts the type is overridden, and the response carries a `Warning` header and a `warnings` list. `connection-sip-registration-password` defaults to a random 8-character value.  Create route profiles with `POST /domains/{domain}/routeprofiles`. Sending `call-routing` here returns `404`.  Send `synchronous=yes`, in the body or the query string, to wait up to 2 seconds for the connection to be written. You then get `200` with the connection. If it is not written in time, you get the usual `202`.  If a connection with the same `connection-orig-match-pattern` was deleted in the last 15 minutes, and the platform is set to block re-created connections, some servers can refuse the new one after the `202`. Read it back, and repeat the create if it is missing.  A domain that does not exist returns `404`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/connections]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

0096af0eb4ec2fe1.title: Create Domain Connection

ffba703b7b301a0b.description: Delete user contacts by name — Deletes every contact in a user\'s personal address book that matches a first and last name, and optionally a tag. To delete one contact, use `DELETE /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/contacts/{contact_id}` instead.  Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, and Call Center Supervisor can delete from their own address book only. Site Manager can delete from its own and from those of users at its own site, Office Manager from any user\'s in its domain, Reseller from those of users in domains of its territory, and Super User from any. Any other address book returns `403`.  `name-first-name` and `name-last-name` are required and match exactly; `tags` narrows the match to contacts whose stored tags contain its text. Send them in the query string or the JSON body. Every contact that matches is deleted, so check the matches with the list first. When none match, nothing is deleted and the call still returns `202`. Only this address book is searched; the domain\'s shared contacts are never deleted this way. Unlike the delete by ID, this call leaves the contacts\' avatars and video contact copies in place.  `202` means the deletes were accepted and are applied shortly after. — [DELETE /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/contacts]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

name-first-name.description: Deletes only contacts with exactly this first name. Required.

name-last-name.description: Deletes only contacts with exactly this last name. Required.

tags.description: Deletes only contacts whose stored tag list contains this text, such as `cg-Vendors` for the group `Vendors` or `fav` for favorites.

user.description: User whose personal address book you delete from, such as `1001`. `~` means you, and then also sets the domain to your own.

Needs domain tier or above: Office Manager can delete its own domain\'s shared contacts, Reseller those of domains in its territory, and Super User any domain\'s. Only this address book is searched. ff77390204ecdcf3.description: Count custom scopes — Returns the number of custom scopes. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.  Filter with `parent-scope` and `enabled` as on `GET /scopes`. Built-in scopes are never counted, and hidden scopes only with `include-hidden=yes`. — [GET /scopes/count]

enabled.description: `yes` returns only enabled custom scopes and `no` only disabled ones. `true` and `1` mean `yes`; any other value means `no`. Allowed values: "yes", "no", "true", "1"

include-hidden.description: `yes` includes scopes marked `hidden`. `true` and `1` also work. A read of one scope by name always returns it. Allowed values: "yes", "true", "1", "no"

parent-scope.description: Return only custom scopes with this exact parent scope.

ff77390204ecdcf3.title: Count Custom Scopes

c6803cd1f5c1f705.description: List Assignable Scopes — Returns the scopes the caller can assign to a user, built-in and custom together, so one call fills a scope picker.  Any scope can call this. The list holds only scopes the caller is allowed to assign: scopes at or below its own. A caller on a custom scope gets its own scope plus the scopes below its parent.  Hidden scopes and disabled custom scopes are left out for every caller, Super User included. To manage the full catalog, hidden scopes included, use `GET /scopes?include-built-in=yes&include-hidden=yes`. — [GET /scopes/list]
c6803cd1f5c1f705.title: List Assignable Scopes

a94cdbe9a281377d.description: List custom scopes — Returns the custom scopes, sorted by name. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.  A custom scope takes a built-in parent scope and removes rights from it, so it can never do more than its parent. Users and API keys are assigned it by name. Its rights come from these settings:  - **`modifications`.** Per-object limits, keyed by API object name: `none` removes the object, `ro` allows reads only, `update-only` allows reads and updates, and `no-delete` allows everything but deletes. - **`read-only`.** `yes` refuses every write, on every object. - **`enabled`.** `no` refuses every token issued under the scope until you set it back to `yes`.  Changes apply to tokens already issued within seconds. Tokens are not reissued.  Send `include-built-in=yes` to add the built-in scopes after the custom ones, each with `built-in: yes`, so one call fills a scope picker. `hidden` controls only whether a scope appears in `GET /scopes`. It does not change what the scope can do or who holds it. Hidden scopes are left out unless you send `include-hidden=yes`.  Filter with `parent-scope` and `enabled`, page with `limit` and `start`, and order with `sort`. Paging applies to custom scopes only; built-in entries are added after it. For the number of custom scopes, use `GET /scopes/count`. — [GET /scopes]

enabled.description: `yes` returns only enabled custom scopes and `no` only disabled ones. `true` and `1` mean `yes`; any other value means `no`. Allowed values: "yes", "no", "true", "1"

include-built-in.description: `yes` adds the built-in scopes after the custom ones, with `built-in: yes`. `true` and `1` also work. Allowed values: "yes", "true", "1", "no"

include-hidden.description: `yes` includes scopes marked `hidden`. `true` and `1` also work. A read of one scope by name always returns it. Allowed values: "yes", "true", "1", "no"

limit.description: The most custom scopes to return. Default: 100

parent-scope.description: Return only custom scopes with this exact parent scope.

sort.description: The sort order: a column name, optionally followed by a space and `asc` or `desc`. Use the stored names `name`, `parent_scope`, `enabled`, or `hidden`. Separate two with a comma. Defaults to `name asc`.

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

a94cdbe9a281377d.title: List Custom Scopes

30442ecde970f87f.description: Create custom scope — Creates a custom scope and returns it. Requires Super User scope. Super User Read Only can read scopes but cannot change them, and neither can a custom scope, even one derived from Super User.  A custom scope takes a built-in parent scope and removes rights from it, so it can never do more than its parent. Users and API keys are assigned it by name. Its rights come from these settings:  - **`modifications`.** Per-object limits, keyed by API object name: `none` removes the object, `ro` allows reads only, `update-only` allows reads and updates, and `no-delete` allows everything but deletes. - **`read-only`.** `yes` refuses every write, on every object. - **`enabled`.** `no` refuses every token issued under the scope until you set it back to `yes`.  Changes apply to tokens already issued within seconds. Tokens are not reissued.  Send `name` and `parent-scope`. `parent-scope` is one of the eight built-in scopes you can derive from. A name already in use is a `409`, and so is the name of a built-in scope. The scope is applied shortly after the response, so wait for it to appear before you assign it. — [POST /scopes]

description.description: A note about the scope, up to 256 characters.

enabled.description: `no` refuses the scope's tokens until it is enabled. Defaults to `yes`; any value other than `yes`, `true`, or `1` means `no`. Allowed values: "yes", "no", "true", "1". Default: "yes"

hidden.description: `yes` leaves the scope out of `GET /scopes`. `true` and `1` also mean `yes`. Defaults to `no`. Allowed values: "yes", "no", "true", "1". Default: "no"

modifications.description: Rights removed from the parent scope, per object. Each key is an API object name, such as `phonenumber`, `device`, `route`, or `nsconfig`, and an unknown name is refused. Each value is one of these limits: - `none`: the object is refused. - `ro`: reads, lists, and counts only. - `update-only`: reads, lists, counts, and updates. - `no-delete`: everything but deletes. An object not listed keeps the parent's rights.

name.description: The scope name, assigned to users and API keys and carried by their tokens. 1 to 32 characters: letters, digits, spaces, `.`, `_`, and `-`, starting with a letter or digit. It cannot be the name of a built-in scope.

parent-scope.description: The built-in scope this one takes its rights from. A custom scope cannot be a parent. Allowed values: "Basic User", "Call Center Agent", "Call Center Supervisor", "Site Manager", "Office Manager", "Route Manager", "Reseller", "Super User"

bca01aa41f09e684.description: Read custom scope — Returns one custom scope by name. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope. A hidden scope is returned too.  The name of a built-in scope returns its catalog entry, with `built-in: yes` and its `hidden` setting.  A custom scope takes a built-in parent scope and removes rights from it, so it can never do more than its parent. Users and API keys are assigned it by name. Its rights come from these settings:  - **`modifications`.** Per-object limits, keyed by API object name: `none` removes the object, `ro` allows reads only, `update-only` allows reads and updates, and `no-delete` allows everything but deletes. - **`read-only`.** `yes` refuses every write, on every object. - **`enabled`.** `no` refuses every token issued under the scope until you set it back to `yes`.  Changes apply to tokens already issued within seconds. Tokens are not reissued. — [GET /scopes/{name}]

name.description: The scope name: 1 to 32 characters, letters, digits, spaces, `.`, `_`, and `-`, starting with a letter or digit. URL-encode spaces. A built-in scope name addresses its catalog entry.

bca01aa41f09e684.title: Read Custom Scope

a6b418a083489c42.description: Update custom scope — Changes a custom scope. Requires Super User scope. Super User Read Only can read scopes but cannot change them, and neither can a custom scope, even one derived from Super User.  Send only the fields to change. `modifications` replaces the whole map. Changes apply to tokens already issued within seconds, and `enabled: no` refuses them until you enable the scope again. The name cannot be changed.  For a built-in scope name, only `hidden` can be sent. `hidden` controls only whether a scope appears in `GET /scopes`. It does not change what the scope can do or who holds it. Any other field is a `400`.  The response is `202`: the change is accepted and applied shortly after. — [PUT /scopes/{name}]

description.description: A note about the scope, up to 256 characters.

enabled.description: `no` refuses the scope's tokens until it is enabled. Defaults to `yes`; any value other than `yes`, `true`, or `1` means `no`. Allowed values: "yes", "no", "true", "1". Default: "yes"

hidden.description: `yes` leaves the scope out of `GET /scopes`. `true` and `1` also mean `yes`. Defaults to `no`. Allowed values: "yes", "no", "true", "1". Default: "no"

modifications.description: Replaces the whole map. Send `{}` to remove every limit.

read-only.description: `yes` refuses every write. `true` and `1` also mean `yes`. Defaults to `no`. Allowed values: "yes", "no", "true", "1". Default: "no"

4a09bf9102577203.description: Delete custom scope — Deletes a custom scope. Requires Super User scope. Super User Read Only can read scopes but cannot change them, and neither can a custom scope, even one derived from Super User.  Tokens issued under it are refused with `403` from their next request once the delete is applied. Users and API keys still assigned the scope cannot log in until you assign another one. To stop a scope without deleting it, set `enabled` to `no`.  For a built-in scope name, this clears its `hidden` setting back to the default and deletes nothing. It returns `404` when no setting is stored.  The response is `202`: the delete is accepted and applied shortly after. — [DELETE /scopes/{name}]

596429f8a19d67d0.description: Count user dashboards — Counts the dashboards a user sees in the domain, the same set that `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/dashboards/list` returns.  You can always reach your own user. Another user\'s dashboards need Office Manager or Office Manager Read-Only scope in that user\'s domain, Reseller scope with the domain in your territory, or Super User or Super User Read Only scope. Office Manager and Reseller reach only users with a lower scope than their own. A user you cannot reach, or one that does not exist, returns `404`.  The set is what the user sees: dashboards the user owns, dashboards shared with the domain, stock dashboards offered to the user\'s scope, and dashboards shared with the user by name, scope, or department. Share rules are matched against the user\'s own scope and department. Dashboards the user has hidden are left out.  Send only the filters listed here. A query-builder key such as `OR` or `joins`, or a filter name that is not a plain field name, returns `400`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/dashboards/count]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

owner_id.description: Counts only dashboards owned by this extension, such as `1001`. Exact match.

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

Another user\'s dashboards need Office Manager or Office Manager Read-Only scope in that user\'s domain, Reseller scope with the domain in your territory, or Super User or Super User Read Only scope. Office Manager and Reseller reach only users with a lower scope than their own. A user you cannot reach, or one that does not exist, returns `404`.  The set is what the user sees: dashboards the user owns, dashboards shared with the domain, stock dashboards offered to the user\'s scope, and dashboards shared with the user by name, scope, or department. Share rules are matched against the user\'s own scope and department. Dashboards the user has hidden are left out. Stock dashboards offered across the platform have `domain` set to `*`.  Send only the filters listed here. A query-builder key such as `OR` or `joins`, or a filter name that is not a plain field name, returns `400`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/dashboards/list]

ac42d0be9d313a11.description: Read dashboards — Returns the dashboards your token sees in the domain, with their layouts and sharing settings, and whether you marked each one a favorite or hid it.  Requires a token that can read dashboards for the user in the path: the user itself, or Office Manager scope or higher for the domain.  The user in the path is not used to choose the dashboards: the result is always what your own token sees, including dashboards you hid. Filter by `id` for one dashboard: an ID that is not in this domain returns `404`, and one you cannot see returns `403`. For another user\'s dashboards, use `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/dashboards/list`.  Send only the filters listed here. A query-builder key such as `OR` or `joins`, or a filter name that is not a plain field name, returns `400`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/dashboards]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

id.description: Returns only this dashboard.

limit.description: Maximum dashboards to read before the visibility check. Defaults to `100`. Default: 100

owner_id.description: Only dashboards owned by this extension, such as `1001`. Exact match.

share_type.description: Only dashboards with this sharing type. Allowed values: "select", "domain", "stock"

user.description: Extension of a user in the domain, such as `1001`. `~` means your own user. It decides which scope check applies; the dashboards themselves are chosen by your token.

3708117ad9c09eae.description: Create dashboard — Creates a dashboard in the domain in the path, owned by the user in the path unless you name another owner.  Requires a token that can create dashboards for the user in the path: the user itself, or Office Manager scope or higher for the domain. Naming another owner in `owner_id` needs the right to change that user\'s dashboards, and an `owner_type` other than `1` needs Office Manager scope or higher. Otherwise the request returns `403`.  Leave out `id` to have one assigned. The response does not return it, so send your own `id` when you need to know it; an ID already in use returns `409`. Find the dashboard with `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/dashboards/list`, then add charts with `POST /domains/{domain}/charts/{dashboard_id}`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/dashboards]

properties.description: Display settings, as a JSON string the app defines. No practical length limit.

public_id.description: ID of the dashboard's public link. Anyone holding it can open the dashboard.

user.description: Extension of a user in the domain, such as `1001`. `~` means your own user. The dashboard is owned by this user unless `owner_id` names another.

3708117ad9c09eae.title: Create Dashboard

db8119db803f81db.description: Update dashboard — Changes a dashboard, named by `id` in the body. Only the fields you send change, and the dashboard stays in its own domain. A stock dashboard, offered across the platform, can be changed only by a Super User. Sharing a dashboard with someone never lets them change it. Giving the dashboard to another owner needs the same right over that user, and changing `owner_type` needs Office Manager scope or higher.  A dashboard that is not in the domain in the path returns `404`; one you may not change returns `403`. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/dashboards]
