c671375a4c737b17.description: List defaults — Lists stored default values: the rows that fill fields a create leaves out. Each row names an object, a v2 field, a value, and the tier it applies at: the whole system (`reseller` and `domain` both `*`), one territory (`reseller` set), or one domain (`domain` set).  Each scope reads its own tier and the tiers above it, never another tenant\'s rows:  - Super User and Super User Read Only read every row. - Reseller and Route Manager Reseller read their territory\'s rows, the rows of domains in their territory, and, with `full=true`, the system rows. - Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, and Site Manager read their own domain\'s rows and, with `full=true`, the territory and system rows that apply to it. - Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent get `403`.  Each filter matches exactly, and `*` or an empty value means no filter. `full=true` adds the rows your tier inherits. Rows are paged with `start` and `limit`, which defaults to `100`. For keys without values, append `/list`.  How defaults apply: when a domain, user, or device is created, each field the request leaves out takes the value of the most specific matching row. A domain row wins over a territory row, which wins over a system row. Within one tier, a row for the object wins over one whose `default-object` is `*`. User and device creates read the domain\'s rows, its territory\'s rows, and the system rows; a domain create reads territory and system rows, since the domain can\'t hold rows yet. Fields no row covers fall back to the legacy default values.  To see what can carry a default, call `GET /defaults/objects` and `GET /defaults/objects/{object}/fields`. — [GET /defaults]

default-field.description: Returns only rows for this field, as a v2 field name such as `time-zone`. `*` or empty means any. Always an exact match.

default-object.description: Returns only rows for this object: `domain`, `user`, or `device`. `*` or empty means any. With `full=true`, rows with `default-object` `*` are included too.

domain.description: Returns only rows for this domain, such as `example.com`. Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, and Site Manager must send their own domain (another returns `403`, none returns `400`); a Reseller may name a domain in its territory. `*` does not count as a domain.

full.description: `true` also returns the rows the tier inherits. For a domain: the rows of its territory and the system rows (never another territory's). For a Reseller without `domain`: the system rows. `yes` and `1` also work. Defaults to `false`. Default: false

limit.description: Most rows to return, 1 to 1000. Defaults to `100`. Anything else returns `400`. Default: 100

reseller.description: Returns only rows for this territory, such as `example-reseller`. `*` or empty means any. Super User and Super User Read Only can name any territory; a Reseller or Route Manager Reseller naming another territory gets `403`.

sort.description: Sort order: one or more comma-separated terms, each a field name optionally followed by `asc` or `desc` (`asc` when left out; any case). Field names are the seven v2 names `default-object`, `default-field`, `reseller`, `domain`, `default-value`, `created-datetime`, and `updated-datetime`, or the legacy column names `default_object`, `default_field`, `default_value`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`. Anything else returns `400`. With no `sort`, rows come in key order.

start.description: Number of rows to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. A negative or non-integer value returns `400`. Default: 0

c671375a4c737b17.title: List Defaults

3498724c3d47ef1f.description: Create default — Creates a default value, or replaces the value of the row with the same key. The key is `default-object`, `default-field`, `reseller`, and `domain`; each one you leave out is `*`. Send `reseller` for a territory row, `domain` for a domain row, and neither for a system row.  Who can write:  - Super User writes every tier. Only Super User writes system rows (`reseller` and `domain` both `*`). - Reseller writes its territory\'s rows (`reseller` set to your territory) and rows of domains in its territory. - Office Manager and Route Manager write their own domain\'s rows. - Route Manager Reseller, Call Center Supervisor, Office Manager Read-Only, Site Manager, Super User Read Only, and user scopes get `403`.  `default-object` is `domain`, `user`, `device`, or `*`, and is stored lowercase. `default-field` must be a field `GET /defaults/objects/{object}/fields` lists for that object (for `*`, a field of any of the three); credentials, `scope`, and key fields (`domain`, `user`, `device`, `reseller`, `territory`) can\'t carry a default. Keys and value are held to their lengths. Anything else returns `400` before the change is published. `default-value` is up to 255 characters; a number is stored as its string form.  The change is checked, then published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied on every server shortly after, so `202` means accepted, not yet stored. Read the row back to confirm it. Send `domain` and `reseller` in the body: in the query string they\'re ignored. — [POST /defaults]

default-field.description: v2 field the default sets, as `GET /defaults/objects/{object}/fields` lists it. Credentials, `scope`, and key fields are refused

default-object.description: Object the default applies to: `domain`, `user`, `device`, or `*` for any of them. Stored lowercase

default-value.description: Value filled into the field, up to 255 characters. A number is stored as its string form; any other non-string returns `400`

domain.description: Domain the row applies to, or `*`. Defaults to `*`. On `/domains/{domain}/defaults` the path wins

reseller.description: Territory the row applies to, or `*`. Defaults to `*`. On `/resellers/{reseller}/defaults` the path wins

511991b8c7735427.description: Update default — Changes the value of an existing default. Name the row by its key: `default-object`, `default-field`, `reseller`, and `domain`, as the list returns them; each one you leave out is `*`. A key that matches no row returns `404`; to create or replace in one call, use `POST /defaults`. `created-datetime` never changes.  Who can write:  - Super User writes every tier. Only Super User writes system rows (`reseller` and `domain` both `*`). - Reseller writes its territory\'s rows (`reseller` set to your territory) and rows of domains in its territory. - Office Manager and Route Manager write their own domain\'s rows. - Route Manager Reseller, Call Center Supervisor, Office Manager Read-Only, Site Manager, Super User Read Only, and user scopes get `403`.  `default-object` is `domain`, `user`, `device`, or `*`, and is stored lowercase. `default-field` must be a field `GET /defaults/objects/{object}/fields` lists for that object (for `*`, a field of any of the three); credentials, `scope`, and key fields (`domain`, `user`, `device`, `reseller`, `territory`) can\'t carry a default. Keys and value are held to their lengths. Anything else returns `400` before the change is published.  The change is checked, then published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied on every server shortly after, so `202` means accepted, not yet stored. Read the row back to confirm it. — [PUT /defaults]

default-object.description: Object of the row to change: `domain`, `user`, `device`, or `*`. Left out means `*`

1ba3f126daad6f61.description: Delete default — Deletes one default. Name the row in the body by its key: `default-object`, `default-field`, `reseller`, and `domain`; each one you leave out is `*`, so the call removes exactly one row. `default-value` is ignored. The key is not checked against the catalog, so a row stored before the catalog rules can still be removed; `default-object` is matched as sent.  Who can delete:  - Super User writes every tier. The change is checked, then published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied on every server shortly after, so `202` means accepted, not yet stored. Read the row back to confirm it. A key that matches no row deletes nothing and still answers `202`. — [DELETE /defaults]

fd560451e7a0a26a.description: Read domain SIP servers — Returns the SIP servers a domain\'s clients connect to, in the order to try them, with the WebSocket URI for web phones and the DNS SRV records for each transport. Every user can read the servers of their own domain, and Resellers the domains in their territory.  How the list is built:  1. The preferred server is the `provisioning.preferred-server` domain setting, read from the domain, then the reseller, then the system. When none is set, the legacy portal setting is used, then the platform default. 2. The other servers in the preferred server\'s geographic group follow, if they allow backup. When the `provisioning.redundancy` setting is `none`, the list holds the preferred server alone. 3. `servers` is sorted by `priority`, lowest first. The order is not by distance: the API has no location for a browser.  `srv` lists the `_sip._tls`, `_sip._tcp`, and `_sip._udp` names of each server group with their resolved records. `preferred-srv` is the entry for the `provisioning.preferred-transport` setting, or `tls` when it is unset. A Reseller sees the subscriptions in its own territory, except the ones a Super User created, and can narrow to one of its domains. Every other scope sees the subscriptions its own scope created in its own domain, and user-level scopes see only their own and domain-wide ones. Naming a domain you cannot see returns `403`.  `post-url` comes back in full only when you can change the subscription. Otherwise its user-info, query string, and fragment are masked.  Filter with `user`. Page with `start` and `limit`, 100 subscriptions by default. `GET /domains/{domain}/subscriptions/list` returns fewer fields per subscription. b1cd1cbc3b3de942.description: Create domain event subscription — Creates a subscription that sends one domain\'s events of one `model` to your `post-url`. It is `POST /subscriptions` with the domain taken from the path; a `domain` in the body is ignored.  Requires Basic User, Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User, and read access to the model (`403` without it). A Reseller can name any domain in its own territory. Office Manager, Site Manager, and Basic User can name only their own domain, and a Site Manager only users of its own site.  Choose `model` from these values:  | `model` | Sends | |---|---| | `call` | Active call updates | | `call_origid` | Active call updates, only the latest state of each call per batch | | `cdr` | Completed call records | | `agent` | Call center agent status changes, matched on the call queue | | `voicemail` | New voicemail | | `message`, `messagesession` | Chat and SMS messages and sessions |  Also available: `presence`, `subscriber`, `auditlog`, `auditlog_lite` (creates and deletes of main objects only), `domain`, and `device`.  `post-url` must be an `http://` or `https://` URL with a host, at most 256 characters, with the scheme only once and no `user:password@` part. Unless you are a Super User, every address the host resolves to must be public: loopback, link-local, private, shared (CGNAT), and unique-local addresses are refused, and so are this platform\'s own servers. A host that does not resolve is refused too. Each refusal is a `400` that names the rule. An installation can allow private addresses with the `NsSubscriptionAllowPrivateUrls` setting. Use `https://` with a certificate that validates, because a certificate error counts as a failed delivery.  `subscription-expires-datetime` takes RFC 3339, such as `2027-09-01T14:30:00+00:00`, or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC. It is stored in UTC and read back as RFC 3339. Any other value returns `400`.  The call waits up to 5 seconds for the subscription to be stored, then returns it with `200`. Creating the same subscription twice returns `409`. See `POST /subscriptions` for how events are delivered and expired. Retries and a signing secret are tracked in NN-663. — [POST /domains/{domain}/subscriptions]

domain.description: Domain whose events are sent. Defaults to your own domain. `*` means every domain and needs Super User (`403` otherwise). A domain that does not exist returns `404`. Ignored on `/domains/{domain}/subscriptions`, which takes the path domain.

model.description: Kind of event the subscription sends. One model per subscription: `call`, `call_origid` (latest state of each call only), `cdr`, `agent` (matched on the call queue), `voicemail`, `message`, `messagesession`, `presence`, `presense` (a misspelt presence model, still accepted), `subscriber`, `auditlog`, `auditlog_lite` (creates and deletes of main objects only), `domain`, or `device`. Your scope needs read access to the model. Any other value returns `400`. Allowed values: "agent", "auditlog", "auditlog_lite", "call", "call_origid", "cdr", "device", "domain", "message", "messagesession", "presence", "presense", "subscriber", "voicemail"

post-url.description: URL each batch of events is sent to with `POST`. An `http://` or `https://` URL with a host, up to 256 characters, with no `user:password@` part. Unless a Super User sets it, it must resolve only to public addresses outside this platform.

preferred-server.description: Hostname of the core server that should deliver a `subscription-geo-support: yes` subscription. It takes over after it has been up for 60 seconds. Defaults to the server that handled the create. Name a real core server: an unknown hostname can leave the subscription with no server delivering it.

reseller.description: Ignored: the territory comes from the domain. A Super User sending it with `domain` `*` gets `400`.

subscription-expires-datetime.description: When delivery stops, as RFC 3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC. Stored in UTC. Defaults to the expiry of your token, or 20 years for a token that does not expire. Any other value returns `400`.

subscription-geo-support.description: `yes` stores the subscription on every server and has one of them deliver it, with another taking over if that server stops. `no` stores it only on the server that handled the create, which alone delivers it. Defaults to `yes`. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "yes"

user.description: User whose events are sent, or `*` for every user in the domain. `*` needs Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User; a Site Manager must name a user of its own site, and user-level scopes always get their own extension. Default: "*"

a66f24fe781d797e.description: Update domain event subscription — Changes where a subscription sends, what it sends, or how long it lives. Send only the fields to change.  Requires Basic User, Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User.  Who can change or delete a subscription:  - Super User: any subscription - Reseller: one for a domain in its own territory, never a platform-wide one or one a Super User created - Office Manager: any in its own domain - Site Manager: its own, or one for a user of its own site, never a domain-wide one - Every other scope: its own  Anything else returns `403`, and the message names the reason.  You can change `post-url`, `model`, `subscription-expires-datetime`, `subscription-geo-support`, and `preferred-server`. A new `post-url` follows the create rules. A new `model` must be a known model (`400`) that you can read (`403`). Send `error-count` or `posts-count` as `0` to reset it; any other value is ignored. `domain`, `user`, and `reseller` cannot change: a different value returns `400`, so delete the subscription and create a new one. Leaving out `subscription-expires-datetime` keeps the current expiry. `subscription-expires-datetime` takes RFC 3339, such as `2027-09-01T14:30:00+00:00`, or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC. It is stored in UTC and read back as RFC 3339. Any other value returns `400`.  A `202` means the change was saved on this server and published to the others over the service bus (SBUS), including a switch of `subscription-geo-support` from `yes` to `no`. Delivery picks it up within about 5 seconds.  This is `PUT /subscriptions/{id}` under a domain path. The subscription is found by `id` alone; the path domain is checked for your access, not matched against the subscription. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/subscriptions/{id}]

posts-count.description: Send `0` to reset the delivery counter. Allowed values: 0

Each call handles at most `limit` versions and reports how many remain; call again until `remaining` is 0. A reanalysis records new verdicts but never changes which version is live. allowed_hostnames.description: Origins that the remote authentication callbacks may use. Send an array, a comma-separated string, or a JSON array as a string. No member may contain a comma. Stored and returned as a comma-separated string.

37dc5edf31453a0f.description: Deploy extension version — Fetches a bundle, analyzes it, and makes it the live version when it passes. Requires Reseller, Super User, or Admin Super User scope. A Reseller can deploy only its own extensions.  The result is in `status`: `approved` and `flagged` go live; `rejected` changes nothing live. A host that is not in `approved-cdn-origins`, or a bundle that cannot be fetched, is also answered `200` with `status: rejected`; the report says why. When the bytes match the live version, the answer is `unchanged` and nothing is written, so a build pipeline can call this on every run.  On development servers, a `localhost` or `127.0.0.1` URL is not fetched or analyzed: it goes live as `dev`, without an integrity hash.  Each extension allows 10 deploys a minute. `promoted: true` means the version was accepted and takes effect shortly after; send `synchronous=yes` to wait for it. — [POST /ui-extensions/registry/{id}/deploy]

analysis-denylist.description: Denied packages and suppressed findings. Reads include the built-in suppressions, which always apply. On write, an unknown key returns `400`.

analysis-rule-policy.description: Per-rule overrides, keyed by rule id. Send only the rules you change. An unknown rule id returns `400`. `missing-source-map` must stay in `enforce` mode.

analysis-settings.description: Bundle-analysis limits. Reads always return every key. On write, an unknown key, a numeric string, or a value out of range returns `400`.

api-read-deny-resources.description: API resources extensions may not read. Replaces the stored list.

api-write-deny-resources.description: API resources extensions may not change. Replaces the stored list.

approved-cdn-origins.description: Hosts an extension bundle may be served from: bare hostnames or `*.example.com` wildcards, with no scheme or port. Replaces the stored list. `[]` approves no host, which blocks every deploy and reanalysis.

disabled-capabilities.description: Capabilities withheld from every extension. Replaces the stored list.

disabled-zones.description: Zones no extension may mount into. Replaces the stored list. `[]` clears it.

6209960a01470fc7.description: List inboxes — Returns the shared and main-number inboxes in a domain, sorted by extension. Personal inboxes are not listed: read a user\'s inboxes with `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/inboxes`.  An inbox is where SMS conversations are read and answered. A shared inbox has its own extension, and every member sees and answers its conversations.  `inbox_kind` is one of these values:  - `shared`: an inbox you create, with its own extension, one owner, and the members you add. - `main_number`: an inbox you create, with its own extension and no owner. - `personal`: the inbox every user already has, holding their SMS conversations across all their phone numbers (DIDs). It is addressed by the user\'s own extension and is never created or deleted here.  `include_deactivated` adds deleted inboxes, with `deactivated: true`. It accepts `1`, `true`, or `yes`, and only Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can use it: for other scopes it is ignored. `owner` and `inbox_kind` are `null` when they could not be read.  Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Site Manager reaches only the inboxes whose owner is a user in its own site. An inbox with no owner, or whose owner cannot be read, is out of its reach. Other scopes get `403`. For a Site Manager, the list holds only those inboxes. — [GET /domains/{domain}/inboxes]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

include_deactivated.description: Set to `1`, `true`, or `yes` to include deleted inboxes. Only Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can use it; for other scopes it is ignored. Allowed values: "1", "true", "yes"

6209960a01470fc7.title: List Inboxes Domain

78b9966af07278c2.description: Create inbox — Creates a shared or main-number inbox with its own extension. The owner of a shared inbox becomes its first member. The extension then belongs to the inbox: it is hidden from the directory and cannot be given to a user until the inbox is deleted.  `inbox_kind` is one of these values:  - `shared`: an inbox you create, with its own extension, one owner, and the members you add. - `main_number`: an inbox you create, with its own extension and no owner. - `personal`: the inbox every user already has, holding their SMS conversations across all their phone numbers (DIDs). It is addressed by the user\'s own extension and is never created or deleted here.  `owner` names the owner of a `shared` inbox, as an extension in the domain or `<extension>@<domain>`. It defaults to you. It is required when your token is not in `{domain}`, because the owner must be a user of the inbox\'s own domain, and it cannot be changed later. It must be a user, not a call queue, conference, or another inbox. A `main_number` inbox has no owner: sending `owner` returns `400`.  `inbox_name` is split at its first space into a first and last name. A one-word name gets ` Inbox` appended, so `Support` is stored and returned as `Support Inbox`. Names are unique in the domain, compared after that split: a name already in use returns `409`. An extension already in use returns `409`.  A Site Manager can create only a `shared` inbox whose owner, named or defaulted to you, is a user in its own site. Any other owner, or a `main_number` inbox, returns `403`. A `202` means the change is accepted and already applied.  Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope, or Site Manager scope as above. Other scopes get `403`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/inboxes]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

extension.description: The extension the inbox answers on: letters and digits only. It must not be in use in the domain.

inbox_kind.description: The kind of inbox: `shared` (the default) has an owner and members you add; `main_number` has no owner. Allowed values: "shared", "main_number". Default: "shared"

inbox_name.description: The inbox name, unique in the domain. It is split at the first space: each part holds up to 64 characters. A one-word name has ` Inbox` appended.

owner.description: The owner of a `shared` inbox: a user's extension in the domain, or `<extension>@<domain>` naming this domain. Defaults to you. Required when your token is not in this domain. Not allowed for `main_number`. For a Site Manager, the owner, named or defaulted, must be a user in its own site.

78b9966af07278c2.title: Create Inbox Domain

cf6f0fed5efd96a2.description: Read inbox — Returns one shared or main-number inbox. A user\'s extension returns `404`: a personal inbox is read with `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/inboxes`. A deleted inbox returns `404`.  `inbox_kind` is one of these values:  - `shared`: an inbox you create, with its own extension, one owner, and the members you add. - `main_number`: an inbox you create, with its own extension and no owner. - `personal`: the inbox every user already has, holding their SMS conversations across all their phone numbers (DIDs). It is addressed by the user\'s own extension and is never created or deleted here.  Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Site Manager reaches only the inboxes whose owner is a user in its own site. An inbox with no owner, or whose owner cannot be read, is out of its reach. Other scopes get `403`. For a Site Manager, an inbox out of its reach returns `404`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/inboxes/{extension}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

extension.description: The inbox extension: letters and digits only.

cf6f0fed5efd96a2.title: Get Single Inbox

1fb95a37d5a96c0c.description: Rename inbox — Renames a shared or main-number inbox. `inbox_name` is the only field it takes; the extension, kind, and owner cannot be changed.  `inbox_name` is split at its first space into a first and last name. A one-word name gets ` Inbox` appended, so `Support` is stored and returned as `Support Inbox`. Names are unique in the domain, compared after that split: a name already in use returns `409`. Renaming an inbox to its current name succeeds.  A user\'s extension returns `404`: a personal inbox has no name of its own. A `202` means the change is accepted and already applied.  Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Site Manager reaches only the inboxes whose owner is a user in its own site. An inbox with no owner, or whose owner cannot be read, is out of its reach. A Site Manager gets `403` for an inbox out of its reach. Other callers get `403`. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/inboxes/{extension}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

extension.description: The inbox extension: letters and digits only.

inbox_name.description: The inbox name, unique in the domain. It is split at the first space: each part holds up to 64 characters. A one-word name has ` Inbox` appended.

1fb95a37d5a96c0c.title: Update Inbox Domain

2841cc443a0472b2.description: Delete inbox — Deletes a shared or main-number inbox. Its conversations are kept, the inbox is marked deactivated, and the extension is freed for reuse. A new inbox on the same extension starts empty. The API has no restore.  Deleted inboxes appear in `GET /domains/{domain}/inboxes` with `include_deactivated`. A user\'s extension returns `404`: a personal inbox cannot be deleted. A `202` means the delete is accepted and already applied.  Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Site Manager reaches only the inboxes whose owner is a user in its own site. An inbox with no owner, or whose owner cannot be read, is out of its reach. A Site Manager gets `403` for an inbox out of its reach. Other callers get `403`. — [DELETE /domains/{domain}/inboxes/{extension}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

extension.description: The inbox extension: letters and digits only.

2841cc443a0472b2.title: Delete Inbox Domain

c37392afaf2c54fb.description: List inbox members — Returns the members of an inbox and their roles. `{extension}` can be a shared inbox, or a user\'s own extension to address that user\'s personal inbox.  A member\'s `role` is one of these values:  - `owner`: the inbox owner. Set when the inbox is created, and never changed. - `can-reply`: reads and replies to conversations. - `view`: reads conversations only.  `include_deactivated` lists the members of a deleted inbox. It accepts `1`, `true`, or `yes`, and only Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can use it.  You can read the members of an inbox you are a member of, or, for a personal inbox, the one you own. Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can read any inbox\'s members. Other callers get `403`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/inboxes/{extension}/members]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

extension.description: The inbox extension: a shared or main-number inbox, or a user's own extension for that user's personal inbox. Letters and digits only.

include_deactivated.description: Set to `1`, `true`, or `yes` to list the members of a deleted inbox. Only Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can use it; for other scopes it is ignored. Allowed values: "1", "true", "yes"

c37392afaf2c54fb.title: List Inbox Members Domain

fb577e265810366e.description: Add inbox member — Adds a user of the domain to an inbox, giving them its conversations. `{extension}` can be a shared inbox, or a user\'s own extension to address that user\'s personal inbox. Adding a user who is already a member succeeds and changes nothing. Change a member\'s role with `PUT /domains/{domain}/inboxes/{extension}/members/{user}`.  `user` must be a user of the same domain, not another inbox. A `202` means the change is accepted and already applied.  For a shared or main-number inbox, requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. For a personal inbox, its owner can also add members. Other callers get `403`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/inboxes/{extension}/members]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

extension.description: The inbox extension: a shared or main-number inbox, or a user's own extension for that user's personal inbox. Letters and digits only.

user.description: The extension of a user in the same domain. It cannot be another inbox.

fb577e265810366e.title: Create Inbox Member Domain

420f0c2b4dba8bbc.description: Read inbox member — Returns one member of an inbox, with their role. `{extension}` can be a shared inbox, or a user\'s own extension to address that user\'s personal inbox. `{user}` is the member\'s extension, or `~` for you. Returns `404` when the user is not a member.  A member\'s `role` is one of these values:  - `owner`: the inbox owner. Set when the inbox is created, and never changed. - `can-reply`: reads and replies to conversations. - `view`: reads conversations only.  You can read the members of an inbox you are a member of, or, for a personal inbox, the one you own. Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can read any inbox\'s members. Other callers get `403`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/inboxes/{extension}/members/{user}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

extension.description: The inbox extension: a shared or main-number inbox, or a user's own extension for that user's personal inbox. Letters and digits only.

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

420f0c2b4dba8bbc.title: Get Inbox Member

27ac58074bca149b.description: Change inbox member role — Sets a member\'s role on a shared or main-number inbox. `role` is `can-reply` or `view`.  A member\'s `role` is one of these values:  - `owner`: the inbox owner. Set when the inbox is created, and never changed. - `can-reply`: reads and replies to conversations. - `view`: reads conversations only.  The owner\'s role cannot be changed, and `owner` cannot be assigned: either returns an error. Roles cannot be set on a personal inbox (`400`). A `202` means the change is accepted and already applied.  Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Other callers get `403`. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/inboxes/{extension}/members/{user}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

extension.description: The inbox extension: a shared or main-number inbox, or a user's own extension for that user's personal inbox. Letters and digits only.

role.description: The new role: `can-reply` (reads and replies) or `view` (reads only). `owner` cannot be assigned. Allowed values: "can-reply", "view"

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

27ac58074bca149b.title: Update Member Inbox

5d47ae0e34103751.description: Remove inbox member — Removes a member from an inbox and from all of its conversations. `{extension}` can be a shared inbox, or a user\'s own extension to address that user\'s personal inbox. Adding them back later starts them with a new role.  Any member can remove themselves, from any inbox: use `~` or their own extension as `{user}`. Otherwise, for a shared or main-number inbox, requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. For a personal inbox, its owner can also remove members. Other callers get `403`. A `202` means the delete is accepted and already applied. — [DELETE /domains/{domain}/inboxes/{extension}/members/{user}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

extension.description: The inbox extension: a shared or main-number inbox, or a user's own extension for that user's personal inbox. Letters and digits only.

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

5d47ae0e34103751.title: Delete Inbox Member Domain

8628d666400ed881.description: Assign SMS number to inbox — Assigns one of the domain\'s unassigned SMS numbers to a shared or main-number inbox. The inbox can then text from it, and texts sent to it arrive in the inbox. An inbox can have any number of SMS numbers, or none.  Only a number whose SMS application is `available` can be assigned. A number already held by a user, a call queue or another inbox answers `409`; unassign it on the phone numbers page first. Assigning a number the inbox already has succeeds and changes nothing. The inbox\'s numbers are listed in `sms_numbers` on `GET /domains/{domain}/inboxes`.  A `202` means the assignment is accepted; it is applied within a few seconds.  Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Other callers get `403`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/inboxes/{extension}/smsnumbers]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

extension.description: The inbox extension: a shared or main-number inbox. Letters and digits only.

number.description: The SMS number to assign, as the domain lists it.

8628d666400ed881.title: Create Inbox SMS Number Domain

ff7ed682be4b181a.description: Remove SMS number from inbox — Returns one of an inbox\'s SMS numbers to the domain\'s unassigned numbers. The inbox stops texting from it and receiving texts on it. Conversations that were replying from this number switch to another of the inbox\'s numbers.  Removing the inbox\'s last number is allowed: the inbox stays active for internal notes, calls and fax, and can\'t send texts until a number is assigned again.  A `202` means the removal is accepted; it is applied within a few seconds.  Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Other callers get `403`. — [DELETE /domains/{domain}/inboxes/{extension}/smsnumbers/{number}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

extension.description: The inbox extension: a shared or main-number inbox. Letters and digits only.

number.description: The SMS number to remove from the inbox.

ff7ed682be4b181a.title: Delete Inbox SMS Number Domain

90d8134bc44bc3d2.description: List user inboxes — Returns every inbox a user is a member of: shared and main-number inboxes, the user\'s own personal inbox, and personal inboxes other users have shared with them. Use it to build an inbox list for that user.  `inbox_kind` is one of these values:  - `shared`: an inbox you create, with its own extension, one owner, and the members you add. - `main_number`: an inbox you create, with its own extension and no owner. - `personal`: the inbox every user already has, holding their SMS conversations across all their phone numbers (DIDs). It is addressed by the user\'s own extension and is never created or deleted here.  A personal inbox returns one row per phone number: `did` is the number, and `user` and `owner` are the owner. `space_id` identifies each inbox\'s conversations, and stays unique when an extension is reused. `include_deactivated` adds deleted inboxes, with `deactivated: true`. It accepts `1`, `true`, or `yes`, and only Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can use it: for other scopes it is ignored. A user with no inboxes returns an empty array.  Any user can list their own inboxes. Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can list any user\'s in the domain. Site Manager and Call Center Supervisor scopes can list the inboxes of users in their own site. Other callers get `403`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/inboxes]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

include_deactivated.description: Set to `1`, `true`, or `yes` to include deleted inboxes. Only Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can use it; for other scopes it is ignored. Allowed values: "1", "true", "yes"

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

90d8134bc44bc3d2.title: List Inboxes User

fb75796ce934d485.description: Read iNSight metric series — Returns a time series for one iNSight metric, such as active calls or registered devices, for a window that ends now. Requires Super User, Super User Read Only, or Reseller scope.  A Super User reads the whole platform. A Reseller always reads its own territory, and only the labels with a reseller form: `core_activecalls`, `core_domains`, `core_subscribers`, and `core_registered`. Any other label returns `403` for a Reseller, except the `nodeping_` health-check labels. A Super User Read Only token must name a `reseller`.  Set the window with `range`, or with `start` and `end` as Unix timestamps. `step` sets the interval between points. Times in the response are Unix timestamps in seconds, not RFC 3339. A window with no data returns `404`.  The alert labels `active_alerts`, `alert_groups`, `alert_silences`, `ruler_alerts`, and `ruler_rules` need Super User or Super User Read Only scope, ignore the window parameters, and answer an alert envelope instead of a series. See `GET /insight/active_alerts`. `ruler_rules` also takes `type`, `rule_name`, `rule_group`, and `file`. — [GET /insight/{label}]

aggregated.description: `aggregated`, the default, returns one series for the whole platform. `server` returns one series per server, each row naming its `server`. Not every label has a per-server form; one without it returns `400`. Ignored when the request is answered for a reseller. Allowed values: "aggregated", "server". Default: "aggregated"

end.description: The end of the window, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Overrides the end that `range` sets, which is now, rounded down to the step.

label.description: The metric to read. One of `core_activecalls`, `core_domains`, `core_subscribers`, `core_registered`, `node_load5`, `node_load5_max`, `alerts`, `nsnode_sockets`, `system_packet_dispatched_total`, `sip_invite_received_total`, `sbus_system_queued`, `netsapiens_email_smtp_requests`, and the `nsmatrix_` labels `nsmatrix_primaries`, `nsmatrix_tuwunel_up`, `nsmatrix_primary_row_consistent`, `nsmatrix_inbound_events`, `nsmatrix_rooms_created`, `nsmatrix_homeserver_errors`, and `nsmatrix_detached_job_failures`. Any name that starts with `nodeping_` reads that health-check series. `custom` runs your own query, sent in `query`. The alert labels `active_alerts`, `alert_groups`, `alert_silences`, `ruler_alerts`, and `ruler_rules` return the alert envelope described on `GET /insight/active_alerts` instead of a series. Any other name returns `400`. A `nodeping_` label must be `nodeping_` followed by letters, digits, `_`, and `:` only.

query.description: For `custom` only, and required there: the query to run, in the metrics service's query language. Double quotes are changed to single quotes before it is sent. Needs a platform with iNSight Pro; otherwise `403`.

range.description: How far back to read, ending now. A named range (`last_hour`, `last_6_hours`, `last_12_hours`, `last_24_hours`, `last_2_days`, `last_7_days`, or `last_28_days`) or a number followed by `m`, `h`, or `d`, such as `90m`, `24h`, or `3d`. A number with no unit is hours. Defaults to `last_24_hours`. The range also sets the default `step`: `1m` up to 1 day, `10m` up to 3 days, `1h` up to 14 days, and `1d` beyond. `last_7_days` uses `1h` and `last_28_days` uses `1d`. Default: "last_24_hours"

reseller.description: The reseller (territory) to read. A Reseller token always reads its own territory, and naming another one returns `403`; you can leave it out. A Super User or Super User Read Only token that names a reseller gets that reseller's series. Only `core_activecalls`, `core_domains`, `core_subscribers`, and `core_registered` have a reseller form; any other label returns `403`. A quote, backslash, brace, or line break in it returns `400`.

start.description: The start of the window, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Overrides the start that `range` sets. Not an RFC 3339 date-time. Default: 0

step.description: The interval between points: a number and one unit, `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, or `w`, such as `30s`, `10m`, `1h`, or `1d`. Overrides the step that `range` sets. Any other value returns `400`.

transport.description: For `nodeping_` labels only: return only the checks over this transport. One of `udp`, `tcp`, `tls`, `ws`, `wss`, `http`, and `https`, in any letter case. Any other value returns `400`. Allowed values: "udp", "tcp", "tls", "ws", "wss", "http", "https"

fb75796ce934d485.title: Get Insight Label

b89f7824ee9e2ce1.description: List active iNSight alerts — Returns the alerts currently firing on the platform, as the iNSight alerting service reports them. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope; alerts are platform-wide and are not filtered by reseller.  The service\'s answer is passed through unchanged in `data`, wrapped with `status`, `source`, `endpoint`, and `count`. Filter with `filter`, `active`, `silenced`, `inhibited`, and `receiver`; any other parameter is ignored. Nothing firing returns `200` with an empty `data`.  This is `GET /insight/{label}` with the label `active_alerts`. The same envelope answers the other alert labels: `alert_groups` (alerts grouped by route), `alert_silences` (silences), `ruler_alerts` and `ruler_rules` (alert rules, with `source` `prometheus` and no `count`). For the number of firing alerts over time, read the `alerts` label as a series. — [GET /insight/active_alerts]

active.description: `true` to include active alerts, `false` to leave them out. Defaults to `true`. Allowed values: "true", "false"

filter.description: Return only alerts that match this label matcher, such as `severity="critical"`. To send several, repeat it as `filter[]`; an alert must match all of them.

inhibited.description: `true` to include inhibited alerts, `false` to leave them out. Defaults to `true`. Allowed values: "true", "false"

receiver.description: Return only alerts sent to receivers whose name matches this regular expression.

silenced.description: `true` to include silenced alerts, `false` to leave them out. Defaults to `true`. Allowed values: "true", "false"

b89f7824ee9e2ce1.title: Get Insight Active Alerts

5d93f4fa141f2ae8.description: List allowed IPs — Lists the allow list on one server: every entry from every source, with the list\'s status. Addresses on the allow list are always allowed and never blocked by the firewall. Requires Super User or Admin Super User scope.  The request goes to the IP rules service on `{hostname}`, and its status and body come back unchanged. Errors the API decides itself use the `code` and `message` form; errors from the service use the `error` form. — [GET /ipaware/{hostname}/allowed_ips]

hostname.description: Hostname of the server whose IP rules service you are managing, such as `core1.example.com`. It must be one of the platform's servers, matched without regard to case. Any other name returns `404`, and nothing is sent.

5d93f4fa141f2ae8.title: List Allowed Ips

fccd4b8c1a45abc8.description: Add allowed IPs — Adds addresses or CIDR ranges to the allow list on one server, or updates the comment and expiry of an entry that is already there. The entry applies on that server at once, and any firewall block it covers is lifted. The other servers in the cluster receive it shortly after. Requires Super User scope.  Send the address in the body, or in the `cidr` query parameter. Send an array, or repeat the query parameter, to add several in one call; each is applied on its own and the answer reports each one, with `207` when any failed. Match-all ranges such as `0.0.0.0/0` are refused.  The request goes to the IP rules service on `{hostname}`, and its status and body come back unchanged. Errors the API decides itself use the `code` and `message` form; errors from the service use the `error` form. — [POST /ipaware/{hostname}/allowed_ips]

cidr.description: Address or CIDR range to allow, or an array of them.

comment.description: Note stored with the entry. Longer text is cut to 255 characters. Applies to every item of a batch.

hostname.description: Hostname of the server whose IP rules service you are managing, such as `core1.example.com`. It must be one of the platform's servers, matched without regard to case. Any other name returns `404`, and nothing is sent.

ip.description: Same as `cidr`. Used only when `cidr` is not sent.

ttl.description: Seconds until the entry expires. `0`, the default, makes it permanent. Applies to every item of a batch.

fccd4b8c1a45abc8.title: Add Allowed IP

cce45dd825dfd049.description: Remove allowed IPs — Removes addresses or CIDR ranges from the allow list on one server. The other servers in the cluster receive the change shortly after. Requires Super User scope.  Send the address in the body, or in the `cidr` query parameter. It must match the entry as stored. Send an array, or repeat the query parameter, to remove several in one call. Only entries added to this server\'s own list can be removed; `builtin`, `url`, and `vendor` entries cannot.  If your client cannot send a body with `DELETE`, use `POST /ipaware/{hostname}/allowed_ips/remove`.  The request goes to the IP rules service on `{hostname}`, and its status and body come back unchanged. Errors the API decides itself use the `code` and `message` form; errors from the service use the `error` form. — [DELETE /ipaware/{hostname}/allowed_ips]

cidr.description: Address or CIDR range to remove, or an array of them.

hostname.description: Hostname of the server whose IP rules service you are managing, such as `core1.example.com`. It must be one of the platform's servers, matched without regard to case. Any other name returns `404`, and nothing is sent.

ip.description: Same as `cidr`. Used only when `cidr` is not sent.

cce45dd825dfd049.title: Remove Allowed IP

b1dce35b0f68b184.description: Remove allowed IPs with POST — Works the same as `DELETE /ipaware/{hostname}/allowed_ips`, for clients that cannot send a body with `DELETE`. Removes addresses or CIDR ranges from the allow list on one server. The other servers in the cluster receive the change shortly after. Requires Super User scope.  Send the address in the body, or in the `cidr` query parameter. It must match the entry as stored. Send an array, or repeat the query parameter, to remove several in one call. Only entries added to this server\'s own list can be removed; `builtin`, `url`, and `vendor` entries cannot.  The request goes to the IP rules service on `{hostname}`, and its status and body come back unchanged. Errors the API decides itself use the `code` and `message` form; errors from the service use the `error` form. — [POST /ipaware/{hostname}/allowed_ips/remove]

cidr.description: Address or CIDR range to remove, or an array of them.

hostname.description: Hostname of the server whose IP rules service you are managing, such as `core1.example.com`. It must be one of the platform's servers, matched without regard to case. Any other name returns `404`, and nothing is sent.

ip.description: Same as `cidr`. Used only when `cidr` is not sent.

b1dce35b0f68b184.title: Remove Allowed IP Alias

6425bffc014f0004.description: Read configuration — Reads the configuration of the IP rules service on one server: every key\'s value, the keys the file sets, and which changes are waiting for a restart. Requires Super User or Admin Super User scope.  It also lists the keys a change applies at once (`liveKeys`) and the keys a change copies to the rest of the cluster (`replicableKeys`), and in `replication.drift`, the servers whose values differ from this one.  The request goes to the IP rules service on `{hostname}`, and its status and body come back unchanged. Errors the API decides itself use the `code` and `message` form; errors from the service use the `error` form. — [GET /ipaware/{hostname}/config]

hostname.description: Hostname of the server whose IP rules service you are managing, such as `core1.example.com`. It must be one of the platform's servers, matched without regard to case. Any other name returns `404`, and nothing is sent.

6425bffc014f0004.title: Get Config

f0ec5e65a5463219.description: Update configuration — Sets one or more configuration keys of the IP rules service on one server. Requires Super User scope.  Every value is checked first. If any key is invalid, nothing is written and the answer lists each problem in `details`. `listen_addr` and `listen_port` cannot be changed here. Keys in `liveKeys` take effect at once; the rest take effect when the service restarts, and `effects` says which applies to each key. Keys in `replicableKeys` are also copied to the other servers in the cluster; other keys change this server only. Restart the service with `POST /ipaware/{hostname}/restart`.  The request goes to the IP rules service on `{hostname}`, and its status and body come back unchanged. 1cb1efbfb31a79f7.description: Read user greeting — Reads one voicemail greeting by its index. Index `0` is the user\'s recorded name (`name.wav`).  Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent can read their own greetings. Office Manager, Site Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, and Super User can read any user\'s greetings in the domain, as can Office Manager Read-Only and Super User Read Only.  Returns a single object, not an array. An index with no greeting returns `404`. List every greeting with `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/greetings`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/greetings/{index}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

index.description: Index of the greeting, as `ordinal-order` shows it in a list, such as `1`. Digits only. The file is `greeting-1.wav`; a leading zero (`01`) does not match it and returns `404`. `0` is the user's recorded name (`name.wav`).

user.description: User (extension) whose voicemail greetings you work with, such as `1001`. `~` means yourself. A user with no record returns `400` `Invalid User` on a read and `404` `User not found` on a write.

1cb1efbfb31a79f7.title: Read Greeting

8d3474bd164621b8.description: Play greeting — Streams one of a user\'s voicemail greetings, so a browser or an `<audio>` element can play it. Index `0` is the user\'s recorded name.  Call it one of two ways:  - **With a session.** Send a bearer token, or let the browser send its session cookie. The access is the same as for reading the file. Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent can play only their own files. Site Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, and Route Manager can play any user\'s files in their domain. Reseller and Route Manager Reseller can play files in the domains of their territory, and Super User and Super User Read Only in every domain. Any other file answers `403`. - **With a signed link.** Every read of the file returns `file-access-url`, which is this path with `expires` and `signature` added. Anyone holding the link can play that one file, with no token, until it expires (24 hours by default). Treat the link like the file itself.  Without `download`, the file is sent inline and a single range request (`Range: bytes=...`) is answered with `206`, so a player can seek. A range that starts past the end of the file answers `416`. The response is never cached by a shared cache. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/greetings/{index}/play]

convert.description: Transcodes the audio before it is sent: `aac` (`audio/aac`) or `ogg` (`audio/ogg`). Left out, the stored WAV file is sent (`audio/wav`). Allowed values: "aac", "ogg"

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

download.description: `yes` sends the file as a download (`Content-Disposition: attachment`) and turns off range requests. Left out or blank, the file is sent inline so a browser or an `<audio>` element plays it. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

expires.description: The expiry of a signed link, in Unix seconds. Copy it from `file-access-url`; never set it yourself. Leave it out when you call with a token or a session cookie.

index.description: The index of the greeting, as `ordinal-order` shows it in a list, such as `1`. Digits only. The file is `greeting-1.wav`. `0` is the recorded name (`name.wav`). With a token, leading zeros are ignored, so `01` names the same file. A signed link must use the index exactly as `file-access-url` gives it, or it answers `403`.

signature.description: The signature of a signed link, from `file-access-url`. With it the call needs no token, and it plays only the file the path names until `expires`. An expired link answers `403` with `Link has expired`; a changed path or expiry answers `403` with `Invalid signature`. Leave it out when you call with a token or a session cookie.

user.description: The user (extension) whose greeting you play, such as `1001`. Use `~` for yourself. A user that does not exist answers `404`.

7745495ddf17e571.description: Read meeting — Returns one meeting with its attendees, as seen by the user in the path.  Access is checked against the meeting\'s owner: any user in the owner\'s domain can read it, and Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User can read it in the domains they manage. When you are the user in the path and you are on the meeting, you are checked as yourself, so an attendee from another domain reads the meeting through its own path. `meeting-passcode` is shown only to the meeting\'s owner, its hosts, and Office Manager or higher for its domain. Everyone else gets it masked with asterisks; `include-secret=yes` does not change that.  The meeting is returned when the user in the path owns it or is on it, or when it is open to anyone with its ID (`meeting-join-require-invite-enabled` is `0`) and not locked. When you read as yourself with a token that can write, the read also joins you: it adds you as an attendee of an open meeting you are not on, adds you as a host of your own meeting when you are missing from its attendees, and with `isInit=1` starts an instance. Reading on behalf of another user never changes the meeting. `attendees` is a JSON-encoded string. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}]

attendee_id.description: Read the meeting as this attendee: adds `attendee_id`, `attendee_name`, `attendee_email`, `attendee_audio_id`, and `attendee_role`. When the attendee list is hidden and the attendee is not a host or presenter, `attendees` then holds only that attendee and the hosts and presenters.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

isInit.description: `1` starts a new instance of the meeting when none is running, and returns its `meeting-instance-id`. Only when you read as yourself with a token that can write. Allowed values: "1"

user.description: Extension of the user, such as `1001`. `~` means your own user. The meeting is read as this user.

When the meeting exists, access is checked against its owner, so you need list rights over the owner: any user in the owner\'s domain, or Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User for that domain. A meeting that does not exist is checked against the user in the path. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}/count]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

8c8f7fee58456b57.title: Get Domains Domain Users User Meetings Meeting ID Count

When the attendee list is hidden and the attendee is not a host or presenter, `attendees` holds only that attendee and the hosts and presenters.  Access is checked against the meeting\'s owner: any user in the owner\'s domain can read it, and Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User can read it in the domains they manage. When you are the user in the path and you are on the meeting, you are checked as yourself, so an attendee from another domain reads the meeting through its own path. `meeting-passcode` is shown only to the meeting\'s owner, its hosts, and Office Manager or higher for its domain. Everyone else gets it masked with asterisks; `include-secret=yes` does not change that.  The response differs from `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}`: the meeting is wrapped in a one-item `meeting` array, and five fields keep their legacy names: `name`, `type`, `capacity`, `status`, and `duration`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}/attendee/{attendee}]

Only the meeting\'s owner, its hosts, Office Manager for the meeting\'s domain, Reseller for its territory, and Super User can change it. Anyone else gets `403`. A host who is not the owner puts its own user in the path.  The meeting and the attendee come from the path; the attendee\'s meeting, ID, domain, and user cannot be changed. A change to `role` or a restriction is also written to the meeting\'s event log. `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}/attendee/{attendee}]

ca9d050fc16d4cab.description: Read recording playback token — Returns the token a client uses to play back the recording of one instance of the meeting in the path.  Requires a token for the user in the path; a Meeting Guest uses its `guest_` user. Super User can call it for any user. Only the meeting\'s owner, hosts, and attendees, and Office Manager or higher for its domain, get a token; a meeting open to anyone with its ID is not enough. A Meeting Guest gets one only for the meeting its token was issued for.  The token comes from the video service, and every field except `access_token` is passed through as it sends them. When the video service cannot issue it the answer is `502`, or `504` when it does not answer in time. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}/sfu]

Requires a token for the user in the path; a Meeting Guest uses its `guest_` user. Super User can call it for any user. You can join when you own the meeting, are on it, or are Office Manager or higher for its domain, or when the meeting is open to anyone with its ID and not locked. A Meeting Guest joins only the meeting its token was issued for.  The credentials come from the video service, and every field except `access_token` is passed through as it sends them. When the video service cannot issue them the answer is `502`, or `504` when it does not answer in time. Send no body. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}/sfu]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

c3a07f2817491e19.description: Read meeting by registration ID — Returns the meeting a registration link points to, so a registration page can show it before the guest registers.  Needs no token: the registration ID is the credential. Without a token, each client address can make 30 lookups a minute; more returns `429`. `meeting-passcode` is always masked here. — [GET /meetings/register/{registration_id}]

registration_id.description: Registration ID from the meeting's registration link: 8 letters or digits, such as `k4Rt9xQ2`. It is the meeting's `meeting-registration-id`.

c3a07f2817491e19.title: Read Meeting Registration ID

732503cf9f362158.description: Read meeting events — Returns the event log of one instance of a meeting, newest first: starts, joins, locks, and recording changes.  Only the meeting\'s hosts and attendees, its owner, and Office Manager or higher for its domain can use its event log. An attendee puts its own user in the path.  All matching events are returned unless you pass `limit`. With `group_by_instance=yes` the response changes shape: an array holding the instance as one object, with the meeting, its attendees, its registered guests, its events, and `record_url` when a recording was saved. That view holds `null` instead when the user in the path did not join the instance. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}/instance/{instance}/log]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

event.description: Only events of this kind, such as `part_join`.

get_start.description: `true` returns only the `meeting_start` event. Allowed values: "true"

group_by_instance.description: `yes` returns the instance summary described above instead of the event list. Allowed values: "yes"

instance.description: Instance ID of one occurrence of the meeting: 13 characters, such as `66e6f0a1b2c3d`. Each time a meeting starts it gets a new instance ID, returned as `meeting-instance-id`.

limit.description: Most events to return. Without it, every matching event is returned. Default: 100

offset.description: Events to skip before the first one returned, for paging.

target.description: Only events about this target, such as the user who joined.

time_start.description: Only events at or after this time, in the stored form (`YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`).

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

d035fd95975d1d72.description: Create domain video account — Creates an account for the domain at the video service and links the domain to it. Returns the video service\'s answer. The domain\'s video hostname is set from `subdomain` and the territory\'s video hostname suffix, and is applied to the domain shortly after the response.  Next, subscribe the account to a plan with **Create video subscription** or **Update domain video plans**. — [POST /domains/{domain}/video]

name.description: Display name of the account at the video service, usually the organization's name.

b0787a59d6347bd5.description: Create video host for user — Creates a video host for a user, so the user can host video conferences, and links it to the user.  Requires a token for this user. Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User can change the video host of any user in a domain they manage. Only Office Manager scope or higher can set `plan_slug` or `role`.  The domain must have a video account that is not suspended. Otherwise the request returns `400` with `Not Able to make request`. A user that does not exist returns `404`. Fields you leave out are filled from the user: `name` from the first and last name, `email` from the first email address, and the language from the user\'s language when the video portal supports it. f723308e9d6f762e.description: Create message session — Starts a message session by sending its first message, and answers `202`. Every scope reaches its own user. Office Manager reaches every user in its domain, Reseller the domains in its territory, and Super User every domain. You send as the user in the path.  The body is the one `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messages` takes, with the same `type` values and fields. The session is found from who takes part, so the same sender and recipients continue an existing session. To get the stored message and its `messagesession-id` in the answer, use `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messages` instead. For later messages, use `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions/{messagesession}/messages`.  A number that texted STOP to `from-number` does not get the message. When every recipient has opted out, the request answers `409`.  A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made right away can still show the old values. — [POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions]

ba55da71c6529a6c.description: Accept call queue conversation — Takes an SMS conversation that is waiting in a call queue and assigns it to the user, as its agent. Every scope reaches its own user. Office Manager reaches every user in its domain, Reseller the domains in its territory, and Super User every domain. `POST` does the same as `PUT`.  Send the queue\'s user ID in `messagesession-queue-termination`, as the session shows it. The session moves to `active` for this user, and `messagesession-agent-start-datetime` is set.  Below Office Manager, the user in the path must be an agent of the queue the conversation is waiting in, as the user itself or through one of its devices, or the user the conversation was already offered to. Anyone else gets `403`. Office Manager and above can assign the conversation to any user.  When another agent already has the conversation, or every copy is `complete`, the answer is `200` with a body whose `code` is `400` and `status` is `failure`, and nothing changes. Check `code` in the body, not only the HTTP status.  A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made right away can still show the old values. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions/{messagesession}/accept]

messagesession-queue-termination.description: The call queue the conversation is waiting in, as its user ID. Read it from the session's `messagesession-queue-termination`.

user.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

The platform adds the block on STOP and sets it `inactive` on START. While it is `active`, an SMS or MMS from `blocked-number` to `requesting-number` is refused. Use this to record an opt-out that reached you another way. The block is created `active`, and both numbers are normalized: spaces and punctuation are removed, and a 10-digit number gets `+1`. 6aebe5e95c82e5cb.description: List domain network test reports — Lists summaries of the network test reports stored for a domain: when each test ran, the network it ran from, and its speed and call-quality figures. The full report is not included; read one with `GET /domains/{domain}/networktests/{test_id}`.  Requires a token for the domain. Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, Site Manager, and Route Manager get only their own reports, and naming another user in `user` returns `403`. Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only get every report in the domain and can filter by `user`. A Reseller reaches only domains in its own territory.  Reports are sorted newest first by default. Page with `limit` and `offset`. The response has no total, and the `/count` and `/list` suffixes are not supported on this path. Reports are kept for 90 days after they are stored, then deleted automatically. To list one user\'s reports by path, use `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/networktests`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/networktests]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

end_date.description: Return only tests that ran at or before this time, in RFC 3339, such as `2026-09-30T23:59:59+00:00`. Epoch milliseconds are also accepted. A value that can't be parsed is ignored.

limit.description: Maximum number of reports to return. Defaults to 100. A value above 100 returns 100. Default: 100

offset.description: Number of reports to skip before the first one returned, for paging. Defaults to 0. Default: 0

sort_by.description: Field to sort by. `timestamp` is the run time. Any other value sorts by `timestamp`, so use `packet_loss` with an underscore. Allowed values: "timestamp", "mos", "packet_loss", "jitter", "rtt". Default: "timestamp"

sort_order.description: Sort direction. Any value other than `asc` sorts newest or highest first. Allowed values: "asc", "desc". Default: "desc"

start_date.description: Return only tests that ran at or after this time, in RFC 3339, such as `2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00`. Epoch milliseconds are also accepted. The run time is the report's `metadata.timestamp`, so a report without one is left out whenever a date filter is set. A value that can't be parsed is ignored.

user.description: Return only reports attributed to this user extension, such as `1001`. A `user@domain` value is matched on the extension. Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, Site Manager, and Route Manager may name only themselves; another user returns `403`.

6aebe5e95c82e5cb.title: List Networktests Domain

4269f871b98fed8c.description: Create network test report — Stores a network test report for a domain. The app\'s network test tool runs a speed test and a set of test calls, then posts the whole report here. This request only stores results; it does not run a test. The report is kept exactly as sent, and its summary figures are copied out for listing and sorting.  Requires a token for the domain. Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, Site Manager, and Route Manager can store reports only for themselves: `metadata.user`, when sent, must be your own extension. Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Reseller, and Super User can store a report for any user in the domain. A Reseller reaches only domains in its own territory. Read-only scopes can\'t store reports.  The report is attributed to `metadata.user`, or to you when it is left out. `metadata.reportId` becomes the report\'s `test_id` and must be unique across the platform; reusing one returns `409`. Each summary figure must fit its field in the summary, or the request returns `400` naming that field; the request schema gives the limits. The body can be up to 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes). Answers `202` when the report is stored; read it back with `GET /domains/{domain}/networktests/{test_id}`. Reports are kept for 90 days after they are stored, then deleted automatically.  To store a report under a user\'s path, use `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/networktests`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/networktests]

metadata.description: Who ran the test, where, and when. Required.

speedTest.description: Results of the speed test run before the test calls.

e82d32e7644e7b06.description: Read NMS status series — Returns one core server\'s status counters over a time window, grouped into time buckets for graphing. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.  The response has one shared `timestamps` array, and for each metric a `values` array aligned to it, plus summary figures: `current`, `first`, `min`, `max`, `avg`, `change-percent`, `samples`, and, for a counter, `total`.  **`hostname` is required.** Each core server keeps only its own status rows, so name the server to read. Use a `hostname` from `GET /nmsstatus/servers`. A request for another core server is passed to that server, and you get its answer.  **Gauges and counters.** A gauge, such as active sessions or a queue depth, is averaged per bucket unless you set `gauge-aggregate`, and its `current` is the latest raw sample. A counter, such as packets or SIP responses, only increases, so it is reported as a rate per second between consecutive buckets. A counter reset, such as a process restart, shows as `null` for that bucket, never as a negative rate. `GET /nmsstatus/metrics` says which metric is which.  **Window and buckets.** Use `range` for a window ending now, or `datetime-start` and `datetime-end` together for a fixed window. The explicit pair wins over `range`. Buckets are `1m`, `10m`, or `1h`; raw samples are never returned. Without `interval`, the bucket follows the range: `1m` up to `24h`, `10m` for `2d` and `7d`, and `1h` for `28d`. A series is limited to 2,000 buckets by default. An `interval` that would exceed it returns `400`, naming a coarser interval to use. A bucket with no samples is `null`, not `0`.  Times in the response use the offset of the `datetime-start` and `datetime-end` you send, or `+00:00`. Check `start-datetime` and `end-datetime` in the response: today a pair that cannot be read, or whose start is not before its end, is not always refused and can be replaced by a default window of about 61 days.  A series that ends now is cached for up to 60 seconds. — [GET /nmsstatus]

datetime-end.description: The end of a fixed window, in RFC 3339. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC is also accepted, and `YYYY-MM-DD` means the end of that day. It must be after `datetime-start`.

datetime-start.description: The start of a fixed window, in RFC 3339, such as `2026-09-01T14:20:00+00:00`. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC, and `YYYY-MM-DD` for midnight, are also accepted. Send it with `datetime-end`; one without the other returns `400`.

gauge-aggregate.description: How the samples of a gauge inside one bucket are combined. Defaults to `avg`. Counters ignore it. Allowed values: "avg", "max", "min". Default: "avg"

hostname.description: The core server to read, as listed by `GET /nmsstatus/servers`. Exact match: hostnames are lowercase in that list.

interval.description: The bucket width. Defaults by window: `1m` up to `24h`, `10m` for `2d` and `7d`, and `1h` for `28d`. A value that would return more than 2,000 buckets returns `400` naming a coarser interval. Allowed values: "1m", "10m", "1h"

metrics.description: The metrics to return, as metric IDs from `GET /nmsstatus/metrics` separated by commas. The column names are also accepted. Omit it, or send `*` or `all`, for every metric. An unknown ID returns `400` naming it.

range.description: The window, ending now. Defaults to `24h`. Ignored when `datetime-start` and `datetime-end` are sent. Allowed values: "1h", "3h", "6h", "12h", "24h", "2d", "7d", "28d". Default: "24h"

A provider with `allowed-cidrs` is returned only to callers from those addresses. Changes can take up to a minute to appear. Show a logo from `logo-url`. — [GET /oidc-providers/public]

domain.description: Return the providers for this domain and the ones offered to every domain. Omit it for every provider.

cad6956a530fb628.title: Get Oidcproviders Public

747613061bdcd1b5.description: Check OIDC provider settings — Checks OIDC provider settings without saving them, and returns the endpoints the discovery document names so you can fill them in. Requires Super User scope. The checks, in order:  - the discovery document can be fetched and is JSON - it names an issuer, an authorization endpoint, a token endpoint, and a key set - the key set can be fetched and holds keys - the identity provider accepts the client ID and secret, tested with a code it must refuse  The credential check runs only with a client ID, a secret, and a token endpoint. To check a saved provider without its secret, send `existing-provider-id`. When the stored secret is used, it is sent only to that provider\'s stored token endpoint, or, with none stored, to the one its unchanged discovery document names; a `token-endpoint` in the request is not used for it.  The discovery document, the key set, and the token endpoint must be `https` URLs on public addresses. Any other URL fails its check, and the credential check is then not run. A failed check is still a `200`, with `valid: false`. You can call this 15 times a minute. — [POST /oidc-providers/verify]

client-id.description: The client ID the identity provider issued for this platform.

client-secret.description: The client secret to check. Omit it with `existing-provider-id` to use the stored one.

discovery-url.description: The discovery document URL to check. Required.

existing-provider-id.description: The `id` of a stored provider. Its client ID and secret fill in whichever of `client-id` and `client-secret` you omit, so you can check a saved provider without typing the secret again.

jwks-uri.description: The JSON Web Key Set URL used to check ID token signatures. Overrides the discovery document.

token-endpoint.description: The token endpoint. Overrides the discovery document.

747613061bdcd1b5.title: Verify Oidcprovider

52e064b27ddd563a.description: Read OIDC provider logo — Returns a provider\'s uploaded logo as an image, so a login page can show it. No token is needed. The body is the image itself, PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG, or GIF, with a matching `Content-Type`. Browsers may cache it for an hour. — [GET /oidc-providers/{provider-id}/logo]
52e064b27ddd563a.title: Read Oidcprovider Logo

a27ebf2db257665e.description: Read phone number — Returns one phone number in the domain: where calls to it go and its SMS assignment, if any. Every user scope can read the numbers of its own domain. A Reseller reads the domains in its territory, and Super User and Super User Read Only read every domain.  A number that exists only as an SMS assignment comes back with `sms-only` set to `true` and no dial-rule fields. A number assigned to a different domain answers `404`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/phonenumbers/{phonenumber}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

phonenumber.description: The phone number, as stored: digits with the country code, for example `15555550123`. No spaces, dashes, or parentheses. A `+` is accepted only for a number that was stored with one.

a27ebf2db257665e.title: Get Phonenumber

3e0f4151cf3aaafe.description: Read phone — Reads one phone from any domain with its full detail: every line, the model\'s capabilities, line 1\'s registration, and the Endpoints server hostname. Super User, Reseller, and Office Manager read any phone they can see. Site Manager reads phones whose line 1 belongs to a user in its site. Basic User and the other user scopes read only their own phone, the one whose line 1 they own.  Per-line passwords are left out, and `device-provisioning-password` is masked except on your own phone. A Super User can send `include-secrets=yes` to get them in plaintext. The reveal is audit-logged.  Two fields describe a sidecar (expansion module): `device-provisioning-sidecar` is this phone\'s own setting, and `device-models-sidecar-support-enabled` is whether its model supports one. A phone\'s own configuration overrides are returned as `device-provisioning-overrides-blob`. The same value is also returned as `device-models-overrides-blob`, which is deprecated and will be removed in the next release. — [GET /phones/{mac}]

include-secrets.description: `yes` returns `device-provisioning-password` and the per-line passwords in plaintext. Super User only. Any other scope gets `403`. The reveal is audit-logged. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

mac.description: MAC address of the phone: 12 hex digits with no separators, such as `00005e005301`. Letter case does not matter.
