499ca3f9ee52bf6a.description: Read phone configuration file in domain — Returns the configuration file the Endpoints server builds for this phone, the file the phone downloads when it boots. The body is the file itself, `text/plain` or `text/xml` depending on the model. Errors are the usual JSON error body.  Passwords, tokens, and secrets in the file are masked (`ab********yz`), and so is any `user:password@` in a URL. Usernames, line keys, and every other setting are shown as built. A Super User can send `include-secrets=yes` to get the file unmasked. The reveal is audit-logged.  Some phones cannot be read yet, because building the file would change the phone\'s provisioning state. The request returns `409` instead:  - while the phone\'s one-time global password is armed (`global-one-time-pass` is `yes`), because reading the file would use it up - when the phone has no provisioning credentials yet and the server is set to generate them, because reading the file would create them  Both clear once the phone has provisioned.  Office Manager reads any phone in its domain, Reseller any phone in its territory, and Super User any phone. Site Manager reads phones whose line 1 belongs to a user in its site. Basic User and the other user scopes read only their own phone, the one whose line 1 they own. A phone you cannot see returns `404`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/phones/{mac}/config]

domain.description: Domain the phone belongs to, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A phone in another domain returns `404`.

file.description: A secondary file for this phone instead of its main configuration, such as `poly-00005e005301.cfg` (Polycom) or `00005e005301-directory.xml`. It must contain this phone's MAC address, use only letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-`, and end in `.cfg`, `.xml`, `.cnf`, `.txt`, `.conf`, or `.ini`, or have no extension. Anything else returns `400`. Leave it out for the main file.

include-secrets.description: `yes` returns the file with its credentials unmasked. Super User only. Any other scope gets `403`. The reveal is audit-logged. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

mac.description: MAC address of the phone: 12 hex digits with no separators, such as `00005e005301`.

0723e600b804a285.description: List brand defaults — Lists brand default rows: the per-brand vendor parameters that the Endpoints server (NDP) writes into device configuration files. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.  Each row is keyed by `default-brand`, `default-server` and `default-name`. Without `default-server`, only the `default` tier is returned; `default-server=all` returns every tier. Domain and site defaults share the storage but are never listed here: use `/domains/{domain}/provisioning-defaults`. Sending both `default-brand` and `default-name` reads one row: the response is a single object, or `404` when the row does not exist. Append `/count` for a total, or `/list` for the rows without their values. Reads come from the NDP database this API server is connected to.  To find which brands have defaults, use `/brand-defaults/brands`. — [GET /brand-defaults]

default-brand.description: Lowercase brand slug, such as `polycom`, or `*` for the general defaults. `domain` and `site` answer `400`.

default-name.description: Exact vendor parameter name. Combined with `default-brand`, the response is one object, or `404`.

default-server.description: The server tier to read. Omitted means `default`. `all` returns every tier.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return. Default `1000`. Default: 100

sort.description: `default-brand`, `default-server`, `default-name`, `default-description` or `default-timestamp-datetime`, each optionally followed by ` ASC` or ` DESC`. Separate several with commas. Default `default-brand,default-server,default-name`.

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

245ecd952bc3219d.description: Create brand default — Creates one brand default row and publishes it to every Endpoints server (NDP) over the service bus (SBUS). Requires Super User scope.  Send `default-brand`, `default-name` and `default-value`, and optionally `default-server` (default `default`) and `default-description`. A `202` means the change was published, not yet applied: each NDP server applies it when the event arrives. Add `synchronous=yes` to wait until this API server\'s NDP database shows it.  A row with the same brand, server tier and name answers `409`: pass `overwrite=yes` or use `PUT`. A named server that is not in `/phones/servers` answers `404`. The brands `domain` and `site` answer `400`: use `/domains/{domain}/provisioning-defaults`. — [POST /brand-defaults]

default-brand.description: Lowercase brand slug, such as `polycom`, or `*`. Required on `POST /brand-defaults`; on `POST /brand-defaults/{brand}` the path supplies it.

default-description.description: Free-text note about the row, up to 255 characters.

default-name.description: Vendor parameter name, up to 127 characters.

default-server.description: Server tier. Omitted means `default`. A named server must exist in `/phones/servers`, and `all` is refused.

default-value.description: Parameter value, stored as text. Numeric-looking values such as `0123` stay strings.

overwrite.description: `yes` replaces a row that already exists instead of answering `409`. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

synchronous.description: `yes` waits after publishing until this API server's NDP database shows the write, then answers `200` with a one-row report whose `default-applied` is `yes` or `no`. `no` means the write was not observed within the budget, not that it was rejected. Other NDP servers are not checked. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

synchronous-timeout.description: How long `synchronous=yes` waits, in milliseconds, 0 to 5000. Defaults to `2000`. A larger value returns `400`. Default: 2000

8a61df7986d2bf5d.description: List domain provisioning defaults — Lists the domain\'s provisioning options, one object per option, in the order the Endpoints server (NDP) reads them. Super User, Reseller and Office Manager can read and change these defaults. Super User Read Only, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager and Site Manager can read them. A Reseller is limited to domains in its territory, and other scopes to their own domain.  NDP stores these options as one `key="value"` string per domain and server tier; this resource splits it into options so each can be validated. Without `default-server`, the `default` tier is returned; `default-server=all` returns every tier. The result is what is stored for that tier, not the merged set a device receives. NDP applies site options first, then the domain row for the device\'s server, and uses the `default` tier only when that row is absent. A domain with no options on the tier returns an empty array. Add `option-name` to read one option. Append `/count` for a total, or `/list` for option names without values.  For the stored string, use `/domains/{domain}/provisioning-defaults/{server}/raw`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/provisioning-defaults]

default-server.description: The server tier to read. Omitted means `default`. `all` returns every tier.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

limit.description: Maximum rows to return. Default `1000`. Default: 100

option-name.description: Reads one option by name, for a name the path cannot carry. The response is then a single object, or `404` when the option is absent. With `default-server=all` it is an array with one row per tier that holds the option.

sort.description: `option-name` or `server`, optionally followed by ` ASC` or ` DESC`. Omitted keeps the stored order, which is the order NDP reads the options.

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

8a61df7986d2bf5d.title: List Domain Provisioning Defaults

17791269d818b3fd.description: Create domain provisioning option — Adds one provisioning option to the domain\'s row for `default-server` (default `default`), creating the row if needed, and publishes it to every Endpoints server (NDP) over the service bus (SBUS). Requires Super User, Reseller or Office Manager scope. A Reseller is limited to domains in its territory, and an Office Manager to its own domain.  Send `option-name` and `option-value`, and optionally `default-server` and `default-description`. The option is checked against NDP\'s own parser first, so a value the API accepts is one NDP will read. A `400` names the reason: a double quote, the literal text `SPACE`, `EQUALQUOTE`, `EQUALINVALUE` or `<null>`, a character NDP cannot parse, or a row that would exceed 2,000 options. A `202` means the change was published, not yet applied: each NDP server applies it when the event arrives. Add `synchronous=yes` to wait until this API server\'s NDP database shows it.  An option that already exists answers `409`: pass `overwrite=yes` or use `PUT`. A named server that is not in `/phones/servers` answers `404`. — [POST /domains/{domain}/provisioning-defaults]

default-description.description: Sets the row's description, whether the row is new or already exists.

Requires Super User scope. `202` means the change was published on the service bus (SBUS), not that every Endpoints server (NDP) has applied it yet.  The path names the server, so you cannot rename it, and a `name` in the body is ignored. Send a credential as an empty string to leave it unchanged. That way you can send back a row you read without its credentials. A non-blank `core-server-api-key` blanks the 4 OAuth fields and sets `status` to `APIkey enabled`. Otherwise `status` is ignored.  Sending back a masked value such as `ab****yz` returns `400`. An unknown server returns `404`. — [PUT /phones/servers/{server}]

address-location-description.description: Free-text location (`location`). This spelling is the one to send on a write.

backup_ok.description: May this server be chosen as a failover target. NDP treats NULL as `yes`. This raw column name is the one to send on a write. Allowed values: "yes", "no"

core-server-access-expires-datetime.description: When NDP's OAuth access token expires. Written by NDP. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-access-token.description: OAuth access token, written by NDP. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope.

core-server-active.description: Not used. Present in the table, read by nothing.

core-server-api-key.description: API key NDP uses instead of OAuth. When it is not blank, the 4 OAuth fields are blanked and `status` becomes `APIkey enabled`. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope.

core-server-ca.description: PEM CA certificate. Returned only with `include-certs=yes` and a Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

core-server-cert.description: PEM certificate. Returned only with `include-certs=yes` and a Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

core-server-client-id.description: OAuth client ID NDP uses. Defaults to `ndp`. Blanked when an API key is set. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-client-secret.description: OAuth client secret. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Blanked when an API key is set.

core-server-db-hostname.description: Host of this server's SiPbx database. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-hostname.description: SIP proxy FQDN handed to devices. Required on create. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-lat.description: Latitude, a decimal with 4 places, as a string.

core-server-lon.description: Longitude, a decimal with 4 places, as a string.

core-server-oauth-password.description: OAuth password. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Blanked when an API key is set.

core-server-oauth-username.description: OAuth user NDP logs in as. Blanked when an API key is set. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-pass.description: SiPbx database password. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Send an empty string on update to leave it unchanged.

core-server-port.description: SIP port, as a string. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-refresh-expires-datetime.description: When NDP's OAuth refresh token expires. Written by NDP. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-refresh-token.description: OAuth refresh token, written by NDP. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope.

core-server-sipbx-db.description: Name of this server's SiPbx database. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-tac-password.description: TAC endpoint password. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Send an empty string on update to leave it unchanged.

core-server-tac-url.description: TAC endpoint URL. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-tac-username.description: TAC endpoint user name. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-user.description: SiPbx database user. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

device-provisioning-core-server-api-fqdn.description: NsApi FQDN NDP calls for subscriber/device data (`ns_api_hostname`).

device-provisioning-core-server-postfix-.description: DNS suffix appended when building the device registrar (`postfix`).

7bbec70528f17bb5.description: Count processes — Returns the number of processes that `GET /processes` would return for the same filters. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.  Filter with `process-element-id`, `process-application`, `process-element-type`, `process-element-version`, `process-status`, `process-hostname`, `process-mac-address`, `process-ip-address`, and `process-domain-db`. Each filter is an exact match on the whole value. A blank value or `*` means no filter. Each filter also accepts its column-style name, such as `element_status` for `process-status`. A parameter the endpoint does not know is ignored, so a misspelled filter returns every row. `limit`, `start`, and `sort` are ignored.  For one server, use `GET /processes/{hostname}/count`. — [GET /processes/count]

process-element-id.description: Return only the process with this identifier, such as `sipbx`. Exact match. Also accepted as `element_id`. A blank value or `*` means no filter.

process-element-type.description: Return only processes of this type. Exact match. Also accepted as `element_type`. A blank value or `*` means no filter.

process-hostname.description: Return only processes on this server. Exact match. Also accepted as `hostname`. A blank value or `*` means no filter.

process-ip-address.description: Return only processes on the server with this internal IP address. Exact match. Also accepted as `ip_address`. A blank value or `*` means no filter.

01b1d10b6a5797fc.description: List selected process fields — Returns the same rows as `GET /processes`, reduced to the fields named in `fields`. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.  `limit` defaults to 1,000 here, not 100. Name fields by their response names, such as `process-hostname`, or their column-style names, such as `hostname`. The response always uses the response names. If no name in `fields` is a known field, or you send `*`, you get whole rows.  Filter with `process-element-id`, `process-application`, `process-element-type`, `process-element-version`, `process-status`, `process-hostname`, `process-mac-address`, `process-ip-address`, and `process-domain-db`. Each filter is an exact match on the whole value. A blank value or `*` means no filter. Each filter also accepts its column-style name, such as `element_status` for `process-status`. A parameter the endpoint does not know is ignored, so a misspelled filter returns every row.  Sort with `sort`: one or more column-style names, each optionally followed by `asc` or `desc`, separated by commas. A term without a direction sorts descending. Without `sort`, rows are ordered by hostname, then application. That order pages stably with `start` and `limit`. If you sort by something else, end the sort with `hostname asc` to keep paging stable.  For one server, use `GET /processes/{hostname}/list`. — [GET /processes/list]

Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.  Each server reports its own processes, and every server keeps the same inventory, so one request answers for the whole platform. A process is identified by `process-element-id` and `process-hostname`. A process that stops reporting keeps its last row. Check `process-status-update-time` to see how recent a row is.  Filter with `process-element-id`, `process-application`, `process-element-type`, `process-element-version`, `process-status`, `process-hostname`, `process-mac-address`, `process-ip-address`, and `process-domain-db`. Each filter is an exact match on the whole value. A blank value or `*` means no filter. Each filter also accepts its column-style name, such as `element_status` for `process-status`. Sort with `sort`: one or more column-style names, each optionally followed by `asc` or `desc`, separated by commas. A term without a direction sorts descending. Without `sort`, rows are ordered by hostname, then application. That order pages stably with `start` and `limit`. bcc3c2002a49c440.description: List domain push devices — Lists the devices registered for push in one domain, with their push service and owner, without the tokens.  Who can call it:  - Reseller reads domains in its territory. - Super User and Super User Read Only read any domain. - Scopes below Reseller read only their own registrations, and must add `user` with their own user (or `~`). Without it they get `403`.  `/list` returns the devices registered for push and their push service, never the tokens, so it is safe to show in an admin view. It runs the same read as the path without `/list`, with the same filters, paging, and access. `include-secrets` is ignored. `/count` is not supported for push registrations and returns `405`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/push/list]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

limit.description: Most registrations to return, 1 to 1,000. Defaults to 100. A value outside that range is raised or lowered to the nearest end. Default: 100

push-device.description: Only registrations for this device, by its full AOR, for example `sip:1001a@example.com`.

push-network.description: Only registrations on this push service. Push service the token belongs to: `firebase` (Firebase Cloud Messaging, Android), `apns` (Apple Push Notification service, iOS), `apns_chat` (an Apple token used for chat and messages only), or `pwa` (a web push subscription for a progressive web app). Any other value returns `400`. Allowed values: "firebase", "apns", "apns_chat", "pwa"

sort.description: Field to sort by, optionally followed by a space and `asc` or `desc`: `push-device`, `push-network`, `push-test`, `domain`, or `user`. Separate several fields with commas. Any other value returns `400`. Without it, the order is not defined.

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

user.description: Only devices registered by this user (extension). `~` means your own user. Below Reseller, your own user is required.

ce0bdf34204732e5.description: List domain push registrations — Lists the push registrations in one domain: each device token a mobile or web app registered, the device it notifies, and the user who owns it.  Who can call it:  - Reseller reads domains in its territory. - Super User and Super User Read Only read any domain. - Scopes below Reseller read only their own registrations, and must add `user` with their own user (or `~`). Without it they get `403`.  `push-device-token` is a credential. It is returned in clear only to the registration\'s own user. Every other caller gets it masked: a long token shows only its first 2 and last 2 characters. A Super User gets it in clear by adding `include-secrets=yes`, and every such read is logged.  Filters combine with AND. Paging uses `limit` (default 100, at most 1,000) and `start`. An empty result is `[]`. For the devices alone, without tokens, add `/list` to the path. — [GET /domains/{domain}/push]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

include-secrets.description: `yes` returns `push-device-token` in clear for every registration, and the read is logged. Super User only: any other scope that sends `yes` gets `403`. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

limit.description: Most registrations to return, 1 to 1,000. Defaults to 100. A value outside that range is raised or lowered to the nearest end. Default: 100

push-device.description: Only registrations for this device, by its full AOR, for example `sip:1001a@example.com`.

push-device-token.description: Only the registration with this exact push token. The match needs the real token, not a masked one.

push-network.description: Only registrations on this push service. Push service the token belongs to: `firebase` (Firebase Cloud Messaging, Android), `apns` (Apple Push Notification service, iOS), `apns_chat` (an Apple token used for chat and messages only), or `pwa` (a web push subscription for a progressive web app). 545bbc867a81a4ff.description: Update push registration — Changes the push service, sandbox setting, or device of an existing registration anywhere on the platform. The registration is found by `push-device-token`, which is required and cannot itself be changed. To replace a token, register the new one with `POST`, which removes the old one.  Who can call it:  - Super User updates any registration. - Reseller updates registrations in domains of its territory.  Every other scope gets `403`. Use `PUT /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/push` for your own.  The token must be a registration you can manage. A token that is not registered, or whose registration is outside your reach, returns `404`. The registration keeps its owner: `domain` and `user` in the body never move it. A new `push-device` must be another device of the same user.  Answers `202`. The change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made straight after it can still show the previous state. — [PUT /push]

bd4d2fd2b83066af.description: Unregister push device — Unregisters a device from push notifications anywhere on the platform. A mobile or web app calls it when the user logs out.  Who can call it:  - Every scope except the read-only ones can unregister a device it owns. Below Reseller, the body must name you: add `"user": "~"`, or your own `domain` and `user`. Without them the request gets `403`. - Reseller unregisters any device in a domain of its territory. - Super User unregisters any device.  Super User Read Only and Office Manager Read-Only get `403`.  What happens:  - `push-device` is required and must be an existing device within your reach. Any other answers `404` with `Device not found.` Below Reseller it must be your own device. - With `push-device-token`, that registration is removed. The token must be registered on that device, or the request returns `404`. A token that is not registered at all is treated as already removed. - Without `push-device-token`, the registrations stay and only the device\'s push delivery is switched off. - Push delivery is switched off for the device, except for an `apns_chat` token, which covers chat only and leaves call notifications on. - With `push-network` `pwa`, every web push registration of the user named by `domain` and `user` is removed instead, and `push-device` is not needed. Send both, or `"user": "~"` for your own; without them the request returns `400`. The answer is `{"response": "ok"}` with no `device`.  Answers `202` with `{"response": "ok", "device": ...}`. The change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made straight after it can still show the previous state. — [DELETE /push]

push-device-token.description: Token to remove. It must be registered on `push-device`. Without it the registrations stay, and only the device's push delivery is switched off.

push-network.description: Push service the token belongs to: `firebase` (Firebase Cloud Messaging, Android), `apns` (Apple Push Notification service, iOS), `apns_chat` (an Apple token used for chat and messages only), or `pwa` (a web push subscription for a progressive web app). `pwa` removes the user's web push registrations. `apns_chat` leaves call notifications on. Allowed values: "firebase", "apns", "apns_chat", "pwa"

4aa9422f39d794d0.description: Copy recording entries from server — Copies every entry on a source recording server that the recording server in the path does not have, in one request. The copies go to the path\'s recording server only, and every core server gets them.  Requires Super User scope.  An entry is identified by `case-id`, or by `device-aor` when it has no case ID. Only `device-aor`, `case-id`, `transcription`, and `sentiment` are copied. Entries already on the target are left alone unless `overwrite-existing` is `yes`, so running the copy again is safe and finishes a run that stopped early. An entry the API would refuse is not copied and is named in `failures`, and the rest still copy.  The copy runs in the background by default and returns `202` with a `job-id`. Poll it with `GET /recordings/servers/{recording-server-id}/entries/sync/{job-id}`. `synchronous=yes` waits and returns `200` with the result, unless there are too many entries to copy in one request: then it runs in the background and returns `202` with `downgraded-to-async`. `dry-run=yes` copies nothing and returns the counts.  Unknown recording server ids return `404` before anything starts. — [POST /recordings/servers/{recording-server-id}/entries/sync]

cfd8878c4713b536.description: Play recording — Streams the audio of a call recording. Open the `file-access-url` that a recording read returns; do not build the link yourself. The response is binary audio, `audio/wav` by default, or `audio/aac` or `audio/ogg` with `convert`. There is no example body.  No access token is needed. The link is its own credential: anyone who has it can play the recording until it expires, 180 minutes after it was created by default. Every link expires. Read the recording again for a new link.  Byte ranges are honored with `206 Partial Content`, so a media player can seek, unless `download` is set. Each play is recorded in the access log once, on the request for the start of the file.  A link whose signature does not match, that has expired, whose `time` is more than 5 minutes in the future, or whose `uid` names no active login, returns `403` with no body. A recording whose file is no longer on the Recording server or in remote storage returns `404` with no body. — [GET /recordings/play]

accel.description: The Recording server element that holds the file. Copy it from `file-access-url`.

auth.description: The signature over the other link parameters, as 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Copy it from `file-access-url`. Changing any signed parameter makes it fail with `403`.

calid.description: The SIP call ID of the recorded leg, URL-encoded. Copy it from `file-access-url`.

casid.description: The case the recording was made for, such as `1001@example.com`. Copy it from `file-access-url`.

cccid.description: The ID of the recording. Copy it from `file-access-url`.

convert.description: Transcodes the audio before sending it. `aac` answers `audio/aac` and `ogg` answers `audio/ogg`. `wav16`, `signed`, `signed_ffmpeg`, and `gsm` answer a converted WAV file as `audio/wav`. Any other value, `mp3` included, returns the original WAV file. If a conversion fails, the original file is sent. Allowed values: "aac", "ogg", "wav16", "signed", "signed_ffmpeg", "gsm"

download.description: Present with any value, even blank, the whole file is sent in one `200` response with no byte ranges. A value other than `false` also records the request as a download rather than a play. The file is always sent as an attachment.

stereo.description: `true` builds a two-channel file, one channel per side of the call, when the stored file is mono. `force` rebuilds it even when the stored file is already stereo. Works only while the raw call audio is still on the Recording server. A rebuilt file is sent whole, with no byte ranges. Allowed values: "true", "force"

time.description: When the link was created, in UTC, as `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS`. Copy it from `file-access-url`. The link expires 180 minutes later by default. A time more than 5 minutes in the future fails with `403`.

uid.description: The hostname of the server that created the link. Copy it from `file-access-url`. It does not name the person who reads the recording.

d59ba9dc96dec260.description: List rejected SIP requests — Returns the SIP requests that core servers rejected, newest first, one row per source address, method, and address of record. The reject log is platform-wide. It is not filtered by domain or territory, and it holds source addresses and addresses of record from every domain. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.  Each core server keeps its own reject log. Without `reject-hostname`, you get the rows of the core server that answers the request. The other core servers are asked too, but their rows are not included in the response today. To read every server, call `GET /rejectlog/{hostname}` for each core server. `reject-hostname` must name a core server of the platform; any other name returns `404` and no server is asked.  Filter with `reject-received-from`, `reject-method`, `reject-address-of-record`, `reject-user-agent`, `reject-result`, and `reject-cause`. Each is an exact match on the whole value.  `GET /rejectlog/count` returns `{"total": N}` for the same filters, counted on the answering core server only. — [GET /rejectlog]

limit.description: The most rows to return. Defaults to 100. There is no upper limit. Default: 100

reject-action.description: Not applied today: every action is returned whatever you send. Filter the response on `reject-action` instead.

reject-address-of-record.description: Return only requests for this address of record. Exact match. Also accepted as `aor`.

reject-cause.description: Return only requests with this cause. Exact match. Also accepted as `cause`.

reject-hostname.description: Read only this core server, the same as `GET /rejectlog/{hostname}`. This is not a filter on the rows: it selects the server to ask. Also accepted as `hostname`. A name that is not a core server of the platform returns `404`. A core server that does not answer returns an empty array.

reject-method.description: Return only requests with this SIP method, such as `REGISTER`. Exact match. Also accepted as `method`.

reject-received-from.description: Return only requests from this source address. Exact match. Also accepted as `rcv_from`.

reject-result.description: Return only requests with this result. Exact match. Also accepted as `result`.

reject-user-agent.description: Return only requests with this `User-Agent`. Exact match. Also accepted as `user_agent`.

sort.description: The sort order: one or more of `rcv_from`, `hostname`, `method`, `aor`, `rcv_time`, `user_agent`, `contact`, `result`, `action`, `cause`, `count`, and `rate`, each optionally followed by a space and `asc` or `desc`, separated by commas. The response names are not accepted, and any other name fails the request. Defaults to `rcv_time desc`. Without a hostname, rows are always returned newest first, whatever `sort` says.

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

Rows use the connection field names without the SIP fields: no address, credentials, translations, limits, or call counters. `connection-id` is the key for the other route-profile endpoints. Filter with `connection-usage-role`, and page with `start` and `limit`, 100 rows by default. Use `/domains/{domain}/routeprofiles/count` for a total, and `/domains/{domain}/routeprofiles/list` for the identity fields only.  A domain that does not exist returns `404`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/routeprofiles]

b3f5205a3819ec91.description: Create domain route profile — Creates a route profile in the domain, with its route and route connections. Requires Office Manager, Route Manager, or Call Center Supervisor scope in the domain, Reseller scope in its territory, or Super User scope. The API publishes the route on the service bus (SBUS) `NmsRoute` channel and then the profile on `connection_events`, and each is applied when its event arrives, so `202` means published, not applied.  `connection-orig-match-pattern` is required and is the profile\'s key. It must be unique across the platform, not only the domain: a value any connection already uses returns `409`. The API sets the address itself: the domain in capitals, `_`, and the part of `connection-orig-match-pattern` after any `@`, in angle brackets, such as `<EXAMPLE.COM_tollfree>`. The name inside the brackets is the route\'s `route-destination-match-pattern`. `connection-connectivity-type` is always `route_profile`.  Put the route in `call-routing`. `route-method` defaults to `percentage`, `route-is-enabled` to `yes`, and `description` to the profile\'s `description`. Each entry in `routecon` needs `route-connection-translation-destination-host`. `route-connection-ordinal-index` is optional: an entry without one takes the next free index. The whole of `call-routing` is checked before anything is published, so a missing host, or an index that is repeated or not a positive whole number, returns `400` with nothing created. Without `call-routing`, no route is created.  A failed create leaves nothing behind, so it is always safe to retry. Send `synchronous=yes`, in the body or the query string, to wait up to 2 seconds for the change to be applied. You then get `200` with the profile. If it is not applied in time, you get the usual `202` and the write still completes. — [POST /domains/{domain}/routeprofiles]

call-routing.description: The route of a route profile, as sent on create or update.

connection-orig-match-pattern.description: The profile's identifier. Unique across the platform. Also sets the route name.

description.description: Free-text description of the profile.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

150b42f129806daf.description: Update domain route profile — Changes a route profile\'s `description`, or its route and route connections. An id that names no route profile returns `404`, and so does the id of an ordinary connection. — [GET /routeprofiles/{connection-id}]

e91015149d3fc7b2.description: Update route profile — Changes a route profile by `connection-id`, without naming its domain. Requires Super User or Reseller scope. A Reseller can change only a profile in its own territory; other scopes use `PUT /domains/{domain}/routeprofiles/{connection-id}`. The API publishes on the service bus (SBUS) `connection_events` channel and, for route changes, `NmsRoute`, so `202` means published, not applied.  An id outside your territory, or the id of an ordinary connection, returns `404`. Send only what changes. `call-routing` updates the route this profile already points at, whatever address the body names. An omitted `route-method`, `route-is-enabled`, or `description` keeps its stored value. Each `routecon` entry is written by `route-connection-ordinal-index`, and an entry without an index is added after the stored ones. Connections you leave out are kept; remove one with `DELETE /routes/{route-id}/routecon/{index}`. `call-routing` is checked before anything is published, as on create. `synchronous` is ignored. — [PUT /routeprofiles/{connection-id}]

call-routing.description: The route of a route profile, as sent on create or update.

connection-id.description: The route profile's `connection-id`, as a list returns it: base64url, without padding, of `connection-orig-match-pattern`. The raw `connection-orig-match-pattern` is also accepted.

description.description: Free-text description of the profile.

e91015149d3fc7b2.title: Update Route Profile

The API publishes on the service bus (SBUS) `connection_events` and `NmsRoute` channels, so `202` means published, not applied.  An id outside your domain or territory, or the id of an ordinary connection, returns `404`. — [DELETE /routeprofiles/{connection-id}]

A route with no connections, or a `route-id` that names no route, returns `[]`. Page with `start` and `limit`, 100 rows by default. `/routes/{route-id}/routecon/count` counts this route\'s connections only. To read connections across every route, use `GET /routecon`. — [GET /routes/{route-id}/routecon]

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page. Default: 100

route-id.description: The route's `route-id`, as `GET /routes` returns it. It is base64url, without padding, of the route's `route-destination-match-pattern` when the source, class, and hostname are all `*`. Otherwise it encodes all 4 values joined by `||`.

867b2bc7fa680075.description: Create route connection — Adds a route connection, one next hop, to the route that `route-id` names. Requires Super User scope. Other scopes, Reseller included, get `403`. The API publishes the change on the service bus (SBUS) `NmsRoute` channel, and core applies it when the event arrives, so `202` means published, not applied.  `route-connection-translation-destination-host` is required and cannot be blank. `route-connection-ordinal-index` defaults to one more than the route\'s highest index, so the first connection gets `1`. `route-connection-translation-destination-user` defaults to `[*]`. The 4 match fields come from `route-id`, and any in the body are ignored. The API does not check that the route exists or that the index is free.  Send `synchronous=yes`, in the body or the query string, to wait up to 2 seconds for the change to be applied. You then get `200` with every connection of the route. If it is not applied in time, you get the usual `202` and the write still completes. — [POST /routes/{route-id}/routecon]

route-connection-integer-percentage.description: Share of calls, in percent, for this connection when `route-method` is `percentage`. Default: 50

route-connection-ordinal-index.description: Position of this connection in the route, from `1`. With `route-method` `fixed`, connections are tried in this order. On `POST /routes/{route-id}/routecon` it defaults to one more than the highest index. Default: 1

Translation applied to the destination user when the call goes to this connection. Defaults to `[*]`. Default: "[*]"

route-match-server-hostname.description: Read only. The parent route's core server hostname. Default: "*"

route-source-match-pattern.description: Read only. The parent route's source pattern. Default: "*"

synchronous.description: `yes` waits until the change is applied before answering. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

af871711fd2997e1.description: Update route — Changes a route\'s `description`, `route-method`, or `route-is-enabled`. Requires Super User scope. Other scopes, Reseller included, get `403`. The API publishes the change on the service bus (SBUS) `NmsRoute` channel, and core applies it when the event arrives, so `202` means published, not applied.  `route-id` identifies the route. Its 4 match fields come from the path, and any in the body are ignored, so this cannot move a route to another pattern. To do that, create the new route and its connections, then delete the old one. A `route-id` that names no route returns `404`.  Send `synchronous=yes`, in the body or the query string, to wait up to 2 seconds for the change to be applied. You then get `200` with the route. If it is not applied in time, you get the usual `202` and the write still completes. — [PUT /routes/{route-id}]

route-class.description: Call class the route applies to. `*`, the default, matches every class. Part of the route's identity. Default: "*"

route-destination-match-pattern.description: Destination pattern a call must match, such as `sip:1800*@*`. Required on create. Part of the route's identity.

route-id.description: Read only. Key for `PUT` and `DELETE /routes/{route-id}` and the route's connections: base64url, without padding, of `route-destination-match-pattern` when the other 3 match fields are `*`, otherwise of all 4 joined by `||`.

route-match-server-hostname.description: Core server hostname the route is limited to, such as `core1.example.com`. `*`, the default, applies it on every core server. Part of the route's identity. Default: "*"

route-method.description: How the route picks a connection: `fixed` tries them in `route-connection-ordinal-index` order, `cost` picks the lowest `route-connection-integer-cost`, and `percentage` splits calls by `route-connection-integer-percentage`. Defaults to `fixed`. Allowed values: "fixed", "cost", "percentage"

route-source-match-pattern.description: Source pattern a call must match. `*`, the default, matches every caller. Part of the route's identity. Default: "*"

synchronous.description: `yes` waits until the change is applied before answering. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

territory.description: Super User only: returns only the codes of the domains in this reseller's territory. Ignored when `domain` names a domain. Resellers always get their own territory.

863b7d5178667530.title: List Service Codes

0c90c2ca870a6bc8.description: Create service code — Creates a service code for the domain in `domain`, or a system-wide code that every domain shares when `domain` is `*`. `domain` is required: a write without it returns `400`. Send `"domain": "*"` to address a system-wide code, which needs Super User scope.  Requires Office Manager scope or above for your own domain, Reseller scope for the domains in your territory, or Super User scope for any domain. System-wide codes, with `domain` `*`, are shared by every domain. Only Super User scope can create, change, or delete them. Any other scope gets `403`.  `srvcode-code` is required. `srvcode-item` defaults to `*`. Codes that start with `system-` are the platform\'s own, such as `system-aa` and `system-queue`. Name your own codes without that prefix. Use only letters, digits, and `* # . - _` in `srvcode-code` and `srvcode-item`, because the paths that read, change, and delete a code accept nothing else.  A code with the same type, code, and domain returns `409`. Change it with `PUT /servicecode/{type}/{code}` instead. A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after. For a domain\'s own codes, `POST /domains/{domain}/servicecode` puts the domain in the path. — [POST /servicecode]

domain.description: The domain the code is for, or `*` for a system-wide code that every domain shares. `~` means the domain of your token. `domain` is required: a write without it returns `400`. Send `"domain": "*"` to address a system-wide code, which needs Super User scope. Up to 63 characters.

srvcode-code.description: The service code. A user's `service-code` field names it. Codes that start with `system-` are the platform's own. 1 to 31 characters: letters, digits, and `* # . - _`.

srvcode-description.description: A label for the code, shown in admin screens. Up to 255 characters.

srvcode-item.description: The type of the code: a grouping key you choose when you create it. `*`, the default, means no particular type. 1 to 31 characters: letters, digits, and `* # . - _`. Default: "*"

0c90c2ca870a6bc8.title: Create Service Code

b02546c35f3567d6.description: Read service code — Returns one service code, addressed by its type and code, as an object. Send `domain` to read that domain\'s code.  Requires Office Manager scope or above for your own domain, Reseller scope for the domains in your territory, or Super User scope for any domain. The read-only versions of those scopes can read. Below Reseller scope, `domain` is required: without it the answer is `403`.  Without `domain`, a Super User gets a matching code from any domain and a Reseller one from its territory. Which one is not defined. To read one domain\'s code exactly, use `GET /domains/{domain}/servicecode/{type}/{code}`.  Returns `404` when no code matches. — [GET /servicecode/{type}/{code}]

code.description: The service code (`srvcode-code`). Send `*` as `%2A` and `#` as `%23`, so `*72` is `%2A72`.

domain.description: The domain whose code to read. `~` means the domain of your token. Left out or `*`, any domain matches, which only Super User and Reseller scopes can ask for.

fields.description: A comma-separated list of the fields to return, such as `srvcode-code,srvcode-description`. Names the API does not know are ignored. If none is known, every field is returned.

full.description: `yes`, `true`, or `1` also matches the system-wide code with the same type and code. When both exist, which one is returned is not defined. Allowed values: "yes", "no", "true", "false", "1", "0"

type.description: The type of the code (`srvcode-item`). It is a grouping key that you choose when you create the code. The default is `*`. Send `*` as `%2A` and `#` as `%23`.

b02546c35f3567d6.title: Read Service Code

b1f8e16b429ca45b.description: Update service code — Changes the description of one service code. The path names the type and code, and `domain` in the body names the domain. Send `domain` as `*` to change a system-wide code. `domain` is required: a write without it returns `400`. Send `"domain": "*"` to address a system-wide code, which needs Super User scope.  Requires Office Manager scope or above for your own domain, Reseller scope for the domains in your territory, or Super User scope for any domain. System-wide codes, with `domain` `*`, are shared by every domain. Only Super User scope can create, change, or delete them. Any other scope gets `403`.  `srvcode-item` and `srvcode-code` in the body are optional. If you send them, they must match the path, or the answer is `400`. `domain` is read from the body, never from the query string.  A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after. The API does not check that the code exists first. To change a domain\'s own code, `PUT /domains/{domain}/servicecode/{type}/{code}` puts the domain in the path. — [PUT /servicecode/{type}/{code}]

code.description: The service code (`srvcode-code`). Send `*` as `%2A` and `#` as `%23`, so `*72` is `%2A72`.

domain.description: The domain of the code to change, or `*` for a system-wide code. `~` means the domain of your token. `domain` is required: a write without it returns `400`. Send `"domain": "*"` to address a system-wide code, which needs Super User scope. Read from the body only.

srvcode-code.description: Optional. If sent, it must equal `{code}` in the path, or the answer is `400`.

srvcode-description.description: The new label for the code. Up to 255 characters.

srvcode-item.description: Optional. If sent, it must equal `{type}` in the path, or the answer is `400`.

type.description: The type of the code (`srvcode-item`). It is a grouping key that you choose when you create the code. The default is `*`. Send `*` as `%2A` and `#` as `%23`.

b1f8e16b429ca45b.title: Update Service Code

d2fbd0216832e7fc.description: Delete service code — Deletes one service code. The path names the type and code, and `domain` in the body names the domain. Send `domain` as `*` to delete a system-wide code. `domain` is required: a write without it returns `400`. Send `"domain": "*"` to address a system-wide code, which needs Super User scope.  Requires Office Manager scope or above for your own domain, Reseller scope for the domains in your territory, or Super User scope for any domain. System-wide codes, with `domain` `*`, are shared by every domain. Only Super User scope can create, change, or delete them. Any other scope gets `403`.  `domain` is read from the body, never from the query string. `srvcode-description` is ignored if you send it.  A `202` means the delete is accepted and applied shortly after. Deleting a code that does not exist is accepted too. Users whose `service-code` names the deleted code keep that value: `GET /domains/{domain}/billing` reports how many users carry each code. To delete a domain\'s own code, `DELETE /domains/{domain}/servicecode/{type}/{code}` needs no body. — [DELETE /servicecode/{type}/{code}]

code.description: The service code (`srvcode-code`). Send `*` as `%2A` and `#` as `%23`, so `*72` is `%2A72`.

domain.description: The domain of the code to delete, or `*` for a system-wide code. `~` means the domain of your token. `domain` is required: a write without it returns `400`. Send `"domain": "*"` to address a system-wide code, which needs Super User scope. Read from the body only.

type.description: The type of the code (`srvcode-item`). It is a grouping key that you choose when you create the code. The default is `*`. Send `*` as `%2A` and `#` as `%23`.

d2fbd0216832e7fc.title: Delete Service Code

2d745dfa668a5113.description: List services on server — Lists every unit in the service catalog with its live state on one server, read from systemd in a single call.  Requires Super User scope.  A catalog unit that is not installed on the server is still listed, with `installed: false` and empty state fields, so every server answers the same set of units. A unit installed under an alias, such as `mysql` for `mariadb`, is reported under the catalog name with `resolved-unit` naming what systemd loaded.  An `active` unit is not proof of health: every platform daemon restarts itself after a crash, so check `restart-count` too. — [GET /services/{hostname}]

hostname.description: The cluster server to act on, as the hostname it is listed under in `GET /apt/servers`. A name not in that list, a malformed name, or a bare IP address is refused with `400` before anything runs. When it names a server other than the one you called, the request is forwarded there with your token.

2d745dfa668a5113.title: List Services

177671a0f57dc8ac.description: List controllable services — Lists every systemd unit the service routes may control, with the actions allowed for each.  Requires Super User scope.  The list is fixed in the apt manager release and is the same on every server, so this call takes no `hostname` and asks no server. A unit that is not listed is refused with `400` on every other `/services` route. Use `actions` and `allow-stop` to decide which controls to offer; `GET /services/{hostname}` tells you which units are installed on a server. — [GET /services/catalog]
177671a0f57dc8ac.title: List Service Catalog

08785fc5cec599ff.description: Read service status — Returns the live state of one unit on one server, read from systemd.  Requires Super User scope.  Poll this after a start or restart: a `200` from the action only means the process was spawned. The unit is up when `active-state` is `active`, `sub-state` is `running`, and `restart-count` has stopped climbing.  A unit in the catalog that is not installed on the server answers `404` with the package that provides it. A unit that is not in the catalog answers `400`. — [GET /services/{hostname}/{unit}]

hostname.description: The cluster server to act on, as the hostname it is listed under in `GET /apt/servers`. A name not in that list, a malformed name, or a bare IP address is refused with `400` before anything runs. When it names a server other than the one you called, the request is forwarded there with your token.

unit.description: The systemd unit, without the `.service` suffix. It must be one of the units `GET /services/catalog` lists: `netsapiens_nms`, `netsapiens_sbus`, `netsapiens_ncs`, `netsapiens_nfr`, `netsapiens_nmc`, `netsapiens_licf`, `netsapiens-nqs`, `netsapiens-insight-agent`, `netsapiens-ipaware`, `netsapiens-ipaware-ipset`, `nsnode`, `nscdr`, `nsbackup`, `nscertmanager`, `nsgeo`, `nsapmax`, `apache2`, `mariadb`, `php8.5-fpm`, `php7.4-fpm`, `memcached`, `redis-server`. The alias `mysql` is accepted for `mariadb`. Any other name is refused with `400`.

08785fc5cec599ff.title: Read Service

4db2e3a36f8937ef.description: Reload unit files on server — Runs `systemctl daemon-reload` on one server, so systemd reads every changed unit file again. It restarts nothing.  Requires Super User scope.  You rarely need it: a start, stop or restart reloads first when its own unit file has changed. Use it to clear `need-daemon-reload` on every unit at once, typically after an upgrade that replaced several unit files.  `reloaded-units` lists the catalog units that were out of date; an empty list means the call changed nothing. `still-stale` should be empty afterwards.  It is not blocked by a running apt operation, because package installs run a daemon-reload themselves. Only one daemon-reload runs on a server at a time; a second answers `409`. — [POST /services/{hostname}/daemon-reload]

hostname.description: The cluster server to act on, as the hostname it is listed under in `GET /apt/servers`. A name not in that list, a malformed name, or a bare IP address is refused with `400` before anything runs. When it names a server other than the one you called, the request is forwarded there with your token.

ticket.description: Ticket number to record with this change in the audit log

ticket_number.description: Same as `ticket`, which wins when both are sent

4db2e3a36f8937ef.title: Reload Service Units

bb9b0904d16c008c.description: Start, stop, or restart service — Starts, stops or restarts one systemd unit on one server and waits for systemctl to finish, up to 90 seconds.  Requires Super User scope.  A `200` means systemctl ran. Check `success` and `exit-code`: a unit that fails to start is a `200` with `success: false`. Every platform daemon is a `simple` unit, so systemd answers as soon as the process is spawned, before it is ready. The response flags that with `ready-unknown: true`; poll `GET /services/{hostname}/{unit}` to confirm the unit stayed up.  When the unit file changed on disk since systemd read it, the server reloads it first and reports `daemon-reloaded: true`, so the action uses the current file.  An `apache2` restart is scheduled a few seconds later and answered `202`, because the API itself is served through `apache2`. `apache2` cannot be stopped: that is a `403`, because it could then only be started again from the server console.  The action is refused with `409` while an apt operation is running on the server, while another action on the same unit is running, or when the unit is masked. Retry once the apt operation or action finishes, or unmask the unit.  > **Warning:** a stop or restart of `netsapiens_nms`, `netsapiens_ncs` or `netsapiens_licf` drops the calls on that server immediately. This route does not check for active calls, unlike the package upgrade scripts. — [POST /services/{hostname}/{unit}/{action}]

action.description: What to do to the unit. `stop` is refused for a unit whose catalog entry has `allow-stop: false`. Allowed values: "start", "stop", "restart"

hostname.description: The cluster server to act on, as the hostname it is listed under in `GET /apt/servers`. A name not in that list, a malformed name, or a bare IP address is refused with `400` before anything runs. When it names a server other than the one you called, the request is forwarded there with your token.

ticket.description: Ticket number to record with this change in the audit log

ticket_number.description: Same as `ticket`, which wins when both are sent

unit.description: The systemd unit, without the `.service` suffix. It must be one of the units `GET /services/catalog` lists: `netsapiens_nms`, `netsapiens_sbus`, `netsapiens_ncs`, `netsapiens_nfr`, `netsapiens_nmc`, `netsapiens_licf`, `netsapiens-nqs`, `netsapiens-insight-agent`, `netsapiens-ipaware`, `netsapiens-ipaware-ipset`, `nsnode`, `nscdr`, `nsbackup`, `nscertmanager`, `nsgeo`, `nsapmax`, `apache2`, `mariadb`, `php8.5-fpm`, `php7.4-fpm`, `memcached`, `redis-server`. The alias `mysql` is accepted for `mariadb`. Any other name is refused with `400`.

bb9b0904d16c008c.title: Control Service

8915a96aa952299a.description: Delete site — Deletes a site: the system extension that holds its settings, and the records that extension owns.  Requires Office Manager in the domain, Reseller for a domain in your territory, or Super User. Site Manager, Basic User, Super User Read Only, and every other scope get `403`.  A site that still has members is refused with `409`, and the message gives how many. Members are the users, call queues, and other extensions filed under the site. Move them first, or send `force=yes` to clear the site from every member and then delete it. Members keep their own settings, including values they copied from the site when they were created, and their devices are not touched.  Deleting the site also removes what its own extension owns: its devices, time frames, emergency addresses, contacts, conferences, recording settings, and CDR schedules, among other records. Phone numbers routed to the site\'s extension return to inventory. The site\'s group chat is archived last, after everything else succeeds. The site\'s provisioning defaults are not removed.  A `202` means the change was published over the service bus (SBUS), not yet applied. Each core server applies it when the event arrives, so a read straight after the `202` can still show the old state. `DELETE /domains/{domain}/sites`, with no name in the path, returns `405`. — [DELETE /domains/{domain}/sites/{site}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

force.description: `yes` clears the site from every member, however many, then deletes it. `no`, the default, refuses a site that has members with `409`. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

site.description: Site name, exactly as returned in `user` by `GET /domains/{domain}/sites`. Letters, digits, spaces, and `.`, `-`, `_`, `'`, `*`. Names are matched exactly.

8915a96aa952299a.title: Delete Site

2dc7555b485b06e1.description: List SMS carriers — Returns the platform\'s SMS carriers: the builtin carriers (`bandwidth`, `onvoy`, `inteliquent`, `messagemedia`, `impact`, `brightlink`, `thinq`, `voipinno`, and `teli`) followed by the custom carriers. Takes no filters and is not paged.  Super User and Super User Read Only get every carrier in full. `auth` and every value in `custom-outbound-json-fields` are masked: the first 2 and last 2 characters, with asterisks between; a value of 8 characters or fewer is all asterisks. A Super User can send `include-secret=yes` to read them whole; the read is recorded, and any other scope that sends it gets `403`. Every other scope that can read carriers, Basic User included, gets the portal view: enabled carriers only, each reduced to `carrier`, `mms-capable`, and `group-mms-capable`.  `mms-capable` and `group-mms-capable` come from the platform\'s MMS carrier lists, not from the carrier record. — [GET /smscarriers]

include-secret.description: `yes` returns `auth` and the `custom-outbound-json-fields` values unmasked. Super User only; any other scope gets `403`. Each such read is recorded. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

2dc7555b485b06e1.title: List SMS Carriers

a889a10eb20e9bf5.description: Create custom SMS carrier — Adds a custom SMS carrier: the outbound request the platform sends to the carrier, and how to read the carrier\'s inbound webhook. Requires Super User scope.  Send `carrier` and `url`. The name must not be a builtin carrier (`bandwidth`, `onvoy`, `inteliquent`, `messagemedia`, `impact`, `brightlink`, `thinq`, `voipinno`, and `teli`), `twillio`, `nullResponseFields`, or an existing custom carrier. Fields the carrier record does not have, and the read-only `type`, `enabled`, `mms-capable`, and `group-mms-capable`, are ignored, as is a masked `auth` copied from a read. So a row from `GET /smscarriers` can be sent back as it is.  Put the carrier credential in `auth`, or, for a carrier that takes it in the body, in `custom-outbound-json-fields`. Both read back masked. A masked value in `custom-outbound-json-fields` is refused with `400`: send the real value.  The change is saved to the configuration of the server that answers the request, and is in effect when the response arrives. Other servers in the cluster do not receive it. — [POST /smscarriers]
a889a10eb20e9bf5.title: Create SMS Carrier

4935d2884f89c819.description: Read SMS carrier — Returns one SMS carrier, builtin or custom. The name is matched exactly, including case.  Super User and Super User Read Only get every carrier in full. `auth` and every value in `custom-outbound-json-fields` are masked: the first 2 and last 2 characters, with asterisks between; a value of 8 characters or fewer is all asterisks. A Super User can send `include-secret=yes` to read them whole; the read is recorded, and any other scope that sends it gets `403`. Every other scope that can read carriers, Basic User included, gets the portal view: enabled carriers only, each reduced to `carrier`, `mms-capable`, and `group-mms-capable`. — [GET /smscarriers/{carrier}]

carrier.description: Carrier name: a builtin name such as `bandwidth`, or a custom carrier's name. Letters, digits, `-`, and `_`.

include-secret.description: `yes` returns `auth` and the `custom-outbound-json-fields` values unmasked. Super User only; any other scope gets `403`. Each such read is recorded. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

4935d2884f89c819.title: Read SMS Carrier

f72fc0026e0c0c6e.description: Update SMS carrier — Changes an SMS carrier. Requires Super User scope.  - **Builtin carrier.** Send `enabled`; every other field is ignored. `enabled` only hides or shows the carrier in the portal. It does not change how messages are sent. The builtin name is matched without regard to case. - **Custom carrier.** Send the fields to change; fields you leave out keep their values. An empty string removes a field. `custom-outbound-json-fields` replaces the whole map. `enabled` is ignored: a custom carrier is always enabled.  Fields the carrier record does not have, the read-only fields, and a masked `auth` copied from a read are ignored. Put the carrier credential in `auth`, or, for a carrier that takes it in the body, in `custom-outbound-json-fields`. Both read back masked. In `custom-outbound-json-fields`, an entry sent back exactly as a read masked it keeps its stored value; any other masked entry is refused with `400`.  The change is saved to the configuration of the server that answers the request, and is in effect when the response arrives. Other servers in the cluster do not receive it. — [PUT /smscarriers/{carrier}]

carrier.description: Carrier name: a builtin name such as `bandwidth`, or a custom carrier's name. Letters, digits, `-`, and `_`.

f72fc0026e0c0c6e.title: Update SMS Carrier

751d449e8faa7478.description: Delete custom SMS carrier — Deletes a custom SMS carrier and every field it has. Requires Super User scope. A builtin carrier cannot be deleted: hide it with `PUT /smscarriers/{carrier}` and `enabled` set to `false`.  The change is saved to the configuration of the server that answers the request, and is in effect when the response arrives. Other servers in the cluster do not receive it. — [DELETE /smscarriers/{carrier}]

carrier.description: Carrier name: a builtin name such as `bandwidth`, or a custom carrier's name. Letters, digits, `-`, and `_`.

751d449e8faa7478.title: Delete SMS Carrier

3b7e4f5c320da188.description: List device profiles — A device profile describes one phone or sidecar model for the phone template builder: its picture, where each button sits on it, how many button pages it has, and which sidecars it takes. Device profiles are shared by every domain. Each row includes its buttons and an `image` object. The picture itself is served by `GET /deviceprofiles/image/{brand}/{model}`, which needs no token.  Filter with `device-models-brand`, `device-models-model`, and `device-models-type`. Each is an exact match. Page with `start` and `limit`: `limit` defaults to `100`. `GET /deviceprofiles/count` returns the total.  Any scope that can read phone configurations can read device profiles. — [GET /deviceprofiles]

brand.description: Returns only this brand. Exact match.

device_type.description: Returns only phones (`phone`) or only sidecars (`sidecar`). Allowed values: "phone", "sidecar"

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page. Default: 100

model.description: Returns only this model. Exact match.

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

3b7e4f5c320da188.title: Get Deviceprofiles

3123d15349441e67.description: Count device profiles — Returns the number of device profiles on the platform. It always counts every profile: filters do not apply.  Any scope that can read device profiles can count them. — [GET /deviceprofiles/count]
3123d15349441e67.title: Get Deviceprofiles Count

04f84d3f2725e7ea.description: Read device profile — Returns the device profile for one brand and model, with its buttons and `image` object. It adds `devicemodel`: the matching device model, with the button types and features the model supports. Use those values for `phoneconfiguration-button-type` and `phoneconfiguration-button-feature` in phone templates and phone configurations.  Returns `404` when no profile exists for this brand and model. Any scope that can read phone configurations can read device profiles. — [GET /deviceprofiles/{brand}/{model}]

brand.description: The device brand (`device-models-brand`), such as `Grandstream`.

model.description: The device model (`device-models-model`), such as `WP826`. Encode a space as `%20`.

04f84d3f2725e7ea.title: Get Deviceprofiles Make Model

f9b47a656c22df95.description: Count phone configurations — Returns the number of phones in the domain that have their own phone configuration. Templates are not counted: `GET /domains/{domain}/phonetemplates/count` counts those. Returns `404` when the domain does not exist.  Requires Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope. Other scopes get `403`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/phoneconfiguration/count]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

phoneconfiguration-brand.description: Counts only this brand. Exact match.

phoneconfiguration-model.description: Counts only this model. Exact match.

f9b47a656c22df95.title: Get Domains Domain Phoneconfiguration Count

67c381b3600b829f.description: Read phone configuration — Returns the button layout of one phone, by MAC address, with its buttons, directory settings, sidecars, and extra settings. Buttons are in `phoneconfiguration-button-order` order. A `queue_status` button returns an empty target, and a `timeframe_status` button returns the time frame name.  Returns `404` when the domain has no configuration for this MAC address.  Requires Office Manager scope or above for your own domain, Reseller scope for the domains in your territory, or Super User scope. Office Manager Read-Only can read. Below Reseller scope, the domain of your token is read, whatever domain the path names. — [GET /domains/{domain}/phoneconfiguration/{mac}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

mac.description: The phone's MAC address: 12 hexadecimal digits with no separators.

67c381b3600b829f.title: Get Domains Domain Phoneconfiguration Mac

a527068c6631f325.description: Update phone configuration — Changes the button layout of one phone. The path names the phone by MAC address. Fields you leave out keep their values, except the buttons.  `phoneconfiguration-buttons` replaces the whole button list. Send every button on each update: an update without `phoneconfiguration-buttons` deletes every button. Every button you send is saved, and the buttons belong to this configuration in this domain only. The button types and features a model supports come from `GET /deviceprofiles/{brand}/{model}`, in `devicemodel`.  Two button features also write a dial rule. It goes in the dial plan of the user on the first `line` button, or in the domain\'s dial plan when there is no `line` button. A `queue_status` button toggles the user\'s call queue availability: its target is ignored, and reads return it empty. A `timeframe_status` button toggles a time frame: its target is the time frame name, and `Default` means the default time frame. Add `targetUser` to the button\'s `phoneconfiguration-extra` to toggle another user\'s time frame. The dial rules appear with the dial plan\'s other dial rules.  `phoneconfiguration-domain` in the body is ignored: the domain comes from the path. Returns `404` when the domain has no configuration for this MAC address. A `202` means the change is accepted and already applied.  Requires Office Manager scope or above for your own domain, Reseller scope for the domains in your territory, or Super User scope. — [PUT /domains/{domain}/phoneconfiguration/{mac}]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

mac.description: The phone's MAC address: 12 hexadecimal digits with no separators.

phoneconfiguration-brand.description: The phone brand, as `device-models-brand` spells it in the device profiles. Up to 127 characters.

phoneconfiguration-buttons.description: The buttons, in any order. Every button you send is saved, and the buttons belong to this configuration in this domain only. On an update, the list replaces every button: an update without it deletes every button.

phoneconfiguration-description.description: A description of the layout. Up to 255 characters.

phoneconfiguration-directory.description: How the phone's directory is built: which contacts it lists, their order, and who is left out. Stored as sent.

phoneconfiguration-extra.description: Extra settings for the layout, as a JSON object. Stored as sent. `{}` when there are none.

phoneconfiguration-model.description: The phone model, as `device-models-model` spells it in the device profiles. Up to 127 characters.

0440df1aa3d7bdb4.description: Create device profile — Creates a device profile for a brand and model. Overrides of names that have no system speech word are listed too. Results are sorted by name and paged with `start` and `limit`. Each speech word carries `media-path`, a signed link that plays its audio with no access token. The link expires after one day by default. Get only names with `GET /domains/{domain}/speech-words/list`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/speech-words]

A speech word with no row in the requested `language` returns its `en_us` row. The recording state (`recorded`, `file-size`, `recorded-datetime`) describes the returned row\'s own file, so an override with no recorded audio yet shows `recorded` `false` while the system audio still plays. Each speech word carries `media-path`, a signed link that plays its audio with no access token. The link expires after one day by default. — [GET /domains/{domain}/speech-words/{filename}]

Changing the text or voice does not record new audio: call the matching `/render` endpoint afterward, or upload audio. Until the override is recorded, the domain keeps playing the system audio. 2a144fd04ce7a582.description: Render domain speech words in bulk — Records many speech words with text to speech in one call, and reports the outcome of each.  Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope for the domain. A Reseller can change only domains in its own reseller; any other domain returns `403`.  Each recording is stored as the domain\'s override; system speech words are not changed. Each speech word uses its own stored text and voice. A voice or silence field you send applies to every word in the list. Words whose recording is already current are skipped. The text-to-speech calls run in parallel, and the response is sent once every word has finished, so a long list can take a while; send a few dozen names at a time.  A word that fails does not fail the call: the response is `200` with `status` `error` and a `reason` for that word. — [POST /domains/{domain}/speech-words/render]
