97117004ccc0196c.title: Play Speech Word Domain

c2d4ba79b0493392.description: Render domain speech word with text to speech — Records a speech word with text to speech, from its stored text and voice or the values you send, and stores the text and voice used.  Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope for the domain. A Reseller can change only domains in its own reseller; any other domain returns `403`.  The audio is stored as the domain\'s override; the system speech word is not changed. Rendering calls the text-to-speech service and waits for it, so the response can take several seconds. A speech word whose stored text, voice, and silence already match its recorded file is not rendered again. The voice is matched by id or name among the voices for `voice-language`; when none matches, the first voice for the language is used. Render many speech words in one call with the bulk `/render` endpoint. — [POST /domains/{domain}/speech-words/{filename}/render]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

filename.description: Name of the speech word, without the `.wav` extension, such as `hour-10`.

language.description: Language of the speech word, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`. Default: "en_us"

post-silence-ms.description: Silence after the words, in milliseconds. Defaults to the stored value, then `200`.

pre-silence-ms.description: Silence before the words, in milliseconds. Defaults to the stored value, then `500`.

script.description: Words to speak instead of the stored text. Stored as the new text. No practical length limit.

voice-engine.description: Voice type to store with the audio. Taken from the voice when empty.

voice-id.description: Id or name of the voice to use, such as `en-US-Wavenet-C`. When the language has no such voice, its first voice is used.

voice-language.description: Language of the voice, as a BCP 47 tag such as `en-US`. Defaults to the stored value, then `en-US`.

c2d4ba79b0493392.title: Render Speech Word Domain

017456f3ca7a6fab.description: Upload domain speech word audio — Replaces the recorded audio of a speech word with a file you send.  Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope for the domain. A Reseller can change only domains in its own reseller; any other domain returns `403`.  The audio is stored as the domain\'s override. The audio is converted to 8 kHz, 8-bit mono WAV, and the speech word is marked `source-type` `upload`. Its text is kept unless you send `script`.  **Upload a file.** Send `multipart/form-data` with the audio in the `file` part. The part\'s `Content-Type` picks the decoder: `audio/mpeg` or `audio/mp3` for MP3, `audio/ogg` or `audio/webm` for Ogg or WebM, and WAV otherwise.  **Base64 file.** Send JSON with the audio as base64 in `file-base64`, and its format in `file-encoding`. Without `file-encoding`, MP3 is recognized by its header and anything else is read as WAV.  Audio that cannot be converted returns `400` and nothing is stored. — [POST /domains/{domain}/speech-words/{filename}/upload]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

file-base64.description: The audio file, base64-encoded. WAV, MP3, Ogg, or WebM.

file-encoding.description: Format of the audio in `file-base64`. Without it, MP3 is recognized by its header and anything else is read as WAV. Allowed values: "audio/wav", "audio/mpeg", "audio/ogg", "audio/webm"

filename.description: Name of the speech word, without the `.wav` extension, such as `hour-10`.

language.description: Language of the speech word, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`. Default: "en_us"

script.description: New text for the speech word, describing what the audio says. The stored text is kept when you leave it out.

017456f3ca7a6fab.title: Upload Speech Word Domain

f1a5394b6f633e78.description: List system speech word names — Lists the system speech words in one language, by name only.  Requires Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope.  `/list` returns only each speech word\'s `filename`, `domain`, and `language`, and needs the list right instead of read. It takes the same filters and paging. Append `/list` to a keyed path for one speech word in the same shape. For text, voice, and recording state, use `GET /speech-words`. — [GET /speech-words/list]

filename-like.description: Only speech words whose name contains this text, such as `hour`.

language.description: Language to list, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`. Only speech words stored in this language are listed. Default: "en_us"

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page. Default: 100

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

f1a5394b6f633e78.title: List Speech Word Names

c2215e7a88d1ed85.description: List system speech words — Lists the system speech words in one language, with their text, voice, and recording state. Speech words are the short recorded prompts the platform plays, such as numbers and menu phrases. The system set applies to every domain unless a domain overrides a word.  Requires Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope.  Results are sorted by name and paged with `start` and `limit`. Each speech word carries `media-path`, a signed link that plays its audio with no access token. The link expires after one day by default. Get only names with `GET /speech-words/list`, and a domain\'s view with `GET /domains/{domain}/speech-words`. — [GET /speech-words]

filename-like.description: Only speech words whose name contains this text, such as `hour`.

language.description: Language to list, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`. Only speech words stored in this language are listed. Default: "en_us"

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page. Default: 100

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

c2215e7a88d1ed85.title: List Speech Words

ba5e098c3789375f.description: Read system speech word — Gets one system speech word, with its text, voice, recording state, and a signed playback link.  Requires Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope.  A speech word with no row in the requested `language` returns its `en_us` row. Each speech word carries `media-path`, a signed link that plays its audio with no access token. The link expires after one day by default. — [GET /speech-words/{filename}]

filename.description: Name of the speech word, without the `.wav` extension, such as `hour-10`.

language.description: Language of the speech word, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`. A speech word with no row in this language falls back to its `en_us` row. Default: "en_us"

ba5e098c3789375f.title: Read Speech Word

488e8bf618b1377e.description: Create or update system speech word — Sets the text, voice, and silence padding of a system speech word, creating it when it does not exist. The change applies to every domain that does not override the word.  Requires Super User scope. A Reseller changes speech words only as overrides for domains in its own reseller.  Fields you leave out keep their stored value. A new speech word takes them from the system speech word of the same name, so `script` is required only when there is none. Changing the text or voice does not record new audio: call the matching `/render` endpoint afterward, or upload audio. The response is the stored record; read the speech word for its recording state and playback link. — [PUT /speech-words/{filename}]

filename.description: Name of the speech word, without the `.wav` extension, such as `hour-10`.

language.description: Language of the speech word, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`. Default: "en_us"

post-silence-ms.description: Silence after the words, in milliseconds, added when the speech word is rendered. Defaults to `200`.

pre-silence-ms.description: Silence before the words, in milliseconds, added when the speech word is rendered. Defaults to `500`.

script.description: Words the audio should say. Required only when the speech word is new and has no system speech word to take them from. No practical length limit.

voice-engine.description: Voice type, as the text-to-speech service names it. Rendering fills it in when empty.

voice-id.description: Id or name of the text-to-speech voice, such as `en-US-Wavenet-C`. List voices with `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/voices/{language}`.

voice-language.description: Language of the voice, as a BCP 47 tag such as `en-US`.

488e8bf618b1377e.title: Update Speech Word

0517822606b34ce3.description: Render system speech words in bulk — Records many speech words with text to speech in one call, and reports the outcome of each.  Requires Super User scope. A Reseller changes speech words only as overrides for domains in its own reseller.  Each recording replaces the system audio. Each speech word uses its own stored text and voice. A voice or silence field you send applies to every word in the list. Words whose recording is already current are skipped. The text-to-speech calls run in parallel, and the response is sent once every word has finished, so a long list can take a while; send a few dozen names at a time.  A word that fails does not fail the call: the response is `200` with `status` `error` and a `reason` for that word. — [POST /speech-words/render]

filenames.description: Names of the speech words to render, without `.wav`. Duplicates and blank names are ignored. An invalid name is reported as an error for that entry.

language.description: Language of the speech words, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`. Default: "en_us"

post-silence-ms.description: Silence after the words, in milliseconds, for every word.

pre-silence-ms.description: Silence before the words, in milliseconds, for every word.

voice-engine.description: Voice type to store with every word. Taken from the voice when empty.

voice-id.description: Id or name of the voice to use for every word, such as `en-US-Wavenet-C`.

voice-language.description: Language of the voice for every word, as a BCP 47 tag such as `en-US`.

0517822606b34ce3.title: Render Speech Words Bulk

00802a7655d4a608.description: Download system speech word audio — Downloads the recorded audio of a speech word as `audio/wav`, 8 kHz mono.  Requires Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope.  A request with a `Range` header gets `206` with that byte range, so an audio player can seek. The file is sent as an attachment named `<filename>.wav` unless you send `nofilename=yes`. For a link that plays without an access token, read the speech word and use its `media-path`. — [GET /speech-words/{filename}/file]

download.description: `yes` sends the whole file in one response and turns off range requests. Allowed values: "yes"

filename.description: Name of the speech word, without the `.wav` extension, such as `hour-10`.

language.description: Language of the audio, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`. When there is no file in this language, the `en_us` file plays. Default: "en_us"

nofilename.description: `yes` leaves out the `Content-Disposition` header, so a browser plays the audio instead of saving it. Allowed values: "yes"

00802a7655d4a608.title: Read Speech Word File

65ae0561a2db80db.description: Play system speech word from signed link — Plays the recorded audio of a speech word from a signed link, with no access token. Use it as the `src` of an audio player.  No scope is needed: the `time` and `auth` values are the credential. Read the speech word, or list speech words, and use its `media-path` as it is; do not build the link yourself. A link plays only the speech word, domain, and `language` it was made for, and expires after one day by default.  The audio is `audio/wav`, 8 kHz mono. A request with a `Range` header gets `206` with that byte range. An expired link returns `403`: read the speech word again for a new one. — [GET /speech-words/{filename}/play]

auth.description: Signature of the link. Copy it from `media-path` unchanged.

download.description: `yes` sends the whole file in one response and turns off range requests. Allowed values: "yes"

filename.description: Name of the speech word, without the `.wav` extension, such as `hour-10`.

language.description: Language of the audio, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`. When there is no file in this language, the `en_us` file plays. Default: "en_us"

nofilename.description: `yes` leaves out the `Content-Disposition` header, so a browser plays the audio instead of saving it. Allowed values: "yes"

time.description: Time the link was made, in UTC as `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS`. Copy it from `media-path` unchanged.

65ae0561a2db80db.title: Play Speech Word

filename.description: Name of the speech word, without the `.wav` extension, such as `hour-10`.

0f7bdd02d4e87587.description: Create translations — Creates one translation, or several when the body has a `translations` array. Requires Super User scope.  A key created in any namespace other than `common` is also created in `common`, with the same locale, value, and description, unless `common` already has that key. The response reports this in `common_entry_created`. An `id` is generated when you omit it.  A new translation is marked as customized (`source` is `api`), so a filesystem sync never overwrites it. Send `source=filesystem` to let the next sync replace it.  The change is accepted and applied shortly after this response, so a read made immediately after can still show the old value.  A single create of a `locale`, `namespace`, and `key` that already exists returns `409`; change it with `PUT /translations`. Send a `translations` array to act on several translations in one request. A bulk request always returns `200`: each item that failed is listed in `errors` with its position in the array and the reason, and `summary` counts the results. — [POST /translations]
0f7bdd02d4e87587.title: Create Translation

a15d4f09370645a0.description: Update translations — Changes the value, the description, or both, of one translation, or of several when the body has a `translations` array. Requires Super User scope.  Identify each translation by `id`, or by `locale`, `namespace`, and `key`. When `id` is sent it wins. The locale, namespace, and key themselves cannot be changed: delete the translation and create it again.  You can send `description` alone. Every change marks the translation as customized, even a description-only one, so a filesystem sync no longer overwrites its value.  The change is accepted and applied shortly after this response, so a read made immediately after can still show the old value. Send a `translations` array to act on several translations in one request. A bulk request always returns `200`: each item that failed is listed in `errors` with its position in the array and the reason, and `summary` counts the results. — [PUT /translations]
a15d4f09370645a0.title: Update Translation

8288e2467e085550.description: Delete translations — Deletes one translation, or several when the body has a `translations` array. Requires Super User scope.  Identify a translation by `id`, or by `locale`, `namespace`, and `key`, in the body or as query parameters. A query parameter overrides the same field in the body. When you use query parameters, the body can be empty.  The copy in `common` that a create may have added is not deleted. Delete it separately if you no longer want it.  The change is accepted and applied shortly after this response, so a read made immediately after can still show the old value. Send a `translations` array to act on several translations in one request. A bulk request always returns `200`: each item that failed is listed in `errors` with its position in the array and the reason, and `summary` counts the results. — [DELETE /translations]

id.description: The ID of the translation to delete. Overrides `id` in the body.

key.description: The key of the translation to delete, with `locale` and `namespace`. Overrides the body.

locale.description: The locale of the translation to delete, with `namespace` and `key`. Overrides the body.

namespace.description: The namespace of the translation to delete, with `locale` and `key`. Overrides the body.

8288e2467e085550.title: Delete Translation

9ab24ceea6ec0f50.description: Get translations for a locale — Returns every translation for a locale, grouped by namespace, as `{namespace: {key: value}}`. No token is required. A token that you send and that is not valid returns `401`.  Every key comes from the `en-US` translations. Where the requested locale has its own value for a key, that value is returned; otherwise the `en-US` value is. A key or a namespace that exists only in the requested locale, and not in `en-US`, is not returned. There is no other fallback: `fr-CA` does not fall back to `fr`, and the result does not depend on any domain setting. A locale with no translations at all returns the `en-US` values.  The response may be cached for up to 1 hour (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`), so a browser that already loaded it can show an older value after an edit.  To fetch one namespace, use `/translations/{locale}/{namespace}`. — [GET /translations/{locale}]

locale.description: The locale code: 2 letters, optionally followed by a hyphen and 2 letters, such as `en-US`, `fr-CA`, or `fr`. Matched without regard to case. Any other form, such as `zh-Hans`, returns `404`.

9ab24ceea6ec0f50.title: Get All Translations For Locale

b8a17bb8682df8af.description: Get translation descriptions for a locale — Returns the translator descriptions for a locale, grouped by namespace and key. A description explains where a string appears, to help translators. Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope.  Only keys with a non-empty description are returned, and there is no fallback to `en-US`. A locale that has translations but no descriptions returns an empty result, as `[]`. A locale with no translations returns `404`.  The response may be cached for up to 30 seconds. To set a description, use `PUT /translations`. — [GET /translations/descriptions/{locale}]

locale.description: The locale code, such as `en-US`. Use a value from `GET /translations/locales`. A code that is not 2 letters, optionally followed by a hyphen and 2 letters, returns `404`.

b8a17bb8682df8af.title: Get Translation Descriptions

4024c31c6bf15bec.description: List available locales — Lists every locale that has at least one translation, sorted alphabetically. No token is required. A token that you send and that is not valid returns `401`.  Use a value from this list as `{locale}` in `/translations/{locale}`. Takes no parameters. The response may be cached for up to 30 seconds, so a new locale can take that long to appear. — [GET /translations/locales]
4024c31c6bf15bec.title: Get Locales

c8e7b3d097ef1edf.description: List translation namespaces — Lists every translation namespace in use across all locales, sorted alphabetically. No token is required. A token that you send and that is not valid returns `401`.  Use a value from this list as `{namespace}` in `/translations/{locale}/{namespace}`. Takes no parameters. The response may be cached for up to 30 seconds. — [GET /translations/namespaces]
c8e7b3d097ef1edf.title: Get Namespaces

6ac4f2fa6c861d77.description: List translation records — Returns every translation record with its metadata, most recently updated first, for managing translations. Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope.  Takes no parameters. Filtering, paging, and sorting are not supported: any query parameter, such as `locale` or `limit`, is ignored and the whole table is returned. Filter the result yourself.  Each record\'s `availability` lists the locales that have the same `namespace` and `key`, next to every locale in use, so you can find keys that are missing a translation. The response is never cached, so it shows a change as soon as the change is applied.  To read translations as an app uses them, with the `en-US` fallback applied, use `/translations/{locale}`. — [GET /translations/raw]
6ac4f2fa6c861d77.title: Get Raw Translations

085ec165c76b8c56.description: Sync translations from locale files — Loads translations from the locale files installed on the server that answers the request. Requires Super User scope.  Send `project` to load one set of files: `horizon` for the web app, or `auth` for the login pages. Omit it, or send `all`, to load both. For each key in a file:  - **Not in the database:** created, along with its copy in `common` when `common` lacks the key. - **Customized through this API:** left alone. - **Already present, `auth` files:** left alone, so the web app\'s text wins on shared keys. - **Value changed in the file:** updated.  Keys that are no longer in the files are not deleted. For `horizon`, translator descriptions are also loaded, for keys that already exist. Only files named like `en.json` or `en-US.json` are read.  The response lists every change per project and locale, with totals. A project with no locale files on this server is reported with `success: false` inside `projects`, with `200`. The change is accepted and applied shortly after this response, so a read made immediately after can still show the old value.  An unknown `project` returns `400` with the list of valid names. — [POST /translations/sync-filesystem]

project.description: The set of locale files to load. `horizon` is the web app's files, including its translator descriptions. `auth` is the login pages' files. `all`, the default, loads both. The names are case-sensitive, except `all`. Allowed values: "horizon", "auth", "all". Default: "all"

085ec165c76b8c56.title: Sync Filesystem

52ce6364b422e35c.description: Get translations for a namespace — Returns the translations for one namespace in a locale, as a flat `{key: value}` object. No token is required. A token that you send and that is not valid returns `401`.  Every key comes from the `en-US` translations. Where the requested locale has its own value for a key, that value is returned; otherwise the `en-US` value is. A key or a namespace that exists only in the requested locale, and not in `en-US`, is not returned. There is no other fallback: `fr-CA` does not fall back to `fr`, and the result does not depend on any domain setting. A locale with no translations at all returns the `en-US` values. An unknown namespace, or one that has no `en-US` translations, returns an empty result.  The response may be cached for up to 1 hour (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`), so a browser that already loaded it can show an older value after an edit.  To fetch every namespace at once, use `/translations/{locale}`. — [GET /translations/{locale}/{namespace}]

locale.description: The locale code: 2 letters, optionally followed by a hyphen and 2 letters, such as `en-US`, `fr-CA`, or `fr`. Matched without regard to case. Any other form, such as `zh-Hans`, returns `404`.

namespace.description: The namespace, such as `common`. Letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-` only.

52ce6364b422e35c.title: Get Translations Namespace

ef6754280de797d9.description: List user setting names — Lists the names of the settings stored for the user in the path, without their values. Use it to see which settings exist before you read one.  Office Manager can list the settings of every user in its domain, and Site Manager its own settings and those of users in its site. Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, and Office Manager Read-Only can list their own settings only. Reseller can list the settings of users in its domains, and Super User or Super User Read Only the settings of any user. The user in the path decides access: a `uid` in the query has no effect.  A user with no settings returns an empty array. Append `/list` to the keyed path, `/domains/{domain}/users/{user}/settings/{setting}/list`, to check one setting: it returns one entry in the same shape, or `404` when the user does not have it. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/settings/list]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

user.description: User whose settings you work with, such as `1001`. `~` means you, and also sets the domain to your own.

ef6754280de797d9.title: List User Setting Names

5065f3ddc4568ac6.description: List user settings — Returns every setting stored for the user in the path, with its value. A setting is a named per-user preference that an app saves and reads back, such as a dashboard layout or a display option.  Office Manager can read the settings of every user in its domain, and Site Manager its own settings and those of users in its site. Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, and Office Manager Read-Only can read their own settings only. Reseller can read the settings of users in its domains, and Super User or Super User Read Only the settings of any user. The user in the path decides access: a `uid` in the query has no effect.  All settings are returned in one response, with no paging. A user with no settings returns an empty array. A user\'s settings are removed when the user is deleted. To list only the setting names, use **List user setting names**. To read one setting, use **Read user setting**. — [GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/settings]

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

user.description: User whose settings you work with, such as `1001`. `~` means you, and also sets the domain to your own.

5065f3ddc4568ac6.title: List User Settings

bab1362709b86ec1.description: Create or update user setting — Saves one setting for the user in the path, naming it in the body. If the user already has a setting with that name, its value is replaced.  Office Manager can change the settings of every user in its domain, and Site Manager its own settings and those of users in its site. Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, and Office Manager Read-Only can change their own settings only. eaa2fd2b5d8088d0.description: List users (older path) — Returns the users in a domain. This is an older path for `GET /domains/{domain}/users`. It takes the same query parameters and returns the same response, and it accepts only `GET`. Use `GET /domains/{domain}/users` in new integrations. — [GET /domains/{domain}/userinfo]

department.description: Returns only the users in this department. Exact match on one department name.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

email.description: Returns the users that have this email address, ignoring case. A user with several addresses matches on any of them.

fields.description: A comma-separated list of the fields to return, by their names in the response. Names the API does not know are ignored.

filter_users.description: Chooses which rows to leave out. By default the response leaves out the rows that represent a site or a department and the domain's `domain` placeholder user, and includes system users such as call queues and auto attendants. Send a comma-separated list to replace that default. Each item is one of the following: - `departments`, which leaves out department rows - `sites`, which leaves out site rows - `system`, which leaves out every user whose service code starts with `system-` - a service code such as `system-queue`, which leaves out that code - an extension, which leaves out that user `no` returns every row.

include-secret.description: `yes` returns `voicemail-login-pin` in full. By default the PIN is masked: a PIN of 8 characters or fewer is all asterisks, and a longer one shows only its first 2 and last 2 characters. Any token that can read the user can ask for it. Allowed values: "yes", "no". Default: "no"

limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page. Default: 100

login.description: Returns the one user with this login name.

name-first-name.description: Returns only the users with this first name. Exact match.

name-last-name.description: Returns the users whose last name contains this text.

service-code.description: Returns only the users with this service code, such as `system-queue`. Exact match.

site.description: Returns only the users in this site. Exact match.

sort.description: The sort order: `user` (extension, sorted numerically), `site`, or `group` (department), followed by a space and `asc` or `desc`. Defaults to `user asc`. Default: "user asc"

start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page. Default: 0

user-scope.description: Returns only the users with this scope. Send a comma-separated list to match any of several scopes.

d06bb7cfae878222.description: Read vCon for CDR — Returns one vCon document for a call in a domain, addressed under its CDR. It is the same read as `GET /domains/{domain}/vcon/{cdr_id}`. Requires Office Manager, Site Manager, Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope: the same rights as reading the domain\'s CDRs. A Site Manager reads a call only when a user of its own site is a party on a leg in the path domain; any other call returns `404`, as a CDR that does not exist does.  The document follows the IETF vCon core format. It joins every CDR leg of the call, including transfers and queue hops linked by call ID, with the recordings, transcript segments, sentiment, AI summary, and the internal parties\' user profiles. Times are RFC 3339 in UTC with a `Z` suffix. Below Super User and Super User Read Only, a party from another domain carries only what your own CDR names: its SIP URI, extension, and user ID, with no user profile.  CDRs are stored by month. Send `yyyymm` when you know the month of the call. Without it, the API searches back from the current month, 12 months by default, and uses the first month that holds the CDR.  Each recording entry in `dialog` carries a signed `url` you can play without a token, through `GET /recordings/play`. — [GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{cdr_id}/vcon]

cdr_id.description: The CDR ID of the call: the `id` of its first leg, as returned by the CDR endpoints. Letters, digits, `-`, and `_`.

domain.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

yyyymm.description: The month the call is stored under, as 6 digits `YYYYMM`, such as `202609`. Saves searching back month by month. A month from 2000 to next year is accepted; anything else returns `400`.

4ea01214d0f3d1d9.description: Check API health — Checks the dependencies of the server that answered: the cache, every configured database connection, and the message bus. Load balancers and monitoring services can call it without a token.  Without a token, the response carries only `status`, `timestamp`, `hostname`, and `app_version`. With a valid token it also carries `environment`, `php_version`, and `checks`, the result of each dependency. No token is needed. You can still send one (a bearer access token, an API key, or the `ns_access_token` cookie) to get the longer response. Any valid token works, whatever its scope. A token that is sent but is invalid or expired is refused with `401`, and an API key that is not valid with `403`; you do not get the shorter response instead.  The HTTP status is always `200`. Read `status`: `healthy` means every check passed, and `degraded` means at least one failed. Results are cached for 15 seconds per server, so a failure can take up to 15 seconds to show, and repeated calls in that window do not repeat the checks. The `X-Health-Cache` response header is `hit` when the result came from that cache and `miss` when it was just computed. Takes no parameters. — [GET /health]
